Торговий агент постачальника усно прийняв замовлення за адресою узгоджена ціна 250 доларів за десяток. Відповідно до звичайної ділової практики постачальника торговий агент надіслав поштою такий лист-підтвердження, який він підписав і поставив дату: «Згідно з вашим телефонним замовленням, цей лист служить для підтвердження покупки 36 десятків кашемірових шкарпеток, колір фіолетовий, розмір 10. 13, за погодженою ціною 250 доларів США за дюжину: 9000 доларів США. Цей лист був отриманий чоловіком, який мимохіть поглянув на нього, але не помітив ні напису «36 дюжин». Чоловік помістив лист у свої справи та не відповів на нього. A. Так, оскільки статут не був задоволений тендером постачальника товарів, які були відхилені чоловіком, і постачальник не покладався на усну домовленість, окрім спроби доставки.
B. Так, тому що домовлена ціна за три десятки шкарпеток була понад 500 доларів, а в службовій записці постачальника була неправильно вказана кількість замовленого товару.
C. Ні, тому що письмова записка постачальника була достатньою, щоб задовольнити вимоги статуту проти постачальника, а чоловік, маючи підстави знати про зміст записки, не подав повідомлення про заперечення протягом 10 днів після отримання.
D. Ні, тому що письмова записка постачальника діяла як акцепт, з пропозиціями щодо додаткових умов, які стали частиною контракту після того, як чоловік не заперечив проти таких додаткових умов протягом розумного часу.

B. Doug, because the retriever is a domesticated animal.

Question: Max went to a mini-market, took out a pistol, and demanded that the cashier empty the cash register. Question: State educational agency, complying with all legislative requirements, acquired a land plot through eminent domain. The original landowner accepted the just market value and did not appeal it. For the next 15 years, the agency held the property but did not use it for educational purposes. In the 16th year, the agency abandoned its planned educational use and sold it on a publicly announced auction according to state law. The original owner appealed, claiming that the agency only took a fee that could be defined and when it ceased to use the property for educational purposes, the higher-level fee ownership was returned to the original owner. Is it likely that the appellate court will decide that the landowner can claim the right to stop the attempt to transfer?
A. No, because the state also acquired a paid simple ownership through adverse possession after 11 consecutive years of continuous possession.
B. No, because the original transfer was conducted legally, and the landowner received just market value, thus allowing the presumption of a fee simple ownership in the agency.
C. Yes, an eminent domain is limited to the use of property which is temporarily necessary for public use, and not using it for this purpose results in the agency losing ownership rights.
D. Yes, because every acquisition of eminent domain involves a fee that can simply be defined by the state acquisition.

Question: The Federal law provides funds to states for child protection programs on the condition that such programs are carried out in accordance with federal standards. The United States filed a lawsuit against the state regarding judicial immunity, claiming that child protection programs in the state, which were partially funded by federal funds allocated under this statute, did not meet federal standards. The state rejected the lawsuit. Is it likely that the court will dismiss the lawsuit?
A. No, because Congress can impose any conditions regarding the receipt of federal funds.
B. No, because the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit lawsuits filed by the United States.
C. Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits lawsuits against states in federal court.

Question: The landlord owns a two-story building. He rented the building and the surrounding property to the tenant from December 1, 2006, to November 30, 2008. Their rental agreement contained the following terms: "The tenant is obligated to pay rent at a rate of $500 per month on the first day of each month and maintain the building located in the rented premises in as good condition as it was at the time of renting until the end of the contract term 'On April 15, 2007, the tenant hosted an annual tax night where she and her friends all went to the post office to mail their taxes, then had drinks and dinner at the tenant's apartment to celebrate. After a few drinks, one of the tenant's friends became belligerent towards one of the guests at the party who disputed some deductions of his friend. The other attacked another participant of the party and slashed the wall after he stumbled. As a result, one of the walls of the apartment was damaged.' This state is a jurisdiction of common law. Moreover, the statute of limitations for a lawsuit seeking compensation for injuries due to negligence is five years from the date of the injury. In the appropriate lawsuit to interpret the tenant's obligation under the agreement to maintain the premises in repair, which of the following is the most accurate?
A. The tenant is responsible for normal wear and tear according to the repair agreement.
B. The tenant is responsible for any defects under such an agreement, including damaging the wall.
C. The agreement regarding repairs for the tenant is invalid contrary to state policy, since the landlord is obligated to perform repairs on a building that has disappeared.
D. The tenant's obligation to maintain the premises in good condition releases the landlord from the obligation to notify of any hidden defects.

Question: The woman owned four beach cottages. Each cottage had windows in the shape of stars. Since the hurricane season was approaching, she hired a carpenter to build and deliver storm windows to all four cottages within 30 days. In return, she promised to pay $8,000 ( $2,000 per cottage) one week after the work was completed. Two weeks after signing the contract, a fire destroyed the carpenter's workshop where he stored all the completed storm windows for delivery. Then the carpenter sent the woman a letter stating: "The fire destroyed my equipment and inventory, including the storm windows that were finished and waiting for delivery. I am ruined and cannot fulfill my contractual obligations." Later, the woman called the carpenter and told him: "If you do not fulfill your contractual obligations, I will sue you!" In a lawsuit for specific performance to force the carpenter to build and deliver storm windows, the woman, most likely, will be
A. successful, because the loss of the carpenter's equipment does not justify his obligation to perform.
B. successful, because the beach cottages would suffer serious damage during a hurricane without installed storm windows.
C. unsuccessful, because performing the carpenter's task would be justified by God's unforeseen action.
D. unsuccessful, because the loss of the carpenter's equipment will make his work impossible.

Question: Two second cousins inherited co-ownership of real estate as co-tenants with the right of survivorship. One of the second cousins pledged his share in the co-tenancy as collateral for a loan in the amount of 20,000 dollars and signed a court judgment. This was later used as a decision against the second cousin's share in the property. The second cousin died a year later. The other second cousin decided to sell the property, but the mortgagee filed a lawsuit to prevent the sale and intervene with the proceeds. The other second cousin defended on the grounds that any pledge right over the second cousin's share in ownership was extinguished after the second cousin's death. Will the court refer to the mortgagee's lawsuit against the sale of the property by the second cousin who survived?
A. Yes, because the consent of the second cousin to the pledge right under a court decision is presumed by law, and this consent invalidated the co-tenancy.
B. Yes, because a mortgage or a judicial pledge against one co-tenant invalidates the tenancy and extinguishes the right of survivorship.
C. No, because a co-tenant cannot lawfully file a court decision solely regarding the interests of this co-tenant, as it would be an unconstitutional interference with the rights of ownership of the other.
D. No, because when the second cousin died, the second cousin became a sole owner due to the right of survivorship, according to the co-tenancy which remained entirely undisturbed.

Question: Being a guest at his son's place, the grandfather tripped over a toy left on the floor by his four-year-old grandson and fell, sustaining serious injuries. The grandfather regularly visited his son's home and knew that the grandson often left toys scattered around the house. The son never warned the grandfather to be careful about the toys. The grandfather sued his son for compensation of the physical injuries. In the court hearing, after the evidence was presented, both the grandfather and the son appealed for a decision regarding liability. The jurisdiction waived the family immunity and applied traditional rules of landowner liability. What actions should the court take?
A. Dismiss both appeals and refer the case to a jury for the fact of negligence.
B. Dismiss both appeals and refer the case to a jury based on strict liability.
C. Grant the grandfather's appeal as the son bears legal responsibility for not warning about the toys being left on the floor.
D. Grant the son's appeal because the son did not have a duty to warn that the grandson might leave toys on the floor.

Question: The ranch owner - the ranch is located at the top of a mountain. Under the ranch, there is a mansion owned by a millionaire. A stream is an unnavigable watercourse that originates at the top of the mountain and flows down into the valley. Both the ranch and the mansion are within the watershed of the stream. When the millionaire bought the estate in 1956, he began to take water from the stream and use it for irrigating the southern half of his property, which he used as a farm. Before 1956, the southern half of the estate was cleared and cultivated, while the northern half remained forested and largely unused. The millionaire continued this established model of water use and never ceased using water in this manner. In 1986, the ranch owner built a house on the ranch and started cleaning the stream water for domestic needs. That year there were heavy rains, causing the stream to flow with high water levels. However, in 1987, a drought caused very low water levels. Thus, there was enough water only for irrigation of the millionaire's agricultural lands or, alternatively, to meet all domestic water needs of the ranch owner and one quarter of the millionaire's irrigation needs. The mountain is located in a jurisdiction where the statute of limitations is 15 years. The ranch owner continues to take water for personal use but not enough for the irrigation of the estate. Then, in 1996, the millionaire filed a lawsuit claiming that his rights to water in the stream prevail over the ranch owner's rights. Furthermore, the millionaire moved to divert the entire stream flow to himself, regardless of the impact this may have on the ranch owner. If this country follows the general principle of prior appropriation but does not adhere to the doctrine of prior appropriation, who should be the judge?
A. The ranch owner, because as the higher landowner, he would have greater rights to water than the lower landowner.
B. The farmer, because domestic use is better protected than agricultural use.
C. The millionaire, because he acquired a servitude by prescription to divert as much water as needed.
D. The millionaire, because he used the water for benefit before the ranch owner and continuously used the water.

Question: In which of the given situations could the state of intoxication of the accused NOT mitigate their criminal liability?

Then the victim safely escaped from the car. The suspect was arrested and charged with attempted aggravated assault.
B. The defendant was at a wedding in a hotel where he had several shots of hard liquor. After consuming them, the defendant started a fierce argument with the hotel parking attendant. The defendant took the tire iron from his car and threw it at the attendant. The tire iron missed the attendant but struck the victim when he was entering the hotel. The victim was injured by the tire iron. The suspect was arrested and charged with assault.
C. The defendant spent the entire evening drinking alcoholic beverages in a bar with three of his friends. A detective undercover heard the defendant and his friends planning to rob the bar after closing. When the defendant tried to draw a pistol from his coat, the police quickly disarmed him and arrested him. The suspect is charged with robbery.
D. At his law school graduation party, the defendant drank two cases of beer. Around midnight, a girl approached him and asked for a ride home. Despite the fact that the girl was only 15 years old, she looked like a woman around twenty. The defendant, who had been watching over the girl all night, readily agreed and showed her the way to his car. Once inside, they engaged in a sexual act. The age of consent in this jurisdiction is 17 for women. Later, the defendant was arrested and charged with rape.

Question: A woman owned a 10-acre agricultural land at absolute value. The woman agreed to sell the agricultural land to a man, and both signed a document stating: "...for $10,000, receipt of which is confirmed." In reality, the man had not yet paid the woman $10,000. On the closing date, the woman transferred the deed of agricultural land to the man, who gave her a check for $10,000. However, a few days after the woman deposited the check, she received a notification from her bank that the check was not honored due to insufficient funds on the account. Then, the woman sued the man in court. At the trial, the woman tries to prove that the man did not actually pay her $10,000 as stated in their written document. The man denies the woman's claims. Would the judge support the man's denial?
A. No, because the rule of evidence does not apply to events that occur after the text is drafted.
B. No, because the rule of evidence for a conditional reference does not exclude evidence demonstrating the absence or lack of attention.
C. Yes, since the written document appears to be a complete integration of the agreement between the parties.
D. Yes, because the doctrine of accord and satisfaction would not allow the woman to rescind her own signed confirmation that she received $10,000.

B. admissible as an admission.

D. admissible as a then-existing state of mind.

Question: The defendant was charged with murder. The murder occurred on February 1st. At the time of the crime, this jurisdiction required a unanimous verdict from all 12 jurors to convict a crime punishable by death. On November 1st, the state legislative body passed a new law requiring only a majority of seven out of twelve jurors for a conviction for a crime punishable by death. The trial began on December 1st. Later, he was found guilty by eight votes to four. After the court session results, the defense attorney filed a motion to vacate the sentence. What among the above would be the most compelling constitutional basis for vacating the sentence?
A. Post facto concerns.
B. Contract clause.
C. Due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
D. Sixth Amendment right to a fair trial.

Question: A man and a woman were competing in an illegal drag race. Both were speeding, but they were very careful. However, when the woman's car suddenly blew a tire, she lost control and crashed into a pedestrian, injuring them. Later, the pedestrian sued the man because the woman did not have insurance or assets. Is it likely that the pedestrian will win this case?
A. No, because the man did not cause physical injuries.
B. No, because the man was driving very carefully.
C. Yes, because the man and woman were acting together in a dangerous activity.
D. Yes, because the man was speeding.

Question: If the wife sues the department store based on the actions of the employee, she will
A. win, since the complaint was heard by another customer.
B. win, since the clerk's behavior was extreme and offensive.
C. lose, because the clerk simply expressed his opinion.
D. lose, because the wife was merely offended.

Question: An unconditional written offer (firm offer) of a merchant to sell goods
A. Must be separately signed if the addressee of the offer provides a form of contract that includes the offer.
B. Has a validity period of three months.

Question: A company producing paper entered into a contract with a construction company for the construction of a new warehouse. The contract stipulated that the construction company would receive payment after the completion of the warehouse construction. The contractor completed the construction of the warehouse but had minor deviations from the plans due to the substitution of certain building materials that were not available on the market. The construction company finished the work and demands payment. The paper company refused to pay citing deviations from the specifications. Is it likely that the construction company will win in a breach of contract lawsuit against the paper company?
A. Yes, the company performing the construction work can always claim payment for the work done.
B. No, the construction company cannot change the specifications and expect to be paid.
C. No, the construction company is guilty of fraud and deceit.
D. Yes, the construction company mainly fulfilled the contract.

Question: The landlord leased a business building to the tenant for five years. The rent was due on the first day of each month, and the landlord retained the right to terminate the lease if the tenant failed to fulfill their obligations. The lease term ended 18 months ago. However, the tenant remained in possession of the building and continued to pay the rent on time. The landlord continued to accept the rent payments. The current fair rental value of the building now significantly exceeds what the tenant pays, and the landlord recently found a third party willing to pay a higher rent. When the tenant paid the rent six weeks ago, the landlord agreed to accept the payment but six weeks ago and told the tenant that they would be evicted at the end of the month. The tenant, who still occupies the building, informed the landlord that she is willing to pay the current fair rental value. The landlord consulted his lawyer about ownership rights. Who should say who has the right to possession?
A. The landlord, because he properly notified of the termination of the lease agreement.
B. The landlord, because he retained the right of re-entry.
C. The tenant, because she stated that she is willing to pay the current fair rental value.
D. The tenant, because the landlord did not provide valid reasons for terminating the lease agreement.
Question: A. прийнятна як частина res gestae. B. допустимо як допуск. C. неприпустимий як чутка, не в межах жодного визнаного винятку. D. неприпустимий як корисливий.

Question: One company offered to sell several batches of stone for landscape design at a specified price and conditions. The recipient of the offer sent a notification to the offeror stating, "We have received your offer to sell stone for landscape design on these terms today." The offeror shipped the goods after receiving this message. On the day of shipment, the recipient published an acceptance form with minor changes in the terms. After the goods arrived, the recipient called the offeror's manager and said that the company could no longer accept the offer, would return the goods, and "ignore any documents sent by us." The offeror sued the recipient for breach of contract. Who will win?
A. The offeror will have an advantage because the publication of the acceptance concludes the agreement between the parties.
B. The recipient of the offer will have an advantage because he never accepted the offer on the specified terms.
C. The offeror will have an advantage because he shipped the goods when he received the first acceptance.
D. The recipient of the offer will have an advantage because he rejected the offer when he called the offeror's manager.

Question: The suspect is being tried for kidnapping. The victim stated that one of the kidnappers called another person "Spid." The prosecutor calls a prison officer to testify that while the defendant was in prison awaiting trial, other inmates referred to him as "Spid." Are the statements of the prison officer admissible?
A. No, because this is hearsay and there is no exception.
B. No, because it is substantially more prejudicial than probative.
C. Yes, as a direct proof that the defendant was one of the kidnappers.
D. Yes, to confirm the truthfulness of the victim's statement.

Question: The patient of a federal clinic reported to the clinic that a nurse committed sexual assault on her. The man was arrested. During the court hearing, the prosecution presented evidence that the man had been convicted of two previous instances of sexual assault against two other women about two years ago. The methods and circumstances of these assaults were almost identical to this case. The defense attorney objected to the evidence on the grounds that its prejudicial effect outweighs its probative value. Based on the Federal Rules of Evidence, what is the most likely decision the court will make regarding this issue?
A. The evidence is too prejudicial and should be excluded.
B. The evidence is inadmissible as it has no bearing on the charges and has low probative value.
C. The evidence is admissible because current state policy strongly favors the arrest and prosecution of sexual predators.
D. The evidence is admissible due to the factual similarity with this charge, which provides substantial probative value.

Question: The judicial process arose in the courts of the state when the minister of trade tried to prevent a person from mailing new promotional brochures. According to the interpretation of the secretary, the new brochures contained indecent photos and expressions of a sexual nature. The minister acted in accordance with the powers granted by Section 1123(b) of the state law, which provided: "If the minister of trade determines that commercial mailing to residents of the state is inappropriate for minors, the minister has the authority to prohibit such mailing." The case went to the state supreme court, which ruled that the statute was unconstitutional as it violated both commerce provisions and the supremacy clause. If this case were to be reviewed by the United States Supreme Court, it would reach that court
A. through appeal.
B. by certiorari.
C. if five judges vote for its review.
D. notwithstanding the doctrine of adequate and independent state grounds.

Question: The suspect was arrested and charged with conspiracy to obtain stolen goods. During the presentation of the accused, a defense attorney appeared. After posting bail, he was released. After his release, the accused resumed work as a bartender at a local bar. Three weeks before the scheduled trial, an informant visited the bar. After a few drinks, the informant began talking to the accused, who was on duty at the time. The accused did not know that the man was a paid police informant. During their conversation, the informant told the accused that he had read about his arrest in the newspapers and asked the accused for the names of his accomplices. Without suspicion, the accused made some statements, which the informant then passed on to the prosecutor. In court, the prosecution tried to introduce the accused's statements as evidence. The defense's objection to admitting this evidence would most likely be
A. dismissed, since the defense's statements were voluntary.
B. upheld, since the defense took the risk that his trust in the informant was misplaced.
C. granted, since there was a violation of the accused's right to counsel under the Sixth Amendment.
D. granted, since there was a violation of the accused's right against self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment.

Question: A recent law school graduate was hired as an attorney review consultant by a regional bar course's editorial board. Her duties included preparing new course notes, correcting and evaluating students' homework, and she was offered a starting monthly salary of $2500. After three months, the regional director of the bar courses gave her a 60-page brochure titled "Employment Guide" and instructed her to read it, stating that it contained important information regarding company policy and employee compensation. That evening, after returning home from work, she started reading the manual but became tired after about 30 pages and went to sleep, never finishing the rest. Six months later, she received a termination notice from the attorney review course, stating that she was fired for not fulfilling her duties because she complained about the low quality of the materials and refused to work overtime. After her dismissal, she filed a lawsuit against the bar association for breach of contract. What, if true and proven, would provide the best defense for the attorney review course?
A. All other employees of the attorney review course worked overtime when required.
B. When the graduate accepted the position at the attorney review course, the company made no promises regarding job security or employment duration.
C. The materials in the attorney review course had recently been reviewed by the Committee on Legal Education of the American Bar Association and received a "high rating."
D. The second page of the attorney review course manual contained a paragraph stating that all policies, instructions, and compensation for employees were "purely gratuitous and not intended to create any binding contractual obligations."

Question: In the big city, trash is always a problem. The state law on fighting trash prohibits throwing any trash or other items from any car onto public roads. This is an administrative offense that carries a fine of $50 US dollars without imprisonment. For a third offense, the fine is $500 and includes 5 days of imprisonment. There is no requirement for criminal intent in the statute. John and his family return from a weekend picnic when his children throw garbage out of the back window of their moving car. John is pulled over and given a ticket for $50. Can he succeed by arguing that he did not know what his children were doing in the back seat and that he had no criminal intent to break any laws?
A. No, because this is likely a strict liability law that does not provide protection based on mental state.
B. Yes, because he did not know what his children were doing in the back seat, and he did not participate in the offense and did not know they did it or intended to do it.
C. Because the police cannot prove who threw the trash out the back window.
D. No, because his criminal intent is clearly established by the circumstances of the event.

Question: The landlord has a three-story building. The lessor delivered the building and the surrounding property to the lessee for rent for six years, starting from December 1, 2003, and ending on November 30, 2009. On April 15, 2004, the neighbor, who owned an adjacent plot of land, burned leaves and underbrush on their land. Due to the strong wind blowing in the direction of the lessor's land, the fire spread to the lessee's territory. The building caught fire, and the damage from the fire amounted to $150,000. Because of the fire, the lessee did not occupy the rented premises from the day of the fire, as the building was unfit for habitation. This state is governed by common law. Additionally, the statute of limitations for bringing an action for damages due to negligence is five years from the date of the occurrence of the damage. On May 1, 2004, the lessor filed a lawsuit against the lessee, claiming non-payment of rental payments. The court should be
A. in favor of the lessor, since the lessee remains obligated to pay rent even if the property became unfit for habitation due to the fire.
B. in favor of the lessor, because the obligation to pay rent is linked to the land.
C. in favor of the lessee, as it would be unfair to enforce the terms of the rental agreement in the lease contract when the premises became unfit for habitation due to the fire or other natural disasters.
D. in favor of the lessee, as more and more states are adopting laws that release the lessee from their obligation to pay rent if the premises become unfit for habitation due to fire or other natural disasters.

Question: The man is accused of murdering his wife. The accusation states that on December 17th, the man killed his wife by giving her a mass injection of succinylcholine while she was sleeping. Succinylcholine is a drug that anesthesiologists use in small quantities as a muscle relaxant. The accusation claims that the lethal dose given to the wife so paralyzed her respiratory muscles that she suffocated. Other accusations state that the main motive for the man was to get the life insurance policy on his wife worth $500,000 USD, for which he was the beneficiary. The defense called a doctor as the first witness who signed the death certificate. The defense attorney asked her: "Isn't it true that the cause of death was a heart attack?" The doctor answered negatively and stated that the cause of death was unknown. The defense attorney for the defendant called this recent fabrication and asked her if she had claimed during the investigation that the cause of death was a heart attack. The prosecution immediately objected to this point. The judge must decide whether this question:
A. raises an objection because the party cannot impugn its own witness.
B. raises an objection because the defense attorney did not lay a proper foundation.
C. does not raise objections because the party can impugn its own witness through a prior inconsistent statement.
D. does not raise objections because the doctor's testimony at the trial, which took place shortly after the death, was more reliable.

Question: The defendant decided to rob a bar because he knew that the new security system in the bar was malfunctioning, and that night was the best time for the crime. Late in the evening, the defendant broke into the bar and began loading large barrels of beer onto his truck. As he was leaving, he accidentally dropped a lit match into the trash can behind the bar. Soon after, the trash caught fire and a small fire started. Although the accused managed to extinguish the fire without any danger to himself, he did not do so. Instead, he got into his truck and drove away. Despite the fire spreading beyond the trash can, the firefighters responded quickly and were able to extinguish it. The floor behind the bar was charred. Statutes for burglary with assault and arson in this jurisdiction include residential and business structures. For which of the following crimes should the defendant be convicted?
A. Arson, burglary with assault, and theft.
B. Arson and robbery.
C. Theft and robbery.
D. Arson, robbery, and assault.

Question: At the metro station in the city, significant construction is always ongoing, including the reconstruction of the elevator shaft between the platform and ground level. There is a sign warning "this elevator is not working now, please do not use it." A passenger sees the sign but still tries to ride the elevator and gets injured when she falls into the shaft. Question: Daylight Corp. manufactured, assembled, and sold shearing presses for cutting aluminum sheets for can lids. In 2002, Goodboy Beverages purchased a luxurious model of the shearing press from Daylight for $20,000. In 2002 and 2003, Daylight received several complaints about dangerous malfunctions of other customers' cutting presses. In response, Daylight created a safety device and offered it for $5,000 in a brochure sent to all its customers, which mentioned that several users had suffered injuries while using the shearing press model. Goodboy received the brochure but did not purchase the safety device. In 2004, a Goodboy employee was injured by the press. During the trial, Daylight argued that if Goodboy had bought the safety device, the injuries would not have occurred, and sought a directed verdict. The judge should

A. Grant Daylight's request, since Goodboy's refusal to buy the safety device was an effective assumption of risk.

B. Deny Daylight's request, as Goodboy's negligence in not purchasing the safety device was less than Daylight's negligence in initially manufacturing an unsafe press.

C. Deny Daylight's request, as the jury could consider that Daylight could reasonably anticipate that Goodboy would not want to pay $5,000 for a safety device.

D. Deny Daylight's request, as the press was inherently dangerous, and Daylight bore strict liability.

Question: One Sunday, a sports fan went to watch a professional football match. Standing in line near the kiosk, he bumped into three men who were standing ahead of him in line. The three men were friends and had come to watch the game together. One of the men hit the sports fan in the mouth with his fist. A fight broke out. During the fight, one of the other two men hit the fan with a bottle, causing him serious head trauma. The sports fan does not know which of the three men hit him with the bottle. If the sports fan sues the man who hit him in the mouth for compensation for the head injury, will the sports fan win?
A. Yes, because the man who hit him in the mouth was the instigator who started the fight.
B. Yes, because the man who hit him in the mouth and the other two men acted in concert.
C. No, because the man who hit him in the mouth actually did not hit the sports fan with the bottle.
D. No, because the sports fan cannot prove who among the men hit him with the bottle on the head.

Question: The man who owned a haberdashery made a phone order to a wholesale supplier for cashmere and wool clothing. The order was for "three dozen purple cashmere socks, size 1013 at the current resale price." The supplier's sales agent verbally accepted the order at a negotiated price of $250 per dozen. According to the supplier's usual business practice, the sales agent sent a letter confirming the order by mail, which he signed and dated: "According to your telephone order, this letter confirms the purchase of 36 dozens of cashmere socks, color purple, size 10.13, at the agreed price of $250 US per dozen: $9000 US. The letter was glanced over by the man who did not notice the '36 dozens' notation. The man filed the letter away without responding to it. Three weeks later, the supplier offered 36 dozens of purple cashmere socks, which the man rejected on the basis that he had only ordered three dozens. The supplier resold the same purple cashmere socks to another customer for a total of $8000 US. The supplier sued the man for the difference of $1000. If the man relies on fraud as a defense, will this defense be successful?
A. Yes, because the statute was not satisfied by the supplier's tender of goods that were rejected by the man, and the supplier did not rely on oral agreement except for an attempt to deliver.
B. Yes, because the negotiated price for three dozens of socks was over $500, and the supplier's business record incorrectly stated the quantity ordered.
C. No, because the written confirmation from the supplier was sufficient to satisfy the statute against the supplier, and the man, having knowledge of the letter's contents, failed to dispute it within 10 days of receipt.
D. No, because the written confirmation from the supplier acted as an acceptance with additional terms that became part of the contract after the man failed to dispute these additional terms within a reasonable time.

Question: The land development company was the owner of a 400-acre plot in the area of Great Lakes. Over time, the land development company developed two residential areas, eastern and western developments, each containing 150 acres. These subdivisions were created by separate plats that did not relate to one another. However, the restrictions on the plats were practically identical. Plans and every document provide that “the use of the land conveyed here is limited to single-family residences only, and this agreement is intended to apply to each lot in the subdivision and shall be applied together with the land, obliging each owner of a lot, their heirs, and assigns.” After all lots, except four, in each subdivision were sold by the land development company, it sold 50 acres out of the remaining 100 acres of land to a local club under an instrument that contains such provisions: “This instrument is executed and adopted with the understanding that the above-described property is so limited as (1) the described property may be used as a local club with a golf course, swimming pool, tennis courts, clubhouse, eating facilities, and other appropriate improvements for a local club (2) the described property may also be divided and allocated as a residential subdivision similar to the eastern development, and after which the property will be used and conveyed subject to the limitations regarding occupancy, which must conform to these limitations affecting the eastern development. (3) the limitations set forth in this document are considered agreements that operate with the land, and in the event of any breach of any agreement in this document, the person granting the right – the land development company, its successors and assigns – may, at its option, re-enter and terminate the right of ownership conveyed by this document.” At the time of this transfer, the land development company retained the right of ownership on the remaining 50 acres in the initial mass of 400 acres. What below best describes the interest of the local club in the SO-acre mass that it acquired from the land development company?
A. The servitude is easily determinable.
B. The servitude is simple upon the following conditions.
C. The servitude, which is determined, is enforceable.

Question: The married couple sued the real estate broker for inducing them to enter into a contract and breaching the contract terms due to the broker's failure to fulfill his promises regarding the purchase of a house. They claimed that they received promises from the broker that if they bought the house immediately, the seller would give them a discount of $15,000 after closing. During the trial against the broker, the couple called one of the broker's agents to testify, who testified that he was present at a meeting with the buyers and heard the broker make the same promise. B. The testimony is inadmissible because the agent was not authorized to represent his principal.
C. The testimony is inadmissible because it is mere hearsay offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
D. The testimony is admissible even if it is hearsay, as the broker is available for cross-examination.

The information for the year 2 is as follows: Segment (in thousands) A B C Total reported revenue $ 42 $ 121 $ 14 $ 177 Reported income (loss) $ 12 $ 65 $ (3) $ 74 Assets $ 470 $ 800 $ 80 $ 1350 Which of Swift's segments need to be disclosed separately in the financial statements for December 31, 2? A. Only A and B. B. Only A and C. C. Only B and C. D. A, B and C.

Question: A 62-year-old bachelor sold his main residence for a clean sum of $500,000 after all expenses on the sale. Decker bought the house 15 years ago and occupied it until it was sold. On the date of sale, the value of the house was $200,000. Over six months, Decker bought a new house for $600,000. How much should Decker recognize from the sale of the residence?
A. $0
B. $50,000
C. $175,000
D. $300,000

Question: The project should be accepted if the present value of cash flows from the project equals
A. The initial investments.
B. Less than the initial investments.
C. More than the initial investments.
D. Zero.

Question: Skytop Co. is considering the purchase of a machine for $80,000 that will provide a uniform annual cash inflow of $25,000 over four years. Skytop evaluates capital projects using the discounted cash flows method with a cost of capital of 10% per year. Based on the table below, what should Skytop do regarding the purchase of the machine and why? Future value of $1 at 4 years at 10% $1.464 Current value of $1 at 4 years at 10% $0.683 Future value of $1 ordinary annuity at 4 years at 10% $4.641 Current value of $1 ordinary annuity at 4 years at 10% $3.170 A. Yes, the net cash flow is $20,000 B. Yes The net present value is $36,025 C. No, there is no net present value ($750) D. No, there is no net present value ($8750)

Question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding a shareholder's right to inspect corporate books and records? 
A. It is absolute.
B. Provided that the demanding shareholder owns shares worth at least $5,000.
C. It requires that the demand for inspection be made with a proper purpose.
D. It exists only when it involves fraud or illegality.

Question: What is the main difference between the approaches to production that are used in just-in-time (JIT) and traditional methods?
A. JIT typically involves a large number of suppliers, whereas traditional methods typically involve only a few suppliers.
B. JIT requires centralized purchasing, whereas traditional methods encourage employee purchasing decisions.
C. JIT uses a push system, whereas traditional methods use a pull system.
D. JIT operates with low inventory levels, whereas traditional methods can operate with high inventory levels.

Question: On July 7, 7, the Dean Co. issued bonds with a premium with a term of redemption on July 1, 12. Dean incorrectly used the straight-line method instead of the effective interest rate method to amortize the premium. As of June 30, 12, what effect did the error have on the following amounts? Bonds. Undistributed profit
A. Overstated Understated
B. Understated Overstated
C. Overstated No effect
D. No effect

Question: What is the price of a three-year bond (nominal value $100) with a 5% coupon and a 6% yield?
A. $100
B. $104.29
C. $96.71
D. $97.33

Question: Which of the following events is most likely to indicate the existence of related-party transactions?
A. Insuring the lives of key executives and noting the organization as beneficiary.
B. Sale of real estate at a price significantly different from its appraised value.
C. Issuance of a loan with specified planned repayment terms.
D. Granting options on stock to key executives at favorable prices.

Question: Sokro uses an indirect method to prepare a statement of cash flows. In determining its net cash provided by (used in) operating activities, Sokro should add which of the following to the change in net assets?
A. Purchase of equipment.
B. Payment of long-term debt.
C. Depreciation.
D. Reduction of accounts payable.

Question: The CPA prepared a tax return that included a tax shelter transaction that was disclosed in the return. Which of the following situations would not result in a penalty for the individuals who prepared the tax return?
A. The position had significant authority.
B. It was reasonable to believe that the position would not be sustained.
C. There was a reasonable likelihood of success on the position.
D. There was a sufficient basis for the position.

Question: The first reporting period of the company under IFRS relates to the year ended 31 December, 2 years ago. During the preparation of the report on the financial situation for the year 2, the management found an error, due to which the recognition of losses of $90,000 was not recorded. $40,000 of recognized losses related to the event of the year 1, and $50,000 related to the event of the year 2. What amount of recognized losses should the company report in the IFRS financial report for the year ended 31 December, 1 year ago?
A. $0
B. $40,000
C. $50,000
D. $90,000

Question: The basis of taxation for Gulde in Chyme Partnership was $26,000 at the time when Gulde received a liquidating distribution of $12,000 in cash and land with a adjusted basis for Chyme of $10,000 and fair market value of $30,000. Chyme had no unrealized accounts receivable, inventory, or property given by its partners. What was the value of the land of Gulde?
A. $0
B. $10,000
C. $14,000
D. $30,000

Question: During the review of the company's financial statements for the year ended December 31, 1, the auditor notes that the company's sales significantly increased in December 1, with a corresponding decrease in January 2. Evaluating the risk of fraud in financial reporting or misappropriation of assets, what should be the auditor's primary indication of potential sales revenue fraud?
A. There are wide signs of misappropriation of assets.
B. There are signs of embezzlement of the company's property.
C. There are signs of ticket forgery.
D. There are many signs of fraud in financial reporting.

Question: After reviewing the organization's policy on end-user computing (EUC), the internal auditor checks the actuarial function and finds that some minimum control requirements are missing. What is the risk of using potentially incorrect files developed by the end-user?

A. Management relies equally on files as on files created from mainframes.
B. Management receives limited information for decision-making due to the lack of flexibility in EUC files.
C. Management is unable to quickly respond to competitive pressure.
D. Management continues to incur additional costs as EUC requires more hours to perform tasks.

Question: The following information relates to the company Dash Co.'s utility bills: Period Covered Amount Payment Date 16 April – 15 May $5,000 1 June 16 May – 15 June $6,000 1 July 16 June – 15 July $8,000 1 August What amount should Dash report as a liability in its balance sheet as of 30 June?
A. $6,000
B. $7,000
C. $10,000
D. $14,000

Question: Ace Co. issued 1000 shares of its common stock at $15 per share cash. How would this transaction be reflected in Ace's cash flow statement for the year of issuance?
A. $15000 cash inflow from financing activities.
B. $10000 cash inflow from financing activities and a $5000 adjustment to obtain cash flows from operating activities.
C. $15000 cash inflow from investing activities.
D. $10000 cash inflow from investing activities and $5000 adjustment to obtain cash flows from operating activities.

Question: On December 31, 1 year, the wife died. There were no orphans in the couple. What should be the status of the submission of the application by the surviving couple on 2 years?
A. Unmarried.
B. The couple submits jointly.
C. Qualified widow (widow).
D. Head of household.

Question: The Cobb Inc. inventory on May 1 consisted of 200 units with a total value of $1250. Cobb uses periodic inventory method. Purchases for the month were as follows: Date Quantity Unit price Total price May 4 20 5.80 $ 116.00 May 17 80 5.50 $ 440.00 Cobb sold 10 units on May 14 for $120. What is the average selling price of the items sold by Cobb in May?
A. $60.20
B. $62.10
C. $62.50
D. $65

Question: Vale is a 50% partner in Ball Partnership. The company's tax basis in Ball on January 1 was $60,000. Ball had no unrealized accounts receivable, valued inventory or assets, given by his partners. On December 31, Ball divided the undistributed cash of $10,000 to each partner. Ball Partnership's tax return reports the following items for the year 1: Unrecognized percentage income $80,000 Dividend income 12,000 What is the total amount of Ball's gross income that should be included in the adjusted gross income of Vale for the year 1? 
A. $6,000
B. $16,000
C. $36,000
D. $46,000

Question: When reviewing the financial statements of a company that is not the issuer, the accountant learns of several lease agreements that should be capitalized but are not. The accountant believes these lease agreements are material to the financial statements. The accountant decides to modify the standard audit report because management will not capitalize the lease agreements. Under these circumstances, the accountant should
A. Issue a qualified opinion due to departure from GAAP.
B. Express no assurance regarding the organization's financial statements.
C. Emphasize that the financial statements are intended for limited use.
D. Disclose the departure from GAAP in a separate paragraph of the accountant's report.

Question: What from the below is considered part of the necessary additional information for external general-purpose government financial reporting?
A. The financial report of the fund.
B. Combined report of a small fund.
C. Notes to financial reporting.
D. Management discussion and analysis.

Question: What is the deadline for submitting the federal wealth tax return (Form 706) for a taxpayer who died on May 15, 2, if it is assumed that a request for an extension of the deadline has not been submitted?
A. September 15, 2
B. December 31, 2
C. January 31, 3
D. February 15, 3

Question: If the objective of the audit of details is to detect overstatement of sales volume, the auditor should trace transactions from
A. Sales journal to sales invoices.
B. Delivery documents to cash receipt journal.
C. Profit and loss account to customer orders.
D. Customer orders to sales journal.

Question: Which of the following parameters would be considered observable Level 2 input data for determining the fair value of an asset or liability, except
A. Quotations of prices for identical assets and liabilities on inactive markets
B. Quotations of prices for similar assets and liabilities on active markets
C. Internally generated forecasts of cash flows for the relevant asset or liability
D. Observable interest rates that can be observed through standard time intervals

Question: If Jeanne sues Doug Dogman under the theory of strict liability, the court is most likely to find in favor of
A. Jeanne, because Doug's dog was the actual cause of Jeanne's injuries.
B. Doug, because the retriever is a domesticated animal.
C. Doug, if the statute or ordinance does not prohibit letting dogs on public streets.
D. Doug, because the rule of strict liability for dogs would not include dogs that do not demonstrate vicious propensities.

Question: A homeowner transferred his property to his first cousin "for life, with the remainder to the heirs (of the homeowner)". Later, the first cousin transferred the property to a farmer "until he will be working this property". After the first cousin's death, the homeowner's heirs brought an action against the farmer for right of ownership. Which general law doctrine will be most applicable for the court to determine the right of ownership in the property?
A. The Rule in Wild's Case.
B. The doctrine of destruction of conditional remainders.
C. The doctrine of worthier title.
D. The Rule against Perpetuities.

Question: A person on trial got into an argument with a neighbor. When they were arguing, the person on trial pulled out a penknife, intending only to scare the neighbor. The person on trial accidentally slightly cut the neighbor's arm with the knife. The person on trial did not know that the neighbor was suffering from hemophilia, which then caused the neighbor to die from the cut. What is the most serious crime that the person on trial can be convicted of?
A. Murder.
B. Intentional murder.
C. Unintentional murder.
D. Manslaughter.

Question: A consumer from state A filed a lawsuit against a manufacturer registered and based in state B for $100,000 for products, claiming that the product's defect caused the consumer serious injuries. The manufacturer responded by filing a third-party claim against the product designer, also registered and based in state B. The manufacturer argued that the designer was fully responsible for the defect that caused the injuries, and that the manufacturer was not liable. Which of the following arguments is most likely to achieve the designer's goal of dismissing the third-party claim?

A. The court lacks subject-matter jurisdiction over the third-party claim because both the manufacturer and the designer are citizens of state B.
B. The manufacturer failed to obtain the court's permission to file the third-party claim.
C. The manufacturer's failure to follow the designer's specifications resulted in a defect that caused the consumer's injuries.
D. The manufacturer's third-party claim did not include a proper joinder of the third-party defendant.

Question: One day at night the victim was at home when she heard a knock on the door. When the victim opened the door, three defendants were standing in front of her. They pushed the victim into her house and threatened her with bodily harm if she did not cooperate. Tying her up with ropes, the trio continued to search the victim's house. Then they put a lot of the victim's valuables and other things in a large sack and quickly left her house. Which crimes should the defendants be convicted of?
A. Assault, beating, and robbery.
B. Theft, robbery, and robbery.
C. Robbery and robbery.
D. Only robbery.

Question: Max went into a mini-market, took out a pistol and demanded that the cashier empty the cash register. When he nervously looked around for the police, the cashier stretched out his hand and tried to grab the pistol. After that, Max dropped the pistol, which accidentally fired, killing a nearby customer. Max is charged with first-degree murder. He is likely to be
A. Acquitted, since he did not have the necessary intent, necessary for first-degree murder.
B. Acquitted, since the direct cause of death was the cashier's actions.
C. Convicted, since any death that is a natural and probable consequence of a crime is first-degree murder.
D. Convicted, since the use of deadly force implies intent to inflict serious bodily harm.

Question: The man was arrested and charged with robbery. After being taken into custody, he received his Miranda rights, and then was taken to the police station to prepare a protocol. In the station, the man told the policeman that he was willing to confess. After this, the policeman turned on the video recorder and recorded the man's confession on video. At the trial, the prosecution called the policeman to testify about the incriminating statements the man made in his confession. After the man's lawyer objected, the proposed testimony of the officer of the police is
A. inadmissible, since the video recording is the best evidence of the man's confession.
B. not acceptable, since it is hearsay that is not within any exception.
C. acceptable, since the policeman knew about the confession from the start.
D. acceptable, because the man had been given his Miranda rights before the confession was obtained.

Question: The state educational agency, following all requirements of the law, received the land parcel through a known domain. The landowner accepted the fair market value and did not appeal it. Over the next 15 years, the agency held the property, but did not use it for educational purposes. In the 16th year, the agency refused the planned educational use and sold it on a properly announced auction according to state law. The original landowner filed an appeal, claiming that the agency is taking only a fee that can be determined, and when it stopped the purposeful use in educational purposes, the right to the higher level of ownership was returned to the original owner. Will the appellate court likely decide that the landowner can claim the right to stop the attempt of transfer?

A. No, because the state also acquired a paid simple right of ownership through adverse possession after 11 continuous years of possession.
B. No, because the original transfer was made lawfully, and the landowner received the fair market value, thus allowing the presumption of the agency's fee simple ownership.
C. Yes, the notable domain is limited to the use of the property, which is urgently needed for public use, and its non-use for this purpose loses the agency's right of ownership.
D. Yes, because every acquisition of a notable domain involves a payment that can be simply determined for the state acquisition.

Question: A man claims to have inherited property from a wealthy businessman. The birth certificate of the man indicates that he was born out of wedlock. The protocol of the proceedings on alimony shows that the businessman was recognized as the father of the man. However, the man can only establish his status as the heir of the businessman if he was legally married to his mother after his birth. Thus, the man must prove that this marriage was. The man's lawyer was unable to find any certificate or testimony of the marriage. However, the lawyer has a photograph showing a couple dressed in wedding attire. The scene is the facade of a church. It can be seen that passersby are throwing rice at the couple, and they seem to be smiling and bowing in response. The man gave the photograph to his lawyer. He found it in the belongings of his mother after her death. The man believes that the bride on the photograph is his mother. He cannot recognize the groom. A former acquaintance of the businessman, who saw the photograph, told the lawyer that he believes the groom is the businessman. If the lawyer wants to present the photograph as evidence that the mother and the businessman were married, the judge must make a ruling on the photograph.
A. acceptable, only if the photographer is available to testify about the circumstances in which the photograph was taken.
B. acceptable, only if a witness confirms that it is a correct and accurate representation of the relevant facts.
C. not acceptable as inadmissible hearsay not falling under any recognized exception.
D. not acceptable as not the best evidence.

Question: A man is being tried for manipulating securities. He becomes a witness in his own defense. During direct examination, the man's lawyer presents evidence of his good character. If the prosecution objects, which of the following statements is correct?
A. The defendant may present evidence to prove his credibility.
B. The defendant may present evidence to show his integrity.
C. The defendant may not present evidence to show integrity, as character evidence is inadmissible.
D. The defendant may not present evidence of credibility unless it is cross-examined.

Question: How many people together kidnapped a painting from an art museum. One of them, who was a driver, was detained during the commission of another crime. He told the police, "I even didn't receive money from the art museum. It all went to the first guy and the second guy." When the first and second guys are tried for the theft of the painting, does the driver's statement come under review in court?
A. Yes, as a confession of a party opponent.
B. Yes, as a statement against the interests of other defendants.
C. No, because it was made during detention and therefore is unreliable.
D. No, because this statement was not made in the course of or in aid of a conspiracy, and therefore it is hearsay.

Question: A high school student ran for president of the student council. He was the best student chosen to be honored by the class. In some way he delivered a campaign speech at school assembly that was full of vivid stories and anecdotes about the fictional sexual exploits and heroism of certain teachers and students. Several teachers and students complained. The principal suspended him for five days and stripped him of honors. The student together with his parents filed a lawsuit in federal court demanding an injunction and damages on the basis of the First Amendment's freedom of speech. The federal court ruled in favor of the student, but the case was transferred to the Supreme Court of the United States for final ruling. Did the Supreme Court uphold the aid given to the student?

A. No, the school was performing its proper function in attempting to limit the use of obscenity and inflammatory discourse in a high school where freedom of speech may be limited.

B. Yes, despite some discomfort for teachers and students, the immature presentation should be tolerated with respect to the need to give students a platform for free speech.

C. No, the student did not have a right to free speech, especially considering the violent disturbances in schools in recent years.

D. Yes, in modern society, sexual innuendos and sexual humor are so woven into the fabric of society that in the interests of free speech this is what should be tolerated.

Question: A man told two men that the medical equipment company now uses an old river warehouse to store defibrillators. One evening, two men broke into the warehouse and began loading large boxes of defibrillators onto their truck. When they left, one of the men accidentally threw a lit cigarette into a pile of old cardboard boxes and papers. Shortly after, the trash ignited in a small fire. Although the men were able to extinguish the fire without any danger to themselves, they did not do so. Instead, they fled. Meanwhile, the fire quickly spread, engulfing the entire warehouse. If later the accused is charged as an accomplice to the conspiracy, he is most likely to be held accountable
A. accessory before the fact.
B. second-degree director.
C. accomplice.
D. none.

Question: The landlord owns a two-story building. The lessor leased the building and surrounding chattels to the lessee for a term that began on December 1, 2006, and ended on November 30, 2008. Their lease contained the following provisions: "The lessee is required to pay rent in the amount of $500 per month on the first day of each month and to maintain the building located in the leased premises in the same good condition as on the date of the lease." On April 15, 2007, the lessee hosted an annual party called "Tax Time," where she and her friends all went to the post office to mail their taxes, and then drank and dined at the lessee's apartment to celebrate. After a few drinks, one of the lessee's friends became belligerent towards one of the partygoers who had disputed some of the friend's expenditures. The friend then charged at another partygoer and crashed into a wall after the latter stepped off the road. As a result of the accident, one of the apartment's walls was damaged. This fact pattern is a jurisdiction of common law. In addition, the applicable statute of limitations for a claim for damages for negligence is five years from the time the cause of damage arose. In the corresponding claim for interpretation of the lessee's obligation under the agreement to maintain the premises in repair, as stated below, which is the most accurate?

A. The lessee is liable for normal wear and tear under the repair agreement.
B. The lessee is liable for such an agreement for all defects, including the damage to the wall.
C. The lessee's agreement to repair is void ab initio as against public policy, since the lessor is required to perform repairs on the disappeared premises.
D. The lessee's obligation to maintain the premises in a good state of repair releases the lessor from the obligation to disclose any hidden defects.

Question: A contractor was hired to fumigate one of two buildings in a condominium complex that shared a wall. The owners of the complex informed the contractor that the shared wall separating the infested building from the uninfested one was a fireproof wall. The contractor conducted its own thorough inspection and found that the buildings were indeed separated by a wall. The residents of the uninfested building were told to evacuate, but the residents of the uninfested building were told they could stay until the other building was treated. During and shortly after the fumigation, in which a highly toxic chemical was used, many residents of the uninfested building became ill. It was determined that their illnesses were caused by the fumigant. In fact, there was a hole in the fireproof wall separating the two buildings, but since it could only be seen from a particular vantage point in the crawl space of the uninfested building, it was not discovered by either the contractor or any previous building inspector. Is it likely that the residents of the uninfested building will win a tort action against the contractor?

A. No, because the condominium owners were responsible for the accurate reporting of the condition of their buildings.
B. No, because the contractor exhibited a high level of care.
C. Yes, because the contractor may be held strictly liable for its actions.
D. Yes, because the contractor released a hazardous product into the stream of commerce.

Question: A man and his wife were in an unhappy marriage. The man was an alcoholic who physically abused his wife when drunk. One night, the man beat his wife, and she decided to kill him. The wife, who had experience with firearms, planned to shoot the man while he slept. Before carrying out her plan, the wife took out a life insurance policy on her husband for $1,000,000, naming herself as the beneficiary. Shortly after, the couple celebrated their 10th wedding anniversary. They went out for dinner and had a truly pleasant evening together. After a wonderful night, the wife changed her heart and decided that she really loved her husband and did not want to kill him. The wife confessed and told her husband about her plan, begging for forgiveness. The husband was shocked. He filed for divorce and informed the police about his wife's plan. If the wife is charged with attempted murder, she will be found
A. guilty, because she bought the life insurance policy.
B. guilty, because she intended to kill her husband.
C. not guilty, because she did not commit a substantial act in the commission of murder.
D. not guilty, because she actually backed out of the criminal activity.

Question: Two first cousins acquired the right of ownership to real property as joint tenants with the right of survivorship. The first cousin pledged his share of the joint tenancy as security for a loan of $20,000 and executed a court order. Later this was entered as a judgment against the first cousin's share of the property. The first cousin died a year later. The second cousin decided to sell the property, but the mortgagee filed a suit to enjoin the sale and to have himself brought in. The second cousin defended on the ground that any right of mortgage against the first cousin's share of the property was extinguished after the first cousin's death. Will the court bring in the mortgagee against the sale of the property by the surviving first cousin?
A. Yes, because the first cousin's consent to the mortgage by the court decree is presumed by law, and this consent destroyed the joint tenancy.
B. Yes, because a mortgage or court order against one joint tenant destroys the tenancy and destroys the right of survivorship.
C. No, because a joint tenant cannot on legal grounds bring in a court order solely as to the interests of that joint tenant, since this would be an unconstitutional interference with the rights of the other.
D. No, because when the first cousin died, the second cousin became sole owner by virtue of the right of survivorship, in accordance with the joint tenancy, which was entirely unaffected.

Question: In which of the situations the defendant's intoxication could not have been used to refute his criminal charge?
A. The defendant had drunk a fifth of bourbon. Later that day he approached the victim and, wielding a knife, told her to go with him, or he would strike her. He led the victim to his car, and then told her to undress. When the victim was removing her stockings, she kicked the defendant in the head, temporarily injuring him. Then the victim safely escaped from the car. The suspect was arrested and charged with attempted rape.
B. The defendant had been at a wedding in a hotel, where he had drunk several vodka daiquiris. After drinking, the defendant began a violent argument with the hotel parking attendant. The defendant took a lug wrench from his car and threw it at the attendant. The attendant missed the defendant and hit the victim, who was entering the hotel. The defendant was arrested and charged with assault with intent to commit a battery.
C. The defendant had drunk alcoholic beverages all evening in a bar with three of his friends. A detective in undercover heard the defendant and his friends plan to rob the bar after closing. When the defendant tried to pull out a gun from his coat, he was quickly disarmed and arrested by the detectives. The defendant is charged with attempted robbery.
D. At his law school graduation party, the defendant had drunk two cases of beer. Around midnight, a girl approached the defendant and asked him to drive her home. Despite the fact that the girl was only 15 years old, she looked like a woman of about 20. The defendant, who had been watching the girl all night, quickly agreed and showed her the way to his car. Once inside, they engaged in sexual intercourse. The age of consent in this jurisdiction is 17 years for women. The defendant was later arrested and charged with rape.

Question: A hunter shot at a deer, which was open to hunters with rifles, in the forest. One hunter shot at the deer, hoping to hit and kill it. Instead, he hit and injured a tourist. The hunter did not understand that the injured person was a tourist. Does the injured traveler have a claim against the hunter for battery?
A. No, because the hunter did not intend to shoot at the tourist.
B. No, because the hunter did not have direct physical contact with the tourist.
C. Yes, because the bullet from the hunter's rifle had direct physical contact with the tourist.
D. Yes, because the hunter intentionally shot the rifle.

Question: A woman owned four beach houses. Each house had windows in the form of a star. Since the hurricane season was approaching, she hired a carpenter to build the star-shaped windows and deliver them to the four houses. Due to the unique shape of the windows, the carpenter had to do all the work by hand. The carpenter and the woman signed a contract, according to which the carpenter promised to build and deliver storm windows to all four beach houses within 30 days, and the woman promised to pay $8,000 (2,000 dollars per cottage) within one week after completion of the work. Two weeks after signing the contract, a fire destroyed the carpenter's workshop, where he stored all the completed storm windows awaiting delivery. Then the carpenter sent the woman a letter, which read: "The fire destroyed my equipment and inventory, including the completed storm windows that were waiting for delivery. I am ruined and cannot fulfill my contractual obligations. Then the woman called the carpenter and told him: "If you do not fulfill your contractual obligations, I will sue you!" In a lawsuit to specifically enforce the carpenter to build and deliver the storm windows, the woman, most likely will

A. be successful, because the carpenter's loss of inventory does not justify his obligation to perform.
B. be successful, because the beach houses will suffer serious damage in the event of a hurricane without the installation of storm windows.
C. not be successful, because the carpenter's performance would be justified by an unforeseen act of God.
D. not be successful, because the carpenter's loss of inventory will make his work impossible.

Question: The owner of the ranch – the owner of a ranch located at the top of a mountain. Below the ranch is an estate owned by a millionaire. The stream – is a non-navigable watercourse, which begins at the top of the mountain and flows into the valley. Both the ranch and the estate are within the watershed of the stream. When the millionaire bought the estate in 1956, he began taking water from the stream and using it for irrigation of the southern half of his property, which he used as a farm. By 1956, the southern half of the estate had been cleared and put into cultivation, while the northern half remained wooded and unused. The millionaire continued this established model of use and never ceased using the water in this way. In 1986, the owner of the ranch built a house on the ranch and began taking water from the stream for domestic use. In that year there were heavy rains, and this caused the stream to flow from the mountain at a high water level. However, in 1987 a drought caused a very low water level. Thus, there was enough water only for irrigation of the millionaire's agricultural land or, alternatively, for meeting all the domestic needs of the owner of the ranch in water and one quarter of the needs of the millionaire in irrigation. The mountain is in a jurisdiction where the statute of limitations is 15 years. The owner of the ranch continues to take water for personal use, but there is not enough for irrigation of the estate. Then the millionaire brings an appropriate suit in 1996 to declare that his rights to the water in the stream prevail over the rights of the owner of the ranch. In addition, the millionaire moves to have the entire flow of the stream transferred to him, regardless of the impact this may have on the owner of the ranch. If this state follows the common law riparian rights, but not the doctrine of prior appropriation, who should the court rule for?

A. The owner of the ranch, because as the landowner upstream, he would have greater rights to the water than the landowner downstream.

B. The rancher, because domestic use is the better and more protected use than agricultural use.

C. The millionaire, because he received a servitude by prescription to divert as much water as he may need.

D. The millionaire, because he used the water for his benefit before the owner of the ranch, and he has continuously used the water.

Question: Is it likely that the construction company will win a breach of contract claim against the paper company?
A. Yes, the contractor is always entitled to payment for work performed.
B. No, the construction company cannot change the specifications and expect payment.
C. No, the construction company is liable for fraud and deceit.
D. Yes, the construction company has substantially performed the contract.

Question: The federal statute provides funds to states for child protection programs on the condition that such programs are conducted in accordance with federal standards. The United States has filed a lawsuit against the state to the federal court, alleging that the child protection programs in the state, which were partially funded with federal funds allocated under this statute, did not meet federal standards. The state has refused the lawsuit. Is it likely that the court will dismiss the lawsuit?
A. No, because Congress can impose any conditions on the receipt of federal funds.
B. No, since the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit the lawsuit filed by the United States.
C. Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits lawsuits against a state in a federal court.
D. Yes, because the protection of children is the responsibility of the states.

Question: A woman owned a 10-acre tract of rural agricultural land in absolute fee. The woman agreed to sell the agricultural land to a man, and each signed a document that the agricultural land had been sold: “...for $10,000, receipt of which is acknowledged.” In fact, the man had not yet paid the woman $10,000. On the date set for closing, the woman delivered the deed to the man, who gave the woman a check for $10,000. However, a few days after the woman deposited the check, she received a notice from her bank that the check had not been paid because of insufficient funds in the account. The woman then brought an action against the man. At trial, the woman sought to testify that the man had not in fact paid her $10,000 as stated in their written document. The man objected to the woman’s proposed testimony. Should the judge sustain the man’s objection?
A. No, because the parol evidence rule does not apply to events occurring after the execution of the document.
B. No, because the parol evidence rule does not operate to exclude evidence that shows a lack of or absence of consideration.
C. Yes, because the written document appears to be a complete integration of the parties’ agreement.
D. Yes, because the doctrine of debt does not allow the woman to disavow her signed acknowledgment that she received $10,000.

Question: A woman was in her seventh month of pregnancy with her first child. One day, while the woman was preparing a snack in her home kitchen, she looked out the window and witnessed a heinous crime. The woman was horrified as she watched a member of the local gang produce a pistol and use it to shoot a victim, a member of a competing gang. The gang member did not know that someone was witnessing him shoot the victim. The woman watched as the victim fainted and fell dead on the neighbor's lawn. As a result of the shock from witnessing this heinous crime, the woman suffered a miscarriage. If the woman were to sue the member of the local gang who shot the victim, the woman would

A. recover, since she suffered physical injury, not just emotional distress.
B. recover, since the gang member acted intentionally in shooting the victim.
C. not recover, since the woman was not in the zone of danger.
D. not recover, since the gang member did not know that the woman was witnessing.

Question: A man and his passenger were killed in a car accident involving the defendant. The man's wife is now suing for compensation for the loss of companionship and society. The wife testified that she and her husband had a close relationship and were happy in their marriage for over 15 years. During cross-examination, the defendant's attorney asked her if she "knew about the affair her husband had with his passenger?" The wife's attorney immediately objected to the question. The judge must rule that the question is 

A. objectionable because it goes beyond the scope of the direct examination.
B. objectionable because it was very leading.
C. not objectionable, because the wife's knowledge of the affair was relevant to the value of her loss.
D. not objectionable, because it is a question of irrelevance.

Question: The player learned that his friend was planning a vacation to visit a casino. The avid player, who was a passionate fan of college football, approached his friend. The player explained that he wanted to make a bet with a bookmaker on the fact that his favorite team would win the college football championship next year. The player then explained that he had read that the chances of his team winning the football championship next year were listed as 100-1, and he wanted to make a bet on his team for $1,000. The avid player told his friend that he would pay him for his efforts. After further discussion, the avid player wrote the following agreement: “By this I agree to pay my friend $100 if he will bet for me $1,000 on the fact that my favorite team will win the college football championship next year. The bet should be made on My Lucky Sports Book at the casino. I also agree to pay my friend $100 within 30 days after the bet is made. My friend promised not to tell anyone about the bet. After the player and his friend signed the agreement, the player gave him $1,100, that is, $1,000 to make the bet, and $100 as an advance payment for his friend’s efforts. Then the friend went on vacation. Shortly after arrival, the friend tried to make the bet with the player’s lucky bookmaker. However, the friend found that the player’s lucky bookmaker had recently closed its sports book.
