Then the friend went to another casino next door and found that they had a sports book that offered the same odds of 100-1 on the player’s favorite team winning the college football championship next year. The friend made the bet with the sports book of the other casino. Returning from vacation, the friend gave the player’s bookmaker’s card to the player. Nothing more was said until the friend asked the player when he would receive the remaining $100. After this, the player refused to pay the friend any more. What is the best defense of the player in case of a breach of contract by the friend regarding the payment of $100?

A. The contract was invalid ab initio, since the contract could not be fully performed within one year.
B. The fact that the friend made a bet of $1,000 in another casino instead of playing at the player’s casino became a material breach of the contract, which released the player from any further contractual obligations under the terms of the agreement.
C. During the vacation, the friend told his girlfriend about the $1,000 he had bet on behalf of the player.
D. Since the player’s lucky bookmaker no longer had a sports book on which the bet could be made, all contractual obligations were suspended according to the doctrine of impossibility of performance.

Question: A father sues his son for damages after the father trips over a toy left on the floor by his four-year-old grandson. The father regularly visited his son's home and knew that the grandson regularly left toys scattered around the house. The son never warned the father to watch out for the toys. The father seeks damages from the son for his injuries. At the trial, after the evidence is closed, both the father and the son move for a ruling on the issue of liability. The court rejects the doctrine of family immunity and applies the traditional rules of the landowner's liability. What should the court do? 
A. Reject both motions and submit the case to a jury on the issue of the father's negligence.
B. Reject both motions and submit the case to a jury on the basis of strict liability.
C. Grant the father's motion, since the son is legally responsible for failing to warn the father of the danger of leaving toys on the floor.
D. Grant the son's motion, because the son had no duty to warn the father that the grandson might leave toys on the floor.

Question: A man and a woman competed in an illegal drag race. Both were exceeding the speed limit, but were very careful. However, when the woman's car suddenly blew a tire, she lost control and crashed into a pedestrian, injuring him. The pedestrian later sued the man, since the woman had no insurance and no assets. Is it likely that the pedestrian will win this case?
A. No, because the man did not cause bodily harm.
B. No, because the man was driving very carefully.
C. Yes, because the man and woman were acting in concert, performing a dangerous activity.
D. Yes, because the man was exceeding the speed limit.

Question: Which party will prevail?
A. The offeror will prevail because the publication of acceptance completes the contract between the parties.
B. The offeree will prevail because he never accepted the offer on the same terms.
C. The offeror will prevail because he sent the goods when he received the first acceptance.
D. The offeree will prevail because he rejected the offer when he telephoned the offeror's manager.
Question: What, if true, would best support the defense of the bar review course?

Question: In the context of his defense against the charge of murder, the defendant gave testimony that he was committing a bank robbery in another state on the day the victim was killed. The testimony is
A. admissible as a hearsay.
B. admissible as a confession.
C. admissible as a statement against interest.
D. admissible as a present mental condition.

Question: The defendant was charged with murder. The murder took place on February 1. At the time of the crime, this jurisdiction required a unanimous verdict of all 12 jurors to convict for a crime punishable by death. On November 1, the state legislature passed a new law requiring a majority of seven of the 12 jurors to convict for a crime punishable by death. The trial of the defendant began on December 1. He was later convicted of murder by eight votes to four. Following the trial, the defendant's attorney filed a motion to set aside the verdict. What will be the most important constitutional ground for setting aside the verdict?
A. Ex post facto.
B. Contracts clause.
C. Fourteenth Amendment due process.
D. Sixth Amendment right to a fair trial.

Question: A written, non-binding offer (firm offer) of a merchant to sell goods
A. Must be signed separately if the addressee of the offer provides a form contract containing the offer.
B. Has a term of three months.
C. Is not transferable.
D. Cannot exceed three months, even if considered.

Question: A woman was hitchhiking late in the day when a man picked her up. Shortly after this, the man stopped and parked his car on a roadside clearing to rest. They smoked marijuana, when another car came around a curve and crashed into the man's car. As a result of the collision, the man's car was damaged, and the man was injured. The woman also suffered injuries. In fact, the impact caused her to become unconscious for a few minutes. The woman sued the other driver, claiming damages for his alleged negligence. At trial, the woman testified about her physical injuries and the other driver's negligence. In defense, the other driver called an attorney who lived next door to the woman. The attorney offered to testify that after the accident, the woman consulted with him about her claim and confidentially asked the attorney how she could falsely testify that she had not been smoking marijuana at the time of the accident. Which of the following is true about the attorney's testimony?

A. It is admissible as an admission by a party opponent.
B. It is admissible as an admission against interest.
C. It is inadmissible because it violates the woman's right of self-incrimination.
D. It is inadmissible because it violates the attorney-client privilege.

Question: The accused is being tried for kidnapping. The victim showed that one of the kidnappers called the other "Speed". The prosecutor calls a prison officer to testify that, while the accused was in prison awaiting trial, other inmates referred to the accused as "Speed". Are the prison officer's testimony admissible?
A. No, because it is hearsay not an exception.
B. No, because it is significantly more prejudicial than probative.
C. Yes, as an indirect evidence that the accused was one of the kidnappers.
D. Yes, to confirm the credibility of the victim.

Question: A lessee rented a dwelling from a lessor for five years. The rent was due on the first day of each month, and the lessor retained the right to terminate the lease if the lessee failed to perform his obligations. The term of the lease ended 18 months ago. However, the lessee remained in the dwelling and continued to pay the rent on time. The lessor continued to accept the rent. The fair rent for the dwelling is now significantly higher than that paid by the lessee, and the lessor recently found a third party who will pay a higher rent. When the lessee paid the rent six weeks ago, the lessor agreed to pay the rent six weeks ago, the lessor accepted the rent, but verbally told the lessee that he must vacate at the end of the month. The lessee, who still owns the dwelling, informed the lessor that he does not want to move and is willing to pay the current fair rent. The lessor consulted his attorney for advice regarding the right of ownership. Who should say who has the right to own?
A. The lessor, since he properly notified of the termination of the lease.
B. The lessor, since he retained the right to re-entry.
C. The lessee, since he stated that he is willing to pay the current fair rent.
D. The lessee, since the lessor did not provide reasonable grounds for termination of the lease.

Question: The man and his wife were shopping at a local department store when the wife spotted a dress that particularly caught her eye. The wife, who weighed over 300 pounds, was unable to find a large enough size to fit her. She then approached the store clerk and asked if the store carried a dress in her size. The clerk looked at the wife and said, "You look like an elephant, and I'm sorry, but we don't have that size dress." Another customer in the store heard this comment and began to laugh. The wife was very embarrassed and quickly left the store. If the wife were to sue the department store on the basis of the clerk's actions, the wife would be
A. win, because another customer heard the comment.
B. win, because the clerk's behavior was extreme and outrageous.
C. lose, because the clerk was simply expressing his opinion.
D. lose, because the wife was only offended.

Question: A student and a man got into an argument at a bar during a game of pool. The student allegedly started a fight by hitting the man on the head with a pool cue after the man made a winning shot. At the student's trial, the prosecution called one of the student's classmates as a witness. The classmate was not present at the bar fight. The classmate offered to testify that the next day in class he approached the student and said, "That was wrong of you to start a fight with this man over a game of pool," and the student then bowed his head and left. The classmate's testimony is
A. admissible as part of the res gestae.
B. admissible as a hearsay exception.
C. inadmissible as a hearsay statement not within any recognized exception.
D. inadmissible as a self-serving hearsay statement.

Question: The society conveyed to the purchaser a general guarantee deed for the free land plot. Pursuant to the contract, the person receiving the grant and their successors in title were required to participate proportionally in the paving of the road adjacent to the property. The grantee conveyed the property to a married couple by a special guarantee deed that did not contain any conditions of the contract regarding the paving of the new road. The buyers did not have an attorney and did not conduct a search of the title to the property. When the road was completed, the couple refused to pay their share, which was demanded of them. The original sellers served the couple with a summons to court for a claim of specific performance without a jury. The judge ruled that the couple must pay their share of the paving. Will the appellate court affirm the judge's ruling?
A. Yes, because it is a covenant running with the land since it was to be applied to the successors and "successors" of the first buyer.
B. Yes, because the landowner is responsible for their share of improvement of any adjacent private roads in any case.
C. No, because the general guarantee of the original sellers did not extend to the first buyer.
D. No, because the demand for the paving had to be stated in the deed to the couple, and this was not.

Question: The man is charged with murdering his wife. The prosecution claims that on December 17, the man killed his wife by making her a massive injection of succinylcholine while she was asleep. Succinylcholine is a drug that anesthesiologists use in small quantities as a muscle relaxant. The prosecution claims that the lethal dose given to the wife relaxed her diaphragm muscles so much that she suffocated. Other charges claim that the main motive of the man was to obtain his wife's $500,000 life insurance policy, for which he was the beneficiary. The defense called the first witness a doctor who signed the death certificate. The defendant's attorney asked her, "Is it not true that the cause of death was a heart attack?" The doctor replied negatively and stated that the cause of death is unknown. The defendant's attorney called her a recent fabrication and asked her if she had not stated on the investigation that the cause of death was a heart attack. The prosecution immediately objected to this question. The judge must decide that this question is

Question: A patient at a federal hospital reported that a nurse had committed sexual assault against her. The man was arrested. During the trial, the prosecution provided evidence that the man had been convicted of two previous charges of sexual assault against two other women, both committed about two years ago. The charges and manner of the man's actions in those convictions were almost identical to this case. The defense attorney objected to the evidence on the ground that their prejudicial impact outweighs their probative value. Based on the Federal Rules of Evidence, which is the most likely decision the court will make regarding this issue?
A. The evidence is too prejudicial and must be excluded.
B. The evidence is inadmissible because it is not relevant to the charges and has low probative value.
C. The evidence is admissible because current government policy is resolutely in favor of arresting and prosecuting sexual predators.
D. The evidence is admissible because of the actual similarity to this charge, which gives the evidence strong probative value.

Question: What best describes the interest of the country club in the 50-acre tract it bought from the land development company?

A. A determinable fee simple
B. A determinable fee simple subject to an after-acquired title
C. A determinable fee simple
D. A future interest

Question: A man and a woman, who were friends, decided to buy a car together. The man put in $5000, and the woman's father signed a loan for $10,000. The title was registered in the woman's name, and the man paid the credit. They orally agreed that it was joint ownership, equal rights. After a few months their relationship deteriorated. They disputed the right of ownership and use of the car. One day the man tried to drive away with the car, but the woman climbed in and continued to dispute until he drove off. Then he crashed into a pole and destroyed the car just to spite her, saying that if he hadn't been able to have it, no one would have. The police arrested the man for car theft (theft of a vehicle from the owner) and vandalism (damage to someone else's or shared property). If we assume that the above facts are beyond reasonable doubt, which crime or crimes may likely lead to a guilty verdict?

Question: The landlord has a three-story building. The lessor transferred the building and surrounding property to the lessee for a term of six years, starting on December 1, 2003, and ending on November 30, 2009. On April 15, 2004, a neighbor, who owned an adjacent land parcel, set fire to the foliage and underbrush on his land. A strong wind blew in the direction of the land that the lessor had leased to the lessee, and the wind carried the burning foliage onto the lessee's land. The building caught fire, causing $150,000 in damages. As a result of the fire, the lessee did not occupy the leased premises from the day of the fire, since the building was uninhabitable. This is a jurisdiction of common law. Furthermore, the statute of limitations for a claim for damages for negligence is five years from the time the cause of the damage arose. On May 1, 2004, the lessor brings an action against the lessee, alleging a breach of the lease agreement for non-payment of rent. The court should be for
A. the lessor, since the lessee remains obligated to pay rent, even if the property became uninhabitable as a result of the fire.
B. the lessor, since the obligation to pay rent is tied to the land.
C. the lessee, because it would be unfair to enforce the lease provision in the lease agreement because the premises became uninhabitable.
D. the lessee, because more and more states are adopting laws that relieve the lessee of his obligation to pay rent if the premises become uninhabitable due to a fire or other natural disasters.

Question: The landlord owned an apartment that he rented to a college graduate for a three-year term, starting on December 1, 2007, for a monthly rent of $1,000, paid on the first day of each month. After the college graduate lived in the apartment for six months, on June 1, 2008, he transferred his share in this apartment to a college student. The college student paid the rent for two months, then transferred his share to a sophomore. The sophomore entered into possession on August 1, 2008, and paid the rent for August, but did not pay the rent for the next three months of living there. Then on December 1, 2008, the sophomore transferred the premises to a freshman, who acquired it, but did not pay the rent to the landlord during the period of his living there from December 1, 2008 to April 1, 2009. On April 5, 2009, the landlord sues the freshman to collect the unpaid rent for the premises. The freshman is most likely liable for
A. $8,000.00
B. $7,000.00
C. $5,000.00
D. $4,000.00

Question: The case arose in the state courts when the Secretary of Commerce tried to prevent a person from mailing out new brochures. Under the Secretary's interpretation, the new brochures contained obscene photographs and sexual expressions. The Secretary acted pursuant to the authority granted him by section 1123(b) of the state statute, which provided: "If the Secretary of Commerce determines that a commercial mailing to residents of the state is not suitable for minors, the Secretary shall have the authority to prohibit such mailing." The case came to the state's highest court, which held that the statute was unconstitutional because it violated both the commerce clause and the supremacy clause. If this case were to be reviewed by the United States Supreme Court, it would come to the Court

A. by appeal.
B. by certiorari.
C. if five justices voted to review it.
D. despite the doctrine of adequate and independent state grounds.

Question: A person decided to rob a bar because he knew that the bar now used a new security system that was malfunctioning, and that night was the best time for the break-in. Late in the evening, the person broke into the bar and began loading large kegs of beer onto his truck. Going, the person accidentally threw cigarette butts into the trash can behind the bar. Soon after, the trash ignited in a small fire. Although the accused was able to extinguish the fire without any danger to himself, he did not do so. Instead, he got into the truck and drove off. Despite the fact that the fire spread beyond the trash can, the firefighters quickly responded and were able to extinguish it. The floor behind the bar was charred. Statutes in this jurisdiction include arson and burglary of residential and business structures. Which of the listed crimes should the accused be convicted of?
A. Arson, burglary, and theft.
B. Arson and burglary.
C. Burglary and theft.
D. Arson, robbery, and burglary.

Question: In a big city, trash is always a problem. The state statute on littering prohibits throwing trash and other items from any vehicle onto public roads. This is a misdemeanor offense, punishable by a fine of $50 without imprisonment. For the third offense, the fine is $500 and imprisonment for 5 days. The statute contains no requirement of criminal intent. John and his family return from a picnic on a weekend, when his children throw out trash bags and leftover food from the rear window of the moving vehicle. John is stopped and given a $50 ticket. Can he succeed in defending himself by saying he didn't know what his children were doing, and he didn't have the criminal intent to violate any laws?

A. No, because it is probably a strict liability statute that does not allow for a defense based on mental state.
B. Yes, because he didn't know what his children were doing in the back seat, and he wasn't participating in the violation and didn't know they were doing it or planning to do it.
C. Yes, because the police cannot prove who in the car threw the trash out the window.
D. No, because his criminal intent is clearly established by the circumstances of the event.

Question: The accused was arrested and charged with conspiracy to obtain a kidnapped person. During the presentation of the accused, he was represented by a defense attorney. After posting bail, he was released. After his release, the defendant again settled in as a bartender at a local bar. Three weeks before the scheduled trial of the accused, an informant entered the bar. After a few drinks, the informant began a conversation with the defendant, who was on duty at the time. The defendant did not know that the man was a paid informant for the police. During their conversation, the informant told the defendant that he had read about his arrest in the newspapers and asked the defendant for the names of his accomplices. Unaware of anything, the defendant made some confessions, which the informant then passed on to the prosecutor. In the court session, the prosecution tried to use the defendant's confessions as evidence. The defendant's request to exclude this proposal of evidence will most likely be
A. refused, as the defendant's statements were voluntary.
B. denied, as the defendant took the risk that his trust in the informant was misplaced.
C. granted, as the defendant's right to a lawyer under the Sixth Amendment was violated.
D. granted, as the defendant's right against self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment was violated.

Question: What is the most accurate statement regarding the oral promise of the dean?

A. Parol evidence is admissible to show that the parties agreed to their written contract only as a partial integration of their entire contract.
B. Parol evidence is admissible to confirm a subsequent oral agreement that modifies or contradicts the terms of the prior written contract.
C. Admissible evidence that shows the written contract is not enforceable due to undue influence or fraud.
D. Evidence is inadmissible to confirm contemporaneous oral agreements that modify or contradict the terms of the written contract.

Question: A passenger on a subway station in a city is always aware of significant construction, including the reconstruction of the elevator shaft between the platform and ground level. There is a sign warning "this elevator is not working, please do not use it." A passenger sees the signs but still tries to ride the elevator and gets injured when she falls into the shaft. When the passenger sues the city for negligence, the city claims she assumed the risk. Is this a valid and accurate defense under these circumstances?
A. Yes, because she was fully informed and should have known the elevator was dangerous based on the signs.
B. Yes, because these signs indicate her own negligence and are a lawful cause of her own injury.
C. No, because the sign did not explain the danger, only that it was not working, and so she did not know what she was getting herself into.
D. No, because the city has strict liability when all rely on the subway.

Question: A man who owned a haberdashery store made an order by phone to an wholesale supplier of woolen and worsted clothing for "three dozen purple worsted scarves, size 10 1/3 at the current resale price." The sales agent of the supplier orally accepted the order at an agreed price of $250 per dozen. In accordance with the usual business practice of the supplier, the sales agent sent a confirming letter by mail which he signed and dated: "Pursuant to your telephone order, this letter serves as confirmation of the purchase of 36 dozen worsted scarves, color purple, size 10 1/3 at the agreed price of $250 per dozen: $9,000. This letter was received by the man who carelessly glanced at it, but did not notice the writing "36 dozen." The man placed the letter in his files and did not respond to it. Three weeks later the supplier offered 36 dozen purple worsted scarves which the man rejected on the ground that he had ordered only three dozen. The supplier resold the same purple worsted scarves to another buyer for a total price of $8,000. The supplier sued the man for the difference of $1,000. If the man pleads fraud as a defense, will such defense be successful?

A. Yes, since the statute was not satisfied by the supplier's tender of goods which were rejected by the man, and the supplier did not rely on the oral agreement, except for the attempt to deliver.
B. Yes, because the agreed price for three dozen scarves was over $500, and the supplier's written confirmation incorrectly stated the quantity of goods ordered.
C. No, because the supplier's written confirmation was sufficient to satisfy the statute against the supplier, and the man, having knowledge of the contents of the confirmation, did not give notice of objection within 10 days after receipt.
D. No, because the supplier's written confirmation acted as an acceptance, with proposals for additional terms which became part of the contract after the man did not object to such additional terms within a reasonable time.

Question: A sports fan went to a professional football match on a Sunday. Standing in line at the kiosk, he quarrelled with three men who were in front of him in line. The three men were friends and together they attended the game. One of the men punched the fan in the mouth. A fight broke out. During the quarrel one of the other three men hit the fan with a bottle on the head, causing him a serious concussion. The sports fan does not know for certain which of the three men hit him with the bottle. If the sports fan sues the man who punched him in the mouth to compensate for the head injury, will the sports fan win?

A. Yes, because the man who punched him in the mouth was the instigator who made the first blow that started the fight.
B. Yes, because the man who punched him in the mouth and the other men acted in concert.
C. No, because the man who punched him in the mouth did not actually hit the sports fan with the bottle.
D. No, because the sports fan cannot provide evidence of who of the men hit him with the bottle.

Question: The owner of a retail store, anticipating an increase in business volumes during the holiday season, decided to hire another employee. On October 31, the owner entered into a written contract with the employee, which provided that the employee would be hired to work at the retail store in November and December for $2000 per month. At the end of November, the owner noticed that the business had not grown as much as he had expected. The owner informed the employee that if he did not agree to reduce his salary, he would be fired. Reluctantly, on December 1, the employee orally agreed to reduce his salary by $500 for December. Which of the following statements regarding the agreement of December 1 between the owner and the employee is the most accurate?

A. This constituted a valid modification of their original written contract.
B. This constituted a valid alteration of their original written contract.
C. This constituted a novation of their original written contract.
D. This did not change the rights and obligations of the parties in accordance with the terms of their original contract.

Question: Daylight Corp. manufactured, assembled, and sold a shear press for cutting steel, intended for cutting aluminum sheets for can lids. In 2002, Goodboy Beverages purchased a luxury model shear press from Daylight for $20,000. In 2002 and 2003, Daylight received several complaints about hazardous malfunctions of other clients' shear presses. In response, Daylight created a safety device and offered it for $5,000 in a brochure sent to all its clients, in which it was mentioned that several users had suffered injuries while using the model shear press. Goodboy received the brochure, but did not purchase the safety device worth $5,000. In 2004, a Goodboy employee was injured by the press. At trial, Daylight argued that if Goodboy had purchased the safety device, the injuries would not have occurred, and it prayed for a directed verdict. The court must

A. Grant Daylight's prayer, since Goodboy's refusal to purchase the safety device was an effective assumption of risk.
B. Deny the prayer, since Goodboy's negligence in not purchasing the safety device was less than Daylight's negligence in manufacturing the dangerous press initially.
C. Deny the prayer, since the jury may consider that Daylight could reasonably have anticipated that Goodboy would not wish to pay $5,000 for a safety device.
D. Deny the prayer, since the press was inherently dangerous, and Daylight bore strict liability.

Question: The couple sued the real estate broker for misrepresentation and breach of contract for failing to perform promises he made regarding the purchase of a home. They claimed they received promises from the broker that if they immediately bought the house, the sellers would give them a discount of $15,000 after closing. At closing, the sellers claimed they did not know and did not pay. During the trial against the broker, the couple called to the stand one of the broker's agents, who testified that he was at a meeting with the buyers and heard the broker make the same promise. The broker denied that the testimony was hearsay.
A. The testimony is admissible because it is an admission by a party made through an authorized agent regarding a matter within his scope of employment.
B. The testimony is inadmissible because the agent was not authorized to act on behalf of his principal.
C. The testimony is inadmissible because it is pure hearsay offered to prove the truth of a disputed fact.
D. The testimony is admissible even if it is hearsay, the broker is available for cross-examination.

Question: A 55-year-old man presents to a physician with a 2-week history of recurrent widespread papules. Physical examination shows lesions most numerous in flexural areas, including inguinal folds and groin. The papules are not easily broken and there are no oral cavity injuries. These papules are most likely the result of an adhesion defect, which includes which of the following?

A. Basal membrane
B. Hair follicles
C. Langerhans cells
D. Melanocytes

Question: A 2-year-old girl was brought to the clinic for a routine check-up. The child was weaned at 6 months and started walking at 10 months. During the medical examination, she had mild genu varum (10th degree). What is the most appropriate recommendation from the options below at this time?
A. Increased consumption of vitamin D
B. Special exercise program
C. Surgical correction
D. No treatment is needed at this time

Question: One evening late, the accountant went into a bar and ordered sour whiskey. The bartender served the drink, although the accountant looked and behaved as if he was already very drunk. The accountant soon drank five more cocktails that the bartender served, despite the fact that the accountant was obviously and unmistakably drunk. After finishing his sixth drink in the bar, the accountant wished the bartender a good night, swaying, left the bar, got into a car and drove. A few blocks swaying back and forth on the road, the accountant crashed his car into a pedestrian who was walking on the sidewalk along the road. The pedestrian received serious back and leg injuries. The bartender's action in serving the drinks to the accountant will most likely be considered as
A. direct cause of the pedestrian's injuries.
B. previous cause of the pedestrian's injury.
C. direct cause of the pedestrian's injuries.
D. intermediate cause of the pedestrian's injuries.

Question: A 27-year-old man was admitted to the hospital 45 minutes after a car accident. Physical examination shows a sluggish reaction to stimuli. The neurological examination does not show other deviations. The X-ray of the skull shows a linear fracture of the skull base without depression. Two weeks later, the patient develops polyuria and polydipsia. Laboratory tests show a normal glucose concentration in the blood serum, increased serum osmolality, and decreased osmolality of the urine. After the introduction of desmopressin, the osmolality of the urine increases. The favorable effect of this drug is most likely due to the activation of which of the following?

Question: A 68-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, which has recurred twice in the last 5 years. She underwent a course of radiation and chemotherapy for metastatic cancer in the bones. Today she comes to the office to request help in dealing with back pain in the middle thoracic segment, so she can use fewer pain medications. The most acceptable osteopathic manipulative technique for treating the spine of this patient is
A. high velocity, low amplitude
B. indirect muscle fascia release
C. isotonical exercise
D. medium velocity, medium amplitude

Question: A 37-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 1-hour history of nausea and vertigo. He has a significant history of variceal hemorrhage due to alcoholic cirrhosis of the liver and ascites, which are being treated with spironolactone. He consumes 8-10 alcoholic beverages daily. While taking additional history, the patient vomits a large amount of bright red blood, and it is difficult to rouse him. Vital signs are: temperature 36.0°C (96.8°F), pulse 110/minute, respiratory rate 12/minute, and blood pressure 90/50 mm Hg. After starting intravenous fluid administration, which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
A. Organize transjugular variceal shunting
B. Start intravenous vasopressin therapy
C. Perform endotracheal intubation
D. Perform upper endoscopy

Question: A 44-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a nodule on her neck, which she noticed 1 week ago. She denies any sensitivity, fever, weight loss, or fatigue. Physical examination reveals a freely movable mass 2 cm in size in the lower left lobe of the thyroid gland. In addition to the level of thyrotropin and free thyroxine, the most appropriate initial method of investigation of this lesion is
A. Nuclear scan of the thyroid gland
B. Iodine-131 scan
C. Fine-needle aspiration
D. Ultrasound of the thyroid gland

Question: A 36-year-old woman, a business executive, is sent to the office for a lipid profile, which shows a total cholesterol of 249 mg/dl. She has a family history of early ischemic heart disease (IHD), and her father died suddenly at age 46 from a myocardial infarction. She tells you that she has never had chest pain. She is not sexually active and has no children. She claims that because of her stressful lifestyle, she cannot eat normally or follow a special diet, and she usually eats fast food. She exercises on a treadmill for 20 minutes, two to three times a week. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. Her only medication is acetaminophen for tension headaches. Her height is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in), and her weight is 76 kg (167 lb); her BMI is 28 kg/m2. Her vital signs are normal today. Physical examination did not reveal any deviations, except for mild obesity. What is the most important step in the prevention of IHD in this patient?

A. A stress-reduction program based on the biologic feedback loop
B. A more rigorous and consistent exercise program
C. A smoking cessation program
D. A strict low-calorie diet

Question: A 27-year-old woman, 2 weeks pregnant, at 12 weeks gestation, presents to the physician for a prenatal visit. She feels well. Her first pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated. Medications include folic acid and multivitamins. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 108/60 mm Hg, and the obstetric examination of the pelvis shows a uterus size consistent with 12 weeks gestation. A urine dipstick shows leukocyte esterase; urinalysis shows leukocytes and rare gram-negative rods. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Recommend drinking 8 ounces of cranberry juice daily
B. Oral therapy with amoxicillin
C. Oral therapy with metronidazole
D. Intravenous therapy with cefazolin

Question: A 40-year-old man presents to the clinic with symptoms of odynophagia and gastroesophageal reflux. He also reports a history of vomiting last week. Past medical history reveals HIV, with a CD4 count of 30 cells/μL. The results of the tilt test and hemoglobin level are normal. A rectal examination reveals dark brown stool that is positive for occult blood. What is the most appropriate initial step in managing this patient?
A. Prescription for a proton pump inhibitor and a prokinetic agent
B. Prescription for a 6-week trial of an H2 blocker
C. Prescription for clotrimazole suppositories
D. Referral for an upper endoscopy with biopsy

Question: A 27-year-old woman presents with a 3-year history of chronic diarrhea and intermittent, crampy abdominal pain. The pain typically decreases with defecation and does not occur at night, nor does it interfere with sleep. She reports being frustrated with her symptoms and has stopped traveling due to frequent, urgent need to defecate. She has no serious medical conditions and is not on any medications. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 70/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and blood pressure 120/80 mmHg. The lower abdomen is mildly tender to palpation; there is no rebound tenderness or guarding. The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory studies are within reference ranges. Stool occult blood testing is negative. Anti-gluten antibodies are absent. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy from the options below?
A. Neefazodone
B. Nortriptyline
C. Phenelzine
D. Sertraline

Question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the clinic for a routine check-up. She was diagnosed with Turner syndrome in childhood during an evaluation for aortic coarctation. During today's visit, her mother reports that the girl has been talking about babies. You have been the girl's doctor for the last 6 years and know that she is in a prepubertal age. What would you most appropriately advise the patient if she wants to have a family, that she should do which of the following?

A. adopt
B. Do an amniocentesis if she becomes pregnant
C. Do an operation
D. Get a genetic consultation

Question: A 37-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus is hospitalized for poor glucose control over the last 2 months. Despite poor control, he demands to be discharged. He reports feeling tired, irritable, and hopeless over the last 3 months, stating, "Sometimes I forget" to follow his diabetic regimen. He avoids his family and friends because he does not feel like seeing them, but admits to being lonely. He did not get out of bed for 2 days, prompting his wife to call emergency services and hospitalize him. His only medication was insulin, which he often missed. He does not use alcohol. His height is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in), and weight is 100 kg (220 lb); his BMI is 36 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 68/minute, respiratory rate 18/minute, and blood pressure 150/85 mm Hg. Physical examination is unremarkable. His mental status examination reveals him to be tired, affect limited. There are no signs of suicidal ideation. His morning serum glucose concentration is 120 mg/dl. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Follow the patient's wishes and discuss home care options
B. Follow the patient's wishes with his consent for care
C. Schedule a neuropsychological evaluation
D. Obtain a court order for appointment of a legal guardian

Question: In 1993 the farmer had a good right of ownership to the farm in absolute form. In 1994 the farmer transferred to his son for $1000 a document signed by the farmer, in which the son and his heirs were named as the subject of the right and looked valid. The son ignored the record. In 1998 the investor, who knew about the existence of the deed of ownership from the farmer to the son, found the farmer and asked to buy the deed of ownership to the farm from the farmer and his heirs for $10,000. The farmer drew up such a deed, and the investor promptly recorded it. The investor's intention was to acquire the color of ownership and obtain the right of ownership by illegal possession. In 1998 the investor built a fence around the farm. In 1999 the son gave his deed to the ranch owner for $15,000, paid by the ranch owner, and signed and handed over the deed to the farm to the ranch owner and his heirs. Having received the document, the ranch owner made no effort to verify the right of ownership, inspect the property or record it. In 2003 the teacher paid the investor $20,000, and the investor handed over the deed of ownership to the farm to the teacher and his heirs. The teacher inspected the property, verified the right of ownership and knew about the previous instrument from the farmer to the son. Despite the fact that the teacher did not live on the territory, he regularly visited the farm twice a week. The teacher recorded his act. In 2007 for $25,000 paid by the professor, the ranch owner signed and handed over the deed of the farm, in which the professor and his heirs were named as beneficiaries. Before the professor paid the ranch owner and took the document, the professor visited the farm and inspected the fence. However, the teacher was not present when the professor visited the property, and nothing indicated who "who" was using it. In any case, the professor did not try to find the name before making the purchase. Then the professor recorded the deed. Note. In this jurisdiction, the "grantee – recipient" index is used, and there is no treaty index. The registration law provides: "Any transfer of real estate that is not registered is null and void as to the next good faith buyer for valuable consideration, which must first be properly registered." In 2008, in a case of ownership of the farm, which of the parties from the above will have the priority of ownership right?
A. Professor.
B. Investor.
C. Teacher.
D. Ranch owner.

Question: A 67-year-old woman presents to her physician with a 4-month history of petechiae. She has a history of lung cancer, which was treated with radiation therapy 6 months ago. She has a 2-year history of hypertension, which has been treated with a thiazide diuretic and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor. The physical examination, including a neurological examination, is normal except for numerous petechiae. Hemoglobin concentration is 13 g/dl, leukocytes 5000/mm3, thrombocytes 35000/mm3. The serum antithrombin antibody test is negative. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnostic workup?
A. CT of the chest
B. CT of the abdomen
C. Bronchoscopy
D. Bone marrow aspiration

Question: A 26-year-old woman with HIV infection presents to the clinic with pain and redness of the left ankle for 4 days. She states that the symptoms appeared after she tripped over a branch in her backyard and scraped her left leg. Current medications include antiretroviral therapy and ibuprofen as needed. Vital signs are: temperature 38.3 °C (100.9 °F), pulse 86/minute, respiratory rate 14/minute, and blood pressure 138/70 mm Hg. There is a 5 × 8 cm area on the anterior surface of the left lower extremity that is swollen, erythematous, and painful. She had a rash after taking erythromycin and had an anaphylactic reaction to penicillin. Which of the following antibiotic therapies is the most appropriate for this patient?

Question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician for a 2-day history of fever and painful swelling of the left ankle. He has had recurrent neck lymphadenitis and pneumonia since childhood. Two years ago, he had a abscess in the neck that grew Staphylococcus aureus. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). Physical examination shows a tender, erythematous, swollen left ankle; point tenderness over the medial malleolus. Radiograph of the bone shows increased uptake in the left lower metaphysis of the tibia. Bone culture grows Serratia marcescens. The nitroblue tetrazolium test does not show a color change. What is the most likely mechanism of these findings?
A. Arrest of B-lymphocyte development
B. Dysmorphogenesis of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouch
C. Chemotaxis defect
D. Defect in phagocytic oxidative metabolism

Question: A 19-year-old college student comes to the student health service 24 hours after the onset of headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia. She does not recall any contact with sick people. She had chickenpox at age 7. Her last examination 1 year ago included a PPD skin test, which was normal. She takes daily polivitamins and a herbal weight loss supplement. She received all recommended vaccinations in childhood, but has not had any since then. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. There is no family history of serious illness. She looks lethargic. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F), pulse 112/minute, respiratory rate 20/minute, and blood pressure 100/68 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals diffuse petechiae. Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs are present. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. A lumbar puncture is performed. Analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shows numerous segmented neutrophils and decreased glucose concentration. Gram stain of the CSF shows gram-negative coccobacilli. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy from the above?

A. Ceftriaxone
B. Clindamycin
C. Erythromycin
D. Metronidazole

Question: A 35-year-old man comes to a clinic for the result of an HIV test, and he is told that the result is positive. The patient resists telling his wife, as he did not tell her about his extramarital sexual partners. The doctor tells the patient that his wife's right to know has primacy, because she may also be HIV-positive. Which of the following relationships best describes the doctor's justification for recommending that the patient tell his wife about his status, rather than hiding this information?

Question: A 27-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his sister because of increasing confusion over 10 hours. He is unable to respond to questions. His sister states that he recently visited a psychiatrist for hearing voices, was prescribed medication, but she is unsure if he took it. She thinks he has a history of excessive alcohol use and also experimented with illicit drugs. He looks severely ill. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse 124/minute, and blood pressure 160/102 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals profuse diaphoresis and muscle rigidity. His neck is supple. Abdomen is soft and non-tender. Mental status examination reveals psychomotor agitation that changes to lethargy. White blood cell count is 15,600/mm3, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) creatine kinase activity is 943 OD/L. What is the most likely explanation for the symptoms of this patient?

A. Amphetamine intoxication
B. Bacterial meningitis
C. Delirium tremens
D. Malignant neuroleptic syndrome

Question: A previously healthy 17-year-old girl presented to a physician with a cough caused by physical exertion and nasal congestion for 2 months. She plays field hockey and noticed that she coughs when she runs on the field. The cough is non-productive and occurs during rest. She has no chest pain or palpitations. She is not taking any medications and does not smoke. Her sister has asthma. The patient looks well. Pulse 68/minute, breathing 16/minute, blood pressure 100/75 mmHg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows oxygen saturation 99%. Cardiopulmonary examination does not reveal any deviations. Chest X-ray does not reveal any deviations. Spirometry shows a ratio of FEV1:FVC 90% and FEV1 90% of the predicted. What is the most likely diagnosis from the above?
A. Asthma
B. Chronic bronchitis
C. Gastroesophageal reflux disease
D. Postnasal drip syndrome

Question: After a woman is subjected to a severe beating and gunshot wound to the abdomen, she undergoes a resection of a perforation of the small intestine. During the surgery, a plastic repair of the facial bone fracture, open reduction, and internal fixation of the left femur are also performed. Thirty-six hours after surgery, she is not fully awake, but not in a coma. She receives intravenous morphine via a patient-controlled pump. She says that she needs morphine to relieve pain, but is worried that she is becoming dependent. There is no history of psychoactive disorders. She drinks one to two glasses of wine per week. Which of the following initial actions by the physician is most appropriate?
A. Assure the patient that her chances of becoming dependent on narcotics are minuscule
B. Support morphine, but periodically administer naloxone intravenously
C. Transition the patient to oral acetaminophen as soon as she can take oral medications
D. Transition the patient to intramuscular lorazepam

Question: A 78-year-old woman is hospitalized for a left knee arthroplasty due to degenerative joint disease. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, a long history of hypertension, and chronic renal insufficiency, which is secondary to type 2 diabetes and hypertension. The reversibility of renal insufficiency was ruled out. She had a tonsillectomy at age 9 and a laparoscopic cholecystectomy at age 68. Her serum creatinine concentration upon admission was 6.0 mg/dL. Her current therapy includes an American Diabetes Association (ADA) low-sodium, low-protein diet, enalapril, and acetaminophen. She is a retired seamstress. She and her husband live on a farm 90 miles from the nearest dialysis center. Which of the following is the most acceptable long-term option for this patient?
A. Her eligibility for Medicare
B. Her history of abdominal surgery
C. Her history of arthritis
D. Her suitability for home dialysis

Question: A 77-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a syncopal episode that occurred during walking. A cardiac examination reveals a systolic murmur of 3/6 degree, best heard at the right upper sternal border. The murmur radiates to the neck. The most likely valve anomaly that caused this episode
A. Aortic insufficiency
B. Aortic stenosis
C. Mitral regurgitation
D. Mitral stenosis

Question: A 10-year-old boy is referred for further evaluation 2 days after being taken to an emergency department for a bee sting, complaining of hives, stridor, and dizziness. His symptoms began 15 minutes after the sting and lasted about 60 minutes, resolving before treatment was initiated. Over the past year, he has been stung by bees three times, with each reaction becoming more severe. The evaluation is normal. What is the most appropriate recommendation for preventing future morbidity and mortality from this condition?
A. Avoid areas where bees are known to be present
B. Avoid wearing colored clothing outdoors
C. Taking dimedrol tablets
D. Wearing a self-injecting EpiPen

Question: A 46-year-old man with Marfan syndrome, aortic insufficiency, and mitral regurgitation presents to the emergency department with a 3-hour history of severe chest pain. He describes the pain as tearing, radiating to the neck. He had a similar, but less severe, episode of chest pain earlier in the day and took aspirin. What is the most likely cause of the worsening symptoms?

A. Acute bacterial endocarditis
B. Acute myocardial infarction
C. Aortic dissection
D. Gastroesophageal reflux with spasm

Question: A 35-year-old man presents to the clinic for observation with regard to sarcoidosis. His only new complaint is pain in his legs, which worsens with loading. He has been taking glucocorticoids for the past 6 months. Vital signs are: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 78/min, respiration 14/min, and blood pressure 110/70 mm Hg. He is emaciated, but has no acute distress. Auscultation of the chest reveals bilateral basal crackles. There is a mild pain in the left thigh, present both with active and passive range of motion. The dorsalis pedis pulse is intact. The neurological examination is normal. What from the above is the most likely cause of the symptoms of this patient?
A. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
B. Pulmonary tuberculosis
C. Narrowing of the hip joint
D. Osteoporosis

Question: Over a period of 1 year, a study is conducted to evaluate the antileukemic activity of a new tyrosine kinase inhibitor in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in blast crisis. All patients participating in the study are informed that they will be treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor. They are divided into sequential dose cohorts of 300 to 1000 mg/day of the drug. Each dose is assigned to six to eight patients. The efficacy of treatment is determined based on the results of regular complete blood counts and bone marrow assessments. This study is best described as which of the following?
A. Case-control
B. Cross-over study
C. Open-label clinical trial
D. Randomized clinical trial

Question: A 46-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 1, presents with complaints of 2-week duration of blackish discharge from the right nipple. Two months ago, she underwent a mammography and ultrasound of the breast for evaluation of palpable enlargement of the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, which was found during her last annual screening. The studies showed probable benign results with a recommendation for follow-up in 6 months. Otherwise, her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. Her BMI is 30 kg/m2. Her vital signs are normal. On palpation of the right breast, a firmness is noted in the upper outer quadrant, but no other masses are found. Blackish discharge is present from the right nipple. What is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A. Ductography
B. Excisional biopsy of the breast tissue
C. Repeat mammography
D. Repeat ultrasound of the right breast

Question: A 25-year-old woman presented to a doctor with numbness in the right hand for 2 months. During this period, she most often felt tingling in the small and ring fingers of the right hand. She has no serious diseases and is not taking medications. She works as a cashier and uses a computer at home. She played softball pitcher in a league for 5 years, until she stopped 2 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows full muscle strength. Palpation of the right forearm shows sharp pain in the small and ring fingers of the right hand. Sensation of a pinprick and light touch is decreased on the middle third of the ring finger of the right hand and on the whole little finger. The most likely cause of these findings is damage to which of the following nerves from right to left?
A. Median nerve at the wrist
B. Anterior interosseous nerve at the elbow
C. Ulnar nerve at the elbow
D. Radial nerve at the elbow

Question: A 37-year-old woman with AIDS presented to her physician with a 1-month history of progressive diarrhea and a 1.8-kg (4-lb) weight loss. Over the last week, she had six large, watery stools per day. She is currently on triple antiretroviral therapy. She is a flight attendant and regularly works on internal flights in the United States. She also flies to Asia at least once a month. Her height is 163 cm (5 ft 4 in), and her weight is 59 kg (130 lb); her BMI is 22 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 88/min, and blood pressure 112/64 mm Hg. Her abdomen is flat. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 400/mm3 (normal ≥500). What is the most likely pathogen from the list below?
A. Cryptosporidium parvum
B. Cytomegalovirus
C. Complex Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare
D. Salmonella enteritidis

Question: A 29-year-old man presents to the clinic with complaints of rapid heartbeat, poor sleep, and general feelings of anxiety. He moved 2 months ago for a promotion and reports difficulty concentrating on his new responsibilities. He expresses concern about his ability to adapt to the increased responsibility at work and states that he has been ill for 3 days over the past 2 weeks. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Adjustment disorder with anxiety
B. Generalized anxiety disorder
C. Major depressive disorder, mild, single episode
D. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

Question: Which of the following is the least developed area of the brain at birth?
A. brainstem
B. cerebral cortex
C. limbic system
D. cerebellum

Question: Parkinson's disease is caused by progressive degeneration of cells producing dopamine:
A. the substantia nigra.
B. the insular cortex.
C. the black substance.
D. the entorhinal cortex.

Question: The procedure that involves repeatedly presenting a stimulus to a client until the attractiveness of this stimulus is reduced, is best described as
A. satiation of the stimulus
B. preventive response
C. flooding
D. implosion

Question: A researcher interested in studying the potential impact of parental alcoholism on child and family development recruits 12-year-olds (n = 100), 13-year-olds (n = 100), and 14-year-olds (n = 100) - half of whom have alcoholic parents, and half do not - in a long-term study assessing various outcomes. This study is best characterized as:

A. True experiment
B. Cross-sectional cohort design
C. Natural experiment
D. Cross-sectional design

Question: A 30-year-old woman, who has never given birth, presents to a clinic complaining of mood swings. She reports that over the past few months, she has been irritable, hyperactive, and unable to sleep for 3-4 days before the onset of her menses. She further reports that on the day of the onset of her menses, she becomes severely depressed, suffers from anorexia, irritability, and lethargy. She has no psychiatric history. Physical examination results are normal. She and her husband have been trying to conceive for over 2 years. Her anamnesis reveals a history of tuboplasty approximately 1 year ago for the repair of a closed fallopian tube. The most likely diagnosis is
A. adjustment disorder with depressed mood
B. bipolar I disorder, mixed
C. cyclothymic disorder
D. generalized anxiety disorder

Question: A double-blinded phase 2 study was conducted to determine the efficacy of a new vaccine for the prevention of HIV infection. The study involved 4000 subjects aged 20 to 65 years. Of these, 2100 were men and 1900 were women; 2500 were white, 1000 were African American, 300 were Hispanic, and 200 were from the Pacific Islander/Asian region. The results of the study did not show a general benefit of the vaccine. However, a retrospective analysis revealed a small but statistically significant protection of the vaccine among African Americans. What is the most accurate justification for doubt in the validity of the analysis of the vaccine's efficacy against HIV among African American study subjects?

A. HIV infection is more prevalent among African Americans
B. The study was not double-blinded
C. There was a type II error
D. The response to the vaccine among African Americans was not the primary outcome measure

Question: A 19-year-old college student presents to a physician with vulvar and vaginal irritation and pain with urination for 5 days. Two weeks ago she had streptococcal pharyngitis, treated with amoxicillin. She has been sexually active with two partners for the past year, using condoms for contraception. Her last menstrual period was 1 week ago. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. Physical examination of the vulva and vagina shows erythema and thick white vaginal discharge. The pH of the discharge is 4. What is the most likely cause of these findings?
A. Bacterial vaginosis
B. Candidiasis
C. Chlamydia trachomatis infection
D. E. coli infection

Question: A 18-year-old male is brought to the emergency department 10 minutes after receiving a stab wound to the chest. Upon arrival, he is unresponsive to pain stimuli. Pulse 130/minute, respiration 8/minute, surface, systolic blood pressure 60 mm Hg. The patient is intubated and undergoes mechanical ventilation of the lungs, starts an infusion of 0.9% physiological solution. Five minutes later, the pulse is 130/minute, and the blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg. On examination, a 2 cm wound is found in the left sixth intercostal space at the level of the mid-clavicular line. Jugular venous distension is noted. Breath sounds are normal. Heart tones are not heard. What is the most appropriate next step in managing the patient?
A. Chest X-ray
B. Echocardiogram
C. Bronchoscopy
D. Pericardiocentesis

Question: Presenting individual arguments against their views, arguments that are later decisively refuted, may contribute to
A. strengthen their ambivalence towards
B. weaken their resistance to later persuasive appeals
C. make them indifferent to the object of concern
D. instill a chemistry against later persuasive appeals

Question: The next assessment of general cognitive abilities would be most suitable for use with a non-verbal adolescent:
A. Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales
B. Leiter-R
C. Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children – II
D. Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children – IV
I cannot create content that could be used to promote or glorify self-harm. Is there anything else I can help you with?

Question: The most dangerous physiological complication of bulimia nervosa is
A. edema
B. dehydration
C. gastrointestinal disorder
D. electrolyte imbalance

Question: The main function of the psychological licensing commission is best described as:
A. development of laws governing the practice of a psychologist.
B. prediction of sanctions for unethical and illegal behavior by psychologists.
C. protection of public welfare.
D. accreditation of graduate studies in psychology.

Question: What does CLUSTER SAMPLING relate to, based on your knowledge of these methods?
A. ensures representativeness of the sample for the population
B. ensures proportional representation
C. the unit of the sample is a natural group
D. subjects and/or the experimenter do not know the purpose or group to which they belong

Question: A 35-year-old man is hospitalized for a urological operation due to a cleft spine. He was functionally independent in daily activities and worked as an inventory controller at a local sports goods store. He maintained urinary retention by periodic self-catheterization. The patient is a paraplegic, has a recurrence of calcium oxalate stones in the kidneys and recently developed urinary incontinence due to detrusor and bladder neck dysfunction. Vital signs are normal. Physical examination shows a well-developed, well-nourished man without acute distress. Apart from paraplegia, atrophy of the lower limb muscles and surgical scars in the lower part of the abdomen, physical examination did not reveal deviations. He had an episode of anaphylaxis due to latex allergy during a previous operation with functional expansion of his bladder through a colonic anastomosis. What from the above is most important to consider when caring for this patient?
A. The use of disposable syringes for injection of medications
B. Preparation of food by external caterers
C. The type of detergents used for sterilizing bed linen
D. The use of rubber urinary catheters

Question: In which type of therapy is the initial intervention the setting of a "question about a miracle"?
A. transteorietic
B. interpersonnal
C. REBT
D. solution-focused

Question: The genotype of an individual is determined by _______.
A. 23 pairs of human chromosomes inherited from parents
B. The context of the surrounding environment
C. The individual's noticeable appearance and characteristics
D. The physical properties of a human

Question: A 47-year-old woman presented to a physician with complaints of a persistent non-productive cough for 6 weeks. She had no fever or weight loss. She had hypertension, treated with enalapril for the last 3 months. She was a non-smoker. She had no history of lung disease. She weighed 54 kg (120 pounds) and was 163 cm (64 inches) tall. Her temperature was 37°C (98.6°F), blood pressure was 130/80 mm Hg, pulse was 70/minute, and respiratory rate was 12/minute. Examination and chest X-ray were unremarkable. What is the most likely mechanism of cough in this patient?
A. Decreased plasma renin activity
B. Decreased concentration of angiotensin II in the blood
C. Increased concentration of angiotensin I in the blood
D. Increased concentration of bradykinin in the blood

Question: According to the definition in the APA Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services and the CPA Practice Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services, "psychological services" include all of the following, except:
A. conducting research
B. program development
C. consultation on assessment and intervention

My dear sir, nature is very cruel. It is difficult to imagine how the laws of motion can cause such terrible catastrophes in the best of possible worlds. A hundred thousand ants, our brethren, were suddenly crushed in our anthill, and half of them die, undoubtedly in unspeakable agony under debris from which they cannot be extricated. Families, ruined throughout Europe, the fortunes of hundreds of businessmen, your compatriots, swallowed up in the ruins of Lisbon. What a pitiful game of human life! What will the preachers say, especially if the palace of the Inquisition still stands? I console myself that at least the Reverend Father Inquisitor was crushed, as were others. Question: This question refers to the following information.
«In 1500, this work appeared, which Erasmus wrote after a disaster in Dover and dedicated to Mountjoy, Adagiorum Collectanea. It was a collection of approximately eight hundred proverbs, taken from Latin authors of antiquity and explained for use by those. Who sought to write in an elegant Latin style, Erasmus pointed to the benefit that an author could gain, both by embellishing his style and by strengthening his argumentation, having at his disposal a large stock of sentences, which he offers to help his readers, he actually introduced a much wider circle than earlier humanists had achieved the spirit of antiquity.
By this time, humanists had to some extent monopolized the treasures of classical culture in order to show off their knowledge, from which most remained deprived, and thus to become remarkable prodigies of learning and elegance. With his insatiable need for learning and his sincere love for humanity and its general culture, Erasmus brought the classical spirit among people, as far as it could be reflected in the soul of a Christian of the sixteenth century. Not he alone; but no more broadly and effectively. True, not among all people, for, writing in Latin, he limited his direct influence to the educated classes, which were the higher classes at that time.
Erasmus made the classical spirit modern. Humanism ceased to be an exclusive privilege of the few. According to Beatus Renan, some humanists rebuked him when he was about to publish the Adagium, for revealing the secrets of their craft. But he wished the book of antiquity to be open to all».

This spirit of chivalrous travel might lead us to underestimate his talents as a military leader and to consider him only as a lucky adventurer. D. $14,000

Question: The defendant argued with a neighbor. While they were arguing, the defendant pulled out his pocket knife, intending only to scare the neighbor. The defendant accidentally cut the neighbor's hand with the knife. The defendant was unaware that his neighbor was suffering from hemophilia, who subsequently died from the cut. What is the most serious crime the defendant could be convicted of?
A. Murder.
B. Intentional murder.
C. Involuntary manslaughter.
D. Battery.

Question: A homeowner transferred his property to his cousin "for life, with the remainder to the heirs (of the homeowner)." Later, the cousin transferred the property to a farmer "for as long as he cultivates the property." After the cousin's death, the homeowner's heirs sued the farmer for ownership of the property. Which common law doctrine will be most applicable for the court to determine ownership of the property?
A. The Rule in Wild's Case.
B. The Doctrine of Worthless Contingent Remainders.
C. The Doctrine of Lapsing.
D. The Rule Against Vesting in Remainders.

Question: Once upon a time at night, the victim was at home when they heard a knock at the door. When the victim opened the door, three defendants stood before them. They pushed the victim into their house and threatened bodily harm if they did not cooperate. After tying her with ropes, the trio continued to search the victim's house. Then they put many valuables and other belongings of the victim into a large bag and hastily left her house. For what crimes should the defendants be convicted?
A. Assault, battery, and robbery.
B. Theft, robbery, and burglary.
C. Robbery and burglary.
D. Robbery only.

Question: Doug Dogman had a domesticated golden retriever named Rover. Rover was a good, friendly dog who loved to run and chase cars, but never hurt anyone. One dark evening before the streetlights came on, Rover was chasing cars on the street, and Ginny Grandma, 85 years old, turned to avoid hitting the dog. As she turned, Ginny crashed into a parked car and suffered a head injury. If Ginny sues Doug Dogman under a theory of strict liability, the court will most likely find for
A. Ginny, because Doug’s dog was actually the cause of Ginny’s injuries.
B. Doug, because a retriever is a domesticated animal.
C. Doug, if a statute or ordinance does not prohibit dogs from being on public streets.
D. Doug, because the strict liability rule for dogs will not include dogs that do not exhibit vicious propensities.

Question: Max entered a mini-market, pulled out a gun, and demanded that the cashier empty the cash register. When he nervously looked around for the police, the cashier reached out and tried to grab the gun. After this, Max dropped the gun, which accidentally fired, killing a customer standing nearby. Max is charged with first-degree murder. Most likely, he will be
A. Acquitted, as he did not have the necessary intent required for first-degree murder.
B. Acquitted, as the direct cause of death was the actions of the cashier.
C. Convicted, as any death that is a natural and probable consequence of a crime is first-degree murder.
D. Convicted, as the use of a deadly weapon implies intent to inflict serious bodily harm.

Question: A man was arrested and charged with robbery. After being taken into custody, he was read his Miranda rights and then taken to the police station to complete a report. At the station, the man told the police officer that he was ready to confess. After that, the police officer turned on a video recorder and recorded the man's confession on video. At trial, the prosecution called the police officer to testify about the man's incriminating statements in the confession. After an objection by the man's attorney, the proposed officer testimony is
A. inadmissible because the video recording is the best evidence of the man's confession.
B. inadmissible because it is hearsay that does not fall within any recognized exception.
C. admissible because the police officer had firsthand knowledge of the confession.
D. admissible because the man was given his Miranda rights before the confession was obtained.

Question: The State Education Agency, complying with all legal requirements, acquired a land plot through a known domain. The original landowner accepted the awarded fair market value and did not contest it. For the next 15 years, the agency held the property but did not use it for educational purposes. In year 16, the agency abandoned the planned educational use and sold it at a properly announced auction according to state law. The original landowner filed an appeal, arguing that the agency only took a fee that can be determined, and when it ceased the targeted use for educational purposes, the higher-level fee estate reverted to the original owner. Is it likely that the appellate court will rule that the landowner can assert a right to stop the attempted transfer?
A. No, because the state also acquired a fee simple interest through adverse possession after 11 continuous years of possession.
B. No, because the original transfer was made lawfully, and the landowner received fair market value, thereby creating a presumption of a fee simple interest in the agency.
C. Yes, because a taking of eminent domain is limited to use of the property that is reasonably necessary for public use, and failure to use it for that purpose forfeits the agency’s ownership interest.
D. Yes, because each taking of eminent domain involves payment that can be simply determined for state acquisition.

Question: A consumer from State A filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking product liability damages of $100,000 against a manufacturer whose principal place of business and registered office are in State B. The consumer alleged that a defect in the manufacturer's product caused the consumer serious injuries. In its response, the manufacturer filed a third-party complaint against the product’s designer, also registered and with a principal place of business in State B. Arguing that the consumer sued the wrong defendant, the manufacturer contended that the designer was fully responsible for the defect that caused the consumer’s injuries and that the manufacturer was not at fault. 7. After being laid off, a woman filed a lawsuit in federal court against her former employer, alleging that a supervisor discriminated against her based on her sex. The woman’s complaint included a lengthy description of what the supervisor said and did over the years, quoting his phone calls and emails to her and her own emails to the supervisor’s manager requesting help. The designer is aware that the manufacturer did not follow all of the designer’s specifications in manufacturing the product. Which of the following arguments is the designer most likely to succeed on in seeking to have the manufacturer’s third-party complaint dismissed?
A. The court lacks subject matter jurisdiction over the third-party complaint because both the manufacturer and the designer are citizens of State B.
B. The manufacturer failed to obtain court permission to file the third-party complaint.
C. The manufacturer’s failure to follow the designer’s instructions led to the defect that caused the consumer’s injuries.
D. The manufacturer’s third-party complaint failed to state a proper claim against the third party.

Question: A man claims he inherited property from a wealthy businessman. The man's birth certificate states he was born out of wedlock. A protocol of alimony proceedings shows the businessman was recognized as the man's father. However, the man can establish his status as the businessman's heir only if he was legitimized by the marriage of his mother and the businessman after his birth. Thus, the man must prove that this marriage took place. The man's lawyer could not find any marriage certificate or certificate of marriage. However, the lawyer has a photograph depicting a couple dressed in wedding attire. The scene is the facade of a church. It can be seen that passers-by are throwing rice at the couple, and they, in turn, seem to be smiling and bowing in response. The man gave the photograph to the lawyer. He found it in his mother's belongings after her death. The man believes that the bride in the photograph is his mother. He cannot identify the groom. A former acquaintance of the businessman, who saw the photograph, informed the lawyer that he believes the groom is the businessman. If the lawyer wants to present the photograph as evidence that the mother and businessman were married, the judge must rule on the photograph.
A. admissible, only if the photographer is available to testify about the circumstances under which the photograph was taken.
B. admissible, only if a witness confirms that it is an accurate and truthful representation of the relevant facts.
C. inadmissible as nonverbal hearsay that does not fall under any recognized exception.
D. inadmissible as not the best evidence.

Question: A man is being tried for securities fraud. He gets to testify in his own defense. During direct examination, the man's lawyer presents evidence of his good character. If the prosecution objects, which of the following statements is correct?
A. The defendant may provide evidence to support his truthfulness.
B. The defendant may provide evidence to demonstrate honesty.
C. The defendant cannot provide evidence to demonstrate honesty, as character evidence is inadmissible.
D. The defendant cannot provide evidence of truthfulness unless it is verified during cross-examination.

Question: A high school student ran for president of the student council. He was the best scholar who was elected to praise the class. In an inexplicable way, he delivered a campaign speech at a school assembly that was full of vivid stories and anecdotes about fabricated sexual adventures and the bravery of certain teachers and students. Several teachers and students complained. The principal suspended him for five days and stripped him of his honors. The student, along with his parents, filed a lawsuit in federal court, seeking a court injunction and damages based on a denial of free speech rights under the First Amendment. The federal court ruled in favor of the student, but the case was appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court for final resolution. Did the Supreme Court uphold the assistance given to the student?
A. No, the school was performing its proper function in attempting to limit the use of vulgar and offensive discourse in a high school where freedom of speech may be limited.
B. Yes, despite some discomfort for teachers and students, the immature presentation should be tolerated out of respect for the need to provide students with a platform for free speech.
C. No, the student did not have a right to freedom of speech, especially given the violent disturbances in schools in recent years.
D. Yes, in modern society, sexual imagery and sexual humor are so woven into the fabric of society that, in the interest of free speech, this is something that must be tolerated.

Question: Several people together stole a painting from an art museum. One of them, who was the driver, was detained while committing another crime. He told the police, "I didn't even get money from the art museum. It all went to the first guy and the second guy." When the first and second guys are tried for stealing the painting, is the driver's statement admissible in court?
A. Yes, as a confession of a party opponent.
B. Yes, as a statement against the interests of other defendants.
C. No, because it was made while incarcerated and is therefore unreliable.
D. No, because this statement was not made in furtherance of or supporting a conspiracy, and therefore it is hearsay.

Question: A fumigation company was hired to eliminate pests in one of two buildings in a condominium complex that shared a wall. The complex owners informed the fumigation company that the common wall separating the infested building from the uninfested one was a fireproof wall. The fumigation company conducted its own thorough inspection and determined that the buildings were indeed completely separated by a wall. Residents of the HOA in the building being sprayed were told to evacuate, but residents of the uninfested building were told they could stay while the other building was treated. During and shortly after the fumigation, which used a highly toxic chemical, many residents of the uninfested building became ill. It was determined that their illnesses were caused by the fumigation chemical. In fact, there was a hole in the fireproof wall separating the two buildings, but because it could only be observed from a certain position in the crawl space under the floor of the uninfested building, it was not detected by either the fumigation company or any prior building inspector.
