D. The testimony is admissible even if it is hearsay, the broker is available for cross-examination.

Question: A 27-year-old man was admitted to the hospital 45 minutes after a traffic accident. Physical examination shows a sluggish response to stimuli. Neurological examination shows no other abnormalities. A skull X-ray shows a linear fracture of the base of the skull without depression. Two weeks later, the patient develops polyuria and polydipsia. Laboratory tests show a concentration of glucose in the serum within normal limits, increased serum osmolality, and decreased urine osmolality. After the administration of desmopressin, the osmolality of the urine increases. The favorable effect of this drug is most likely due to the activation of which of the following?
A. Adenylate cyclase
B. Ca2+ channels
C. Janus kinase
D. Serine kinase

Question: A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department because he had been feeling nauseated and dizzy for the last hour. His history is significant for varices of the esophagus due to alcoholic cirrhosis of the liver and ascites, which are being treated with spironolactone. He drinks eight to ten alcoholic drinks daily. While you are gathering additional history, the patient vomits a large amount of bright red blood and is difficult to arouse. Vital signs are: temperature 36.0°C (96.8°F), pulse 110/min, respirations 12/min, and blood pressure 90/50 mm Hg. After initiating intravenous fluid resuscitation, which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
A. Arrange for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunting
B. Start intravenous vasopressin therapy
C. Perform endotracheal intubation
D. Perform upper endoscopy

Question: A healthy 2-year-old girl was brought to the office for a routine check-up. The child was weaned from the breast at the age of 6 months and started walking at the age of 10 months. Upon medical examination, she has a slight bowing of the legs (10th degree genu varum). Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation for management at this moment?
A. Increased intake of vitamin D
B. Special exercise program
C. Surgical correction
D. No treatment is needed at this moment

Question: In a 68-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer that has recurred twice in the last 5 years. She has undergone a course of radiation and chemotherapy for metastatic bone cancer. Today she comes to the office to ask for help with back pain in the middle thoracic region, so that she can use fewer painkillers. The most acceptable osteopathic manipulative technique for treating the spine of this patient is
A. high velocity, low amplitude
B. indirect myofascial release
C. isotonic exercise
D. medium velocity, medium amplitude

Question: A 44-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a lump in her neck, which she noticed 1 week ago. She denies any sensitivity, fever, weight loss, or fatigue. Physical examination reveals a freely mobile 2 cm lesion in the lower left portion of the thyroid gland. In addition to thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine levels, the most appropriate initial diagnostic method for this lesion is
A. thyroid nuclear scan
B. iodine-131 scan
C. fine-needle aspiration
D. thyroid ultrasound

Question: A 36-year-old female manager of an advertising department is sent to the office to assess her fasting serum total cholesterol level at 249 mg/dl. In her family, there was early ischemic heart disease (IHD), and her father suddenly died at the age of 46 from a myocardial infarction. She tells you that she has never experienced chest pain. Currently, she is not sexually active and has no children. She claims that due to her stressful lifestyle, she cannot eat normally or follow a special diet, and she usually eats fast food. She exercises two to three times a week for about 20 minutes on a treadmill. Over the past 20 years, she has smoked one pack of cigarettes a day. Her only medication is acetaminophen for tension headaches. Her height is 165 cm (5 feet 5 inches) and her weight is 76 kg (167 pounds); her BMI is 28 kg/m2. Vital signs today are normal. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities except for mild obesity. Which of the following is the most important step in the prevention of IHD in this patient?
A. A stress reduction program based on biofeedback
B. A more rigorous and consistent exercise program
C. A smoking cessation program
D. A strict low-calorie diet

Question: A 27-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 12 weeks of pregnancy, comes to the doctor for a prenatal check-up. She feels well. Her pregnancy and delivery of her first child were uncomplicated. Medications include folic acid and multivitamins. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure 108/60 mm Hg. Examination of the pelvis shows that the size of the uterus corresponds to the 12-week gestational age. A urine strip shows leukocyte esterase; urine analysis shows leukocytes and occasional gram-negative rods. Which of the following is the most acceptable next step in management?
A. Recommend drinking 8 ounces of cranberry juice daily
B. Oral therapy with amoxicillin
C. Oral therapy with metronidazole
D. Therapy with cefazolin intravenously

Question: A 27-year-old woman presents to her doctor with complaints of chronic diarrhea for 3 years and periodic colicky pains in the lower abdomen. The pain usually decreases during defecation and does not occur at night nor does it interfere with sleep. She states that she is frustrated with her symptoms and has stopped traveling due to the frequent, urgent need for the toilet. She has no serious illnesses and does not take medications. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 70/bpm, respiration 14/bpm, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg. The lower abdomen is slightly tender on palpation; there is no rebound tenderness or guarding. The rest of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory test results are within reference ranges. Stool test for occult blood is negative. Anti-gliadin antibodies are absent. Which of the following is the most acceptable pharmacotherapy?
A. Nefazodone
B. Nortriptyline
C. Phenelzine
D. Sertraline

Question: A 40-year-old man presented to the clinic with symptoms of odynophagia and gastroesophageal reflux. He also mentions that he had vomiting last week. His past medical history reveals HIV, and his last CD4 level was 30 cells/µL. The result of the tilt test and hemoglobin level are normal. On rectal examination, brown-colored stool is found, which is positive for occult blood. What is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this patient?
A. prescription for a proton pump inhibitor and a prokinetic
B. prescription for an H2-blocker trial for 6 weeks
C. prescription for clotrimazole lozenges
D. referral for upper endoscopy with biopsy

Question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the office for a routine check-up. She was diagnosed with Turner syndrome in childhood during an examination for coarctation of the aorta. During today's visit, her mother reports that the girl has been talking about babies. You have been the patient's doctor for the past 6 years and know that she is in the pre-pubertal stage. The most appropriate advice to give the patient is that if she wants to have a family, she will need to do which of the following?
A. Adopt
B. Have an amniocentesis if she becomes pregnant
C. Have surgery
D. Get genetic counseling

Question: A 37-year-old man with type 1 diabetes is hospitalized due to poor glucose control over the last 2 months. Despite poor control, he demands to be discharged. He reports having fatigue, irritability, and a sense of hopelessness for the past 3 months. He admits to not adhering to his diabetic regimen, adding, "Sometimes I forget." He avoids his family and friends because he is not in the mood to see them, but he acknowledges that he is lonely. He has not gotten out of bed for 2 days, prompting his wife to call an ambulance and hospitalize him. Prior to hospital admission, his only medication was insulin, although he often missed doses. He does not use alcohol. His height is 168 cm (5 feet 6 inches) and weight is 100 kg (220 pounds); his BMI is 36 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 68/bpm, respirations 18/bpm, blood pressure 150/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he is fatigued, affect is restricted. There is no evidence of suicidal thoughts. Cognition is intact. His fasting serum glucose concentration is 120 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Follow the patient's wishes and discuss options for home care
B. Follow the patient's wishes provided he consents to care
C. Order neuropsychological testing
D. Demand a court order for the appointment of a legal guardian

Question: In 1993, a farmer had a good title to a farm in absolute form. In 1994, the farmer transferred to his son for the sum of $1000 a document signed by the farmer in which the son and his heirs were named as the subject of the right and appeared genuine. The son neglected to record the deed. In 1998, an investor, who knew of the existence of the ownership agreement from the farmer to the son, found the farmer and asked to buy for $10,000 the ownership deed to the farm from the farmer to the investor and his heirs. The farmer made such a deed, and the investor promptly had it recorded. The investor's intent was to acquire color of title and obtain ownership of the farm through adverse possession. In 1998, the investor erected a fence around the farm. In 1999, the son delivered his deed to the farm to a rancher and for $15,000, paid by the rancher, signed and transferred the deed to the farm in favor of the rancher and his heirs. Upon receiving the document, the rancher made no effort to check the title, inspect the property, or record the document. In 2003, a teacher paid the investor $20,000, and the investor transferred to the teacher the ownership deed to the farm in favor of the teacher and his heirs. The teacher inspected the property, checked the title, and knew of the prior instrument from the farmer to the son. Although the teacher did not live on the property, he regularly visited the farm twice a week. The teacher recorded his deed. In 2007, for $25,000 paid by a professor, the rancher signed and provided the farm deed in which the professor and his heirs were named as grantees. Before the professor paid the rancher and took the document, the professor visited the farm and inspected the fence. However, the teacher was not present when the professor visited the property, and nothing indicated who was "in use" of it. In any event, the professor did not attempt to search the name before making the purchase. The professor then recorded the deed. Note. In this jurisdiction, the "grantor-grantee" indices are used and there is no deed index. The jurisdiction's recording statute provides: "Any transfer of real property that is not recorded is void as to the subsequent good faith purchaser for valuable consideration, the transfer of which was initially to be duly recorded." In 2008, in a suit over the ownership of the farm, which of the following parties will have priority of ownership to the farm?
A. Professor.
B. Investor.
C. Teacher.
D. Rancher.

Question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the doctor with a 2-day history of fever and painful swelling of the left ankle. Since childhood, he has suffered from recurrent cervical lymphadenitis and pneumonia. Two years ago, a golden staphylococcus was grown from an abscess in the cervical region. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). Examination reveals a tender, erythematous, swollen left ankle; pinpoint tenderness over the medial malleolus. Bone scan shows increased uptake in the left lower metaphysis of the tibia. Culture of bone aspirate grows Serratia marcescens. The nitroblue tetrazolium test shows no color change. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism for these findings?
A. Arrested development of B-lymphocyte maturation
B. Dysmorphogenesis of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches
C. Impaired chemotaxis
D. Impairment of phagocytic oxidative metabolism

Question: A 26-year-old woman with HIV infection presented to the clinic due to pain and redness of the left shin for 4 days. She states that the symptoms appeared after she tripped over a tree branch in her yard and scraped her left leg. Current medications include antiretroviral therapy and ibuprofen as needed. Vital signs: temperature 38.3 °C (100.9 °F), pulse 86/bpm, respirations 14/bpm, and blood pressure 138/70 mm Hg. On the anterior surface of the left lower extremity, there is a 5 × 8 cm area that is swollen, erythematous, and tender. She previously had a rash after taking erythromycin, and she had an anaphylactic reaction to penicillin. Which of the following antibiotic therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
A. Amoxicillin
B. Ciprofloxacin
C. Clarithromycin
D. Clindamycin

Question: A 67-year-old woman presents to her doctor with easy bruising for 4 months. She has a history of lung cancer, which underwent radiation therapy 6 months ago. She has a 2-year history of hypertension, treated with a thiazide diuretic and an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. Examination, including neurological examination, reveals no abnormalities except for numerous ecchymoses. Hemoglobin concentration is 13 g/dl, leukocytes 5000/mm3, platelets 35000/mm3. Serum antiplatelet antibody analysis is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?
A. CT scan of the abdomen
B. CT scan of the chest
C. Bronchoscopy
D. Bone marrow aspiration

Question: A previously healthy 19-year-old college student presents to the student health service 24 hours after the onset of headache, neck stiffness, and light sensitivity. She does not recall any contact with ill individuals. At age 7, she had chickenpox. Her last examination 1 year ago included a PPD skin test and was unremarkable. She takes daily multivitamins and a herbal weight-loss supplement. As a child, she received all appropriate vaccinations but has not had any since. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. There is no significant family history of illness. She appears lethargic. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F), pulse 112/min, respirations 20/min, blood pressure 100/68 mm Hg. On examination, there are diffuse petechiae. Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs are present. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. A lumbar puncture is performed. Analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shows numerous segmented neutrophils and a decreased glucose concentration. Gram staining of the CSF reveals gram-negative cocci. Which of the following is the most acceptable pharmacotherapy?
A. Ceftriaxone
B. Clindamycin
C. Erythromycin
D. Metronidazole

Question: A previously healthy 17-year-old girl presented to her doctor with a complaint of cough induced by physical exertion and nasal congestion for 2 months. She plays field hockey and noticed that she coughs when running on the field. The cough is non-productive and resolves during rest. She has had no chest pain or palpitations. She is not on any medications and does not smoke. Her sister has asthma. The patient appears well. Pulse is 68/min, respirations 16/min, blood pressure 100/75 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows oxygen saturation of 99%. Cardiopulmonary examination reveals no abnormalities. Chest x-ray reveals no abnormalities. Spirometry shows a FEV1:FVC ratio of 90% and FEV1 90% of predicted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Asthma
B. Chronic bronchitis
C. Gastroesophageal reflux disease
D. Postnasal drip syndrome

Question: A 27-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his sister due to increasing confusion over 10 hours. He is unable to answer questions. His sister states that he recently visited a psychiatrist for the first time due to hearing voices; he was prescribed medication, but she is unsure what it is. She mentions that he has a history of excessive alcohol use and thinks he has also experimented with illicit drugs. He appears acutely ill. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse 124/bpm, blood pressure 160/102 mm Hg. On examination, there is profuse diaphoresis and muscle rigidity. His neck is stiff. The abdomen is soft, non-tender. On mental status examination, there is psychomotor agitation alternating with lethargy. The white blood cell count is 15,600/mm3, serum creatine kinase activity 943 U/L. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's symptoms?
A. Amphetamine intoxication
B. Bacterial meningitis
C. Delirium tremens
D. Malignant neuroleptic syndrome

Question: The Law School published advertisements in various law journals regarding the candidacy of a professor of legal ethics and jurisprudence. Although several lawyers were vying for the position, one of the candidates submitted particularly impressive credentials. The dean of the law school immediately wrote to the applicant to offer him the position. In the letter, the dean proposed to employ the applicant for the upcoming academic year, which began on August 15, with a salary of $75,000. The letter also listed the terms of employment, one of which stated that professors are entitled to five paid sick days throughout the year. The dean added a detailed employment contract for the applicant to sign, which contained all these terms. After receiving this letter, the applicant responded by mail, demanding a salary of $85,000 and sick leave of 10 days. Upon receiving the applicant's letter, the dean called the applicant and informed him that the law school adheres to the guidelines of the American Bar Association regarding salaries and sick days for its faculty. The applicant agreed on the issue of salary but insisted on extending his sick leave to 10 days. The dean responded, "Let's not let a minor issue stand in the way of your coming to teach at our law school. If you need more than 5 sick days, I promise that this issue will be resolved in your favor." The applicant told the dean that he would sign the contract and send it back to the dean, which he did immediately. The applicant began teaching at the law school on August 15. Three months later, the applicant was sick for five days with laryngitis. The applicant did not miss any teaching days until Monday, March 8, when he fell ill with food poisoning. This illness kept him home for another five sick days. The applicant returned to work on March 15. When the applicant received his paycheck at the end of the week, his check did not include payment for the previous week (March 8-12). The check was accompanied by a memo stating: "Pay for the period from Monday, March 1, to Friday, March 19, with a proportional deduction to reflect five teaching days missed during the specified period." When the applicant received his check, he immediately confronted the dean and demanded full payment for the week of March 8-12. The dean responded, "I'm very sorry, but I absolutely can't do anything about it." The applicant sued the law school for breach of contract. The applicant proposes to present evidence that during the telephone conversation with the dean of the school, the dean promised, if necessary, to provide him with additional sick days. The most accurate statement regarding the dean's oral promise would be:
A. Parol evidence is admissible to show that the parties agreed to their written contract only as a partial integration of their entire contract.
B. Evidence of partial integration is admissible to prove a subsequent oral agreement that modifies or contradicts the terms of a prior written contract.
C. Admissible evidence that the written contract is unenforceable due to undue influence or fraud.
D. Testimony is inadmissible to prove contemporaneous oral agreements that modify or contradict the terms of the written contract.

Question: A 78-year-old woman is hospitalized for a left knee joint replacement due to degenerative joint disease. She has type 2 diabetes, a long history of hypertension, and chronic kidney disease secondary to both diabetes and hypertension. Reversible causes of kidney disease have been excluded. She underwent a tonsillectomy at age 9 and a laparoscopic cholecystectomy at age 68. Her serum creatinine concentration on admission was 6.0 mg/dL. Her current therapy includes an American Diabetes Association (ADA) low-sodium and low-protein diet, enalapril, and acetaminophen. She is a retired seamstress. She and her husband live on a farm 90 miles from the nearest dialysis facility. In considering long-term treatment options for this patient, which of the following factors is most appropriate to consider?
A. Her eligibility for Medicare
B. Her history of abdominal surgery
C. Her history of arthritis
D. Her suitability for home dialysis

Question: A 35-year-old man visits the office for the result of his HIV test, and he is told that the result is positive. The patient resists disclosure to his wife, as he has not told her about his extramarital sexual partners. The doctor informs the patient that his wife's right to know is of paramount importance, as she may also be HIV-positive. Which of the following relationships best describes the doctor's reasoning for recommending that the patient disclose his status to his wife rather than conceal this information?
A. autonomy outweighs beneficence
B. autonomy outweighs justice
C. beneficence outweighs autonomy
D. non-maleficence outweighs autonomy

Question: A 10-year-old boy is brought for evaluation 2 days after presenting to the emergency department for hives, stridor, and dizziness. His symptoms began 15 minutes after being stung by a bee and lasted approximately 60 minutes; they resolved before he was treated. Over the past year, he has been stung by bees three times, and each reaction has been more severe. Evaluation shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most acceptable recommendation to prevent morbidity and mortality in the future from this condition?
A. Avoid places known to have bees
B. Avoid wearing colorful clothing outside
C. Carrying tablets of dimedrol
D. Carrying self-injectable epinephrine

Question: 77-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a syncopal episode that occurred during walking. Heart examination reveals a systolic murmur of 3/6 grade, which is best heard at the right upper sternal border. Radiation of the murmur to the neck is observed. The valve anomaly that most likely caused this episode is
A. aortic insufficiency
B. aortic stenosis
C. mitral regurgitation
D. mitral stenosis

Question: After severe beating and a gunshot wound to the abdomen, a 42-year-old woman undergoes a resection of a perforation in the small intestine. During the surgery, plastic reconstruction of facial bone fractures, open reduction, and internal fixation of the left femur are also performed. Thirty-six hours post-operation, she is not sleeping but not in full consciousness. She is receiving intravenous morphine through a patient-controlled pump. She says she needs morphine to relieve the pain but is worried about becoming dependent. She has no history of psychoactive disorders. She drinks one or two glasses of wine per week. Which of the following initial actions by the physician is most appropriate?
A. Assure the patient that her chances of becoming addicted to drugs are minuscule
B. Maintain morphine but periodically administer naloxone intravenously
C. Switch the patient to oral acetaminophen as soon as she can take medications orally
D. Switch the patient to intramuscular lorazepam

Question: A 25-year-old woman presented to her doctor with a 2-month history of numbness in her right hand. During this period, she most often felt tingling in her ring and little finger of the right hand. She has no serious illnesses and does not take medications. She works as a cashier and uses a computer at home. She played pitcher in a softball league for 5 years until she stopped 2 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows full muscle strength. Palpation of the right elbow causes sharp pain in the ring and little finger of the right hand. Pinprick and light touch sensation are decreased on the medial half of the right ring finger and the entire little finger. The most likely cause of these findings is entrapment of which of the following on the right?
A. Median nerve at the wrist
B. Radial nerve at the forearm
C. Ulnar nerve at the elbow joint
D. Musculocutaneous nerve at the forearm

Question: A 46-year-old man with Marfan syndrome, aortic insufficiency, and mitral regurgitation presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain over the past 3 hours. He describes the pain as tearing and radiating to the neck. A week prior, he experienced similar but less severe chest pain and self-medicated with aspirin. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his symptom worsening?
A. Acute bacterial endocarditis
B. Acute myocardial infarction
C. Aortic dissection
D. Gastroesophageal reflux with spasm

Question: During a 1-year study to assess the anti-leukemic activity of a new tyrosine kinase inhibitor in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in blast crisis, all participating patients are informed that they will be treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor. They are assigned to sequential cohorts of doses ranging from 300 to 1000 mg/day of the drug. Each dose is administered to six to eight patients. The effectiveness of the treatment is determined based on the results of a complete blood count and bone marrow evaluation, which are regularly performed during the study. This study is best described as which of the following?
A. Case-control
B. Cross-over study
C. Open-label clinical trial
D. Randomized clinical trial

Question: A 35-year-old man presents to the clinic for observation due to sarcoidosis. His only new complaint is pain in his legs, which worsens with exertion. He has been taking glucocorticoids for the last 6 months. Vital signs now are: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 78/bpm, respiration 14/bpm, and blood pressure 110/70 mmHg. The patient is thin, and does not feel acute distress. On auscultation of the chest, scattered bilateral basal crackles are heard. There is mild pain in the left thigh, present in both active and passive range of motion. Dorsalis pedis pulse is intact. Neurological exam is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
A. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
B. Herniated nucleus pulposus
C. Hip joint stenosis
D. Osteoporosis

Question: A 46-year-old patient, gravida 1, para 1, presented with a 2-week history of black-colored discharge from the right nipple, lasting for 2 weeks. The patient underwent mammography and ultrasound of the breasts 2 months ago to evaluate the increased glandular tissue palpable in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, which was found during the last annual check-up. The studies showed likely benign results with a recommended follow-up in 6 months. Otherwise, the medical history is unremarkable, and the patient is not taking any medications. BMI is 30 kg/m2. Vital signs are normal. On palpation of the right breast, a mass is noted in the upper outer quadrant, but no other masses are present. There is minimal black-colored discharge from the right nipple. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the diagnosis?
A. Ductography
B. Excisional biopsy of the glandular tissue
C. Repeat mammography
D. Repeat ultrasound of the right breast

Question: A 37-year-old woman with AIDS came to the doctor with a 1-month history of progressive diarrhea and a weight loss of 1.8 kg (4 pounds). Over the past week, she has had six large, watery bowel movements each day. She is currently receiving triple antiretroviral therapy. She is employed as a flight attendant and regularly works on domestic flights within the US. She also travels to Asia at least once a month. Her height is 163 cm (5 feet 4 inches) and her weight is 59 kg (130 pounds); her BMI is 22 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/bpm, and blood pressure is 112/64 mm Hg. Her abdomen is scaphoid. The rest of the examination shows no abnormalities. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 400/mm3 (normal ≥500). Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?
A. Cryptosporidium parvum
B. Cytomegalovirus
C. Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex
D. Salmonella enteritidis

Question: _______ is the least developed part of the brain at birth.
A. brainstem
B. cerebral cortex
C. limbic system
D. cerebellum

Question: A multicenter phase 2 study was conducted to determine the efficacy of a new vaccine for the prevention of HIV infection. The study included 4000 subjects aged 20 to 65 years. Of these, 2100 were men and 1900 were women; 2500 were white, 1000 were African American, 300 were Latino, and 200 were Asian/Pacific Islander residents. The trial results showed no overall benefit from the vaccine. However, a retrospective analysis revealed a small but statistically significant protection from the vaccine among African Americans. Which of the following is the most accurate rationale for doubting the validity of the analysis of vaccine efficacy against HIV among African American study subjects?
A. HIV infection is more prevalent among African Americans
B. The study was not blinded
C. A type II error occurred
D. Response to the vaccine among African Americans was not a primary endpoint

Question: A 29-year-old man presented to the office with complaints of a racing heartbeat, poor sleep, and a general feeling of unease. He moved 2 months ago to get a promotion and found that he cannot focus on his new responsibilities. He is worried about his ability to adapt to the increased responsibility at work and claims that over the last 2 weeks he has been sick 3 days. Most likely diagnosis
A. adjustment disorder with anxious mood
B. generalized anxiety disorder
C. major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
D. obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

Question: Parkinson's disease is caused by the progressive degeneration of cells that produce dopamine:
A. suprachiasmatic nucleus.
B. insular cortex.
C. substantia nigra.
D. entorhinal cortex.

Question: The procedure that involves repeatedly presenting a stimulus to a client until the attractiveness of this stimulus decreases is best described as
A. stimulus satiation
B. response prevention
C. flooding
D. implosion

Question: The most dangerous physiological complication of nervous bulimia is
A. swelling
B. dehydration
C. gastrointestinal disorder
D. electrolyte imbalance

Question: A 30-year-old woman who has never given birth visited the office complaining of mood changes. She says that over the past few months, she has been anxious, hyperactive, and unable to sleep for 3-4 days before the start of menstruation. Further, she reports that on the day menstruation begins, she becomes acutely depressed, suffers from anorexia, irritability, and lethargy. She has no psychiatric history. The results of the physical examination are normal. She and her husband have been trying to conceive for more than 2 years. The history indicates tuboplasty approximately a year ago to correct a closed fallopian tube. The most likely diagnosis is
A. adjustment disorder with depressed mood
B. bipolar I disorder, mixed
C. cyclothymic personality
D. generalized anxiety disorder

Question: A researcher interested in studying the potential impact of parental alcoholism on child development and family dynamics recruits 12-year-olds (n = 100), 13-year-olds (n = 100), and 14-year-olds (n = 100) — half of whom have alcoholic parents, and half who do not — into a long-term, multi-year study with the assessment of various outcomes. This study is best characterized as:
A. True experiment
B. Cross-sequential cohort design
C. Natural experiment
D. Cross-sectional cohort design

Question: Presenting individual arguments against their views, arguments that are then decisively refuted, can help
A. strengthen their ambivalent attitude
B. weaken their resistance to later persuasive appeals
C. make them indifferent to the object of attitude
D. instill a chemistry against later persuasive appeals

Question: An 18-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department 10 minutes after sustaining a stab wound to the chest. Upon arrival, he does not respond to painful stimuli. Pulse is 130/min, respiration is 8/min, shallow, systolic blood pressure is 60 mm Hg. The patient is intubated and mechanical ventilation of the lungs is initiated, infusion of 0.9% saline solution is started. After 5 minutes, the pulse is 130/min and the blood pressure is 70/40 mm Hg. On examination, a 2 cm wound is found in the left sixth intercostal space at the level of the midclavicular line. Jugular venous distension is noted. Breath sounds are normal. The trachea is in the midline. Heart sounds are not auscultated. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of the patient?
A. Chest X-ray
B. Echocardiography
C. Bronchoscopy
D. Pericardiocentesis

Question: A 35-year-old man with a spinal cord injury is hospitalized for a urological procedure. He was functionally independent in daily activities and works as an inventory controller in a local sports goods store. He maintained urinary continence through periodic self-catheterization. The patient is paraplegic, has a recurrence of calcium oxalate kidney stones, and has recently developed urinary incontinence due to detrusor and bladder neck dysfunction. Vital signs are normal. Physical examination reveals a well-developed, well-nourished man without acute distress. Apart from paraplegia, atrophy of the lower limb muscles, and surgical scars in the lower abdomen, the physical examination did not reveal any abnormalities. He had an episode of anaphylaxis due to a latex allergy during a previous surgery for functional augmentation of his bladder through an intestinal anastomosis. Which of the following is most important to consider in the care of this patient?
A. Administration of injectable medications with single-use syringes
B. Preparation of food by outside contractors
C. Type of detergents used for sterilizing bed linens
D. Use of rubber urethral catheters

Question: The following measurement of overall cognitive abilities would be most appropriate for use with a nonverbal adolescent:
A. Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales–5
B. Leiter-R
C. Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–II
D. Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children–IV

Question: The main function of the psychological licensing commission is best described as:
A. developing laws that govern the practice of psychology.
B. predicting sanctions for unethical and illegal behavior by psychologists.
C. protecting the public welfare.
D. accrediting psychology graduate programs.

Question: According to the definition in the APA General Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services and the CPA Practice Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services, "psychological services" include all of the following, except?
A. conducting scientific research
B. program development
C. consultation regarding assessment and intervention
D. supervision of psychological services

Question: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is most successfully applied in
A. Psychogenic amnesia
B. Catatonic schizophrenia
C. Manic depression
D. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

Question: Which type of therapy begins with the intervention of asking the "miracle question"?
A. transtheoretical
B. interpersonal
C. REBT
D. solution-focused

Question: An individual's genotype ___________.
A. A person inherits 23 pairs of chromosomes from their parents
B. The context of the surrounding environment
C. Noticeable external appearance and characteristics
D. Physical properties of a person

Question: A 19-year-old college student presents to her doctor with vaginal irritation and painful urination for 5 days. Two weeks ago, she had a streptococcal pharyngitis and was treated with amoxicillin. Over the past year, she has been sexually active with two partners and uses condoms for contraception. Her last menstrual period was 1 week ago. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), and her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg. Pelvic examination shows erythema of the vulva and vagina and thick white vaginal discharge. The pH level of the discharge is 4. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
A. Bacterial vaginosis
B. Candidiasis
C. Chlamydia trachomatis infection
D. E. coli infection

Question: The most accurate way to diagnose Alzheimer's disease is by using
A. exclusion of other etiologies through comprehensive psycho-diagnostic examination
B. computer tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging, which shows cerebral atrophy
C. brain biopsy
D. neuropsychological testing, which shows the expected profile of deficits and preserved functions

Question: Parametric tests are used when data is interval or ratio. When is a ONE-WAY ANOVA used?
A. used when there is 1 IV and means of more than 2 groups
B. used when there are 2 IV and means of more than 4 groups
C. used when there are 3 IV and means of more than 5 groups
D. used when there are 4 IV and means of more than 6 groups

Question: There are also certain ways to increase external validity. Based on your knowledge of these methods, what does CLUSTER SAMPLING refer to?
A. ensures representativeness of the sample for the population
B. ensures proportional representation
C. the unit of the sample is a natural group
D. subjects and/or the experimenter do not know the purpose or the group to which they belong

Question: A 47-year-old woman presented to her doctor with complaints of persistent non-productive cough for 6 weeks. She had no fever or weight loss. She has hypertension and has been treated with enalapril for the last 3 months. She does not smoke. There is no history of lung disease. She weighs 54 kg (120 lbs) and is 163 cm (64 inches) tall. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, pulse 70/min, and respirations 12/min. Examination and chest x-ray were unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism of cough in this patient?
A. Decreased plasma renin activity
B. Decreased serum concentration of angiotensin II
C. Increased serum concentration of angiotensin I
D. Increased serum concentration of bradykinin

Question: The effectiveness of a group's task (n) __________ is limited by the productivity of the least qualified or informed group member.
A. addition
B. compensatory
C. disjunctive
D. conjunctive

Question: A child uses a spoon in a similar way to how they once used a rattle. In Piaget's theoretical framework, this is an example of
A. accommodation
B. assimilation
C. response fixation
D. fixed action pattern

Question: Which of the following lists of professional interests is not related to Holland's theory of vocational interests?
A. Kuder Occupational Interest Survey
B. Strong Interest Inventory
C. Campbell Interest and Skill Survey
D. Self-Directed Search

Question: If a psychologist acts both as a fact witness for the plaintiff and as an expert witness for the court in a criminal proceeding, she acted:

Article 12: To permanently eliminate the possibility of violating the personal and property rights of the French, a jury system will be introduced in all criminal cases in all courts of the kingdom, as well as in civil cases for establishing facts.  
Article 17: All differences in punishments must be abolished; and crimes committed by citizens of different estates must be punished independently, according to the same forms of law and in the same manner. The Estates-General seeks to ensure that the consequences of an offense are limited to the individual and do not affect the relatives of the offender who are not guilty of any involvement.  
Article 21: No tax is lawful unless it is accepted by the representatives of the people and sanctioned by the king.

D. Monthly bank reconciliations typically include several large outstanding checks.

Question: What is the main difference between just-in-time (JIT) production approaches and traditional ones?
A. The JIT approach typically involves a large number of suppliers, while traditional approaches usually involve only a small number of suppliers.
B. The JIT approach requires centralized purchasing, while traditional approaches encourage purchasing decisions to be made by production employees.
C. The JIT approach uses a push system, while traditional approaches use a pull system.
D. The JIT approach operates with low inventory levels, while traditional approaches can operate with high inventory levels.

Question: Swift Co. has identified three operating segments that may require separate disclosure in Swift's general-purpose financial statements for the year ended December 31, Year 2. The information for Year 2 is provided below: Segment (in thousands) A B C Total reported revenue $ 42 $ 121 $ 14 $ 177 Reported profit (loss) $ 12 $ 65 $ (3) $ 74 Assets $ 470 $ 800 $ 80 $ 1350 Which of Swift's segments need to be disclosed separately in the financial statements for Year 2 as of December 31?  
A. Only A and B.  
B. Only A and C.  
C. Only B and C.  
D. A, B, and C.

Question: Decker, a 62-year-old unmarried man, sold his primary residence for a net amount of $500,000 after all selling expenses. Decker bought the house 15 years ago and occupied it until it was sold. At the time of sale, the value of the house was $200,000. Within six months, Decker purchased a new house for $600,000. What amount should Decker recognize from the sale of the residence?  
A. $0  
B. $50,000  
C. $175,000  
D. $300,000

Question: Vital Corp. is a C corporation that operates on a calendar year basis. Its reported income for year 2 before federal taxes was $500,000. This amount includes the following items: state franchise tax refund for year 1 $50,000, interest income from municipal bonds $7,500. What should be the amount of taxable income for Vital for year 2 according to Vital's M-1 schedule of Form 1120 U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return?
A. $500,000  
B. $492,500  
C. $450,000  
D. $442,500

Question: Which of the following events is most likely to indicate the existence of related party transactions?
A. Life insurance for key executives with the organization listed as the beneficiary.
B. Sale of real estate at a price significantly different from its appraised value.
C. Granting a loan with specified repayment terms.
D. Providing stock options to key executives at favorable prices.

Question: On January 1, the company enters into an operating lease agreement for office premises and gains control over the property to make improvements to the leased property. The company begins renovations on March 1, and the company's staff moves into the property on May 1. Monthly rent payments start on July 1. The recognition of expenses for the new office lease should begin in which of the following months?  
A. January.  
B. March  
C. May.  
D. July.

Question: Arrange the following pairs (risk, return) from least favorable to most favorable, assuming the perspective of a rational and risk-averse investor: (2,2), (2,3), and (4,2). Risk is measured in standard deviations, and return in percentages. HINT: imagine a scatter plot with standard deviation on the x-axis and return on the y-axis.  
A. (4,2),(2,2),(2,3)  
B. (2,2),(2,3),(4,2)  
C. (2,2),(4,2),(2,3)  
D. (2,3),(2,2),(4,2)

Question: After reviewing the organization's policy on end-user computing (EUC), the internal auditor checks the actuarial function and notices that some minimum control requirements are missing. What of the following is a risk of using potentially incorrect files developed by the end user?  
A. Management relies on the files just as much as on files created from mainframes.  
B. Management receives limited information for decision-making due to the lack of flexibility in EUC files.  
C. Management is unable to respond quickly to competitive pressure.  
D. Management continues to incur additional costs as more hours are needed to perform tasks using EUC.

Question: The non-governmental non-profit organization Zokro uses the indirect method for preparing the cash flow statement. When determining its net cash provided (used) by operating activities, Sokro should add which of the following to the change in net assets?  
A. Purchase of equipment.  
B. Payment of long-term debt.  
C. Depreciation.  
D. Decrease in accounts payable.

Question: On December 31, Year 1, the spouse passed away. The couple had no dependents. What should be the filing status of the surviving spouse for Year 2?
A. Single.
B. Married filing jointly.
C. Qualifying widow (widower).
D. Head of household.

Question: The CPA prepared a tax return that included a tax shelter transaction, which was disclosed in the return. In which of the following situations will no penalty be applied to the individuals who prepared the tax return?  
A. There were significant authorities for this position.  
B. It is reasonable to believe that this position is more likely than not to be upheld.  
C. There was a sufficient likelihood of success for the position.  
D. There was a sufficient basis for such a position.

Question: The first reporting period of the company under IFRS relates to the year ended December 31, Year 2. During the preparation of the statement of financial position for Year 2, management discovered an error that resulted in the accrual of losses of $90,000 not being recorded. $40,000 of the accrued losses related to an event in Year 1, and $50,000 related to an event in Year 2. What amount of accrued losses should the company report in the IFRS statement of financial position for Year 1 as of December 31?  
A. $0  
B. $40,000  
C. $50,000  
D. $90,000

Question: The tax basis of Gulde in Chyme Partnership was $26,000 at the time Gulde received a liquidation distribution of $12,000 in cash and land with an adjusted basis to Chyme of $10,000 and a fair market value of $30,000. Chyme had no unrealized receivables, valued inventory, or property contributed by its partners. What was the amount of land for Gulde?  
A. $0  
B. $10,000  
C. $14,000  
D. $30,000

Question: If the purpose of the audit of details is to detect overstatement of sales volume, the auditor should trace transactions from  
A. Sales journal to shipping documents.  
B. Shipping documents to cash receipts journal.  
C. Cash receipt journals to customer orders.  
D. Customer orders to sales journal.

Question: Ace Co. issued 1000 shares of its common stock with a par value of $10 at $15 per share in cash. How should this transaction be reflected in Ace's cash flow statement for the year of issuance?  
A. $15000 cash inflow from financing activities.  
B. $10000 cash inflow from financing activities and a $5000 adjustment for cash flows from operating activities.  
C. $15000 cash flow from investing activities.  
D. $10000 cash flow from investing activities and a $5000 adjustment for cash flows from operating activities.

Question: During the audit of a company's financial statements for the year ending December 31 of year 1, the auditor notes that the company's sales significantly increased in December of year 1 with a corresponding decrease in January of year 2. In assessing the risk of fraud in financial reporting or misappropriation of assets, what should be the auditor's initial indications regarding potential fraud related to sales revenue?
A. There are broad signs of misappropriation of assets.
B. There are signs of embezzlement of the company's property.
C. There are signs of receipt embezzlement.
D. There are many signs of fraud in financial reporting.

Question: Which of the following is considered part of the necessary additional information for the general purpose external financial reporting of a local government authority?  
A. Financial report of the fund.  
B. Combined report on a small fund.  
C. Notes to the financial statements.  
D. Management discussion and analysis.

Question: What is the deadline for filing the federal estate tax return (Form 706) for a taxpayer who died on May 15, 2, assuming that no extension request was filed?  
A. September 15, 2  
B. December 31, 2  
C. January 31, 3  
D. February 15, 3

Question: Vale is a 50% partner in Ball Partnership. The tax basis of Vale's interest in Ball on January 2 of Year 1 was $60,000. Ball had no unrealized receivables, inventory, or property contributed by its partners. On December 31 of Year 1, Ball distributed non-liquidating cash of $10,000 to each partner. The tax return of Ball Partnership reports the following items for Year 1: Tax-exempt interest income $80,000 Dividend income $12,000 What total amount of gross income from Ball should be included in Vale's adjusted gross income for Year 1?
A. $6,000  
B. $16,000  
C. $36,000  
D. $46,000

Question: Cobb Inc.'s inventory on May 1 consisted of 200 units with a total value of $1,250. Cobb uses the periodic inventory method. Purchases for the month were as follows: Date Quantity Unit Cost Total Cost May 4 20 $5.80 $116.00 May 17 80 $5.50 $440.00 Cobb sold 10 units on May 14 for $120. What is the weighted average cost of goods sold for May for Cobb?  
A. $60.20  
B. $62.10  
C. $62.50  
D. $65

Question: Each of the parameters listed below will be considered observable Level 2 inputs that can be used to determine the fair value of an asset or liability, except for  
A. Quoted prices for identical assets and liabilities in inactive markets  
B. Quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets  
C. Internally generated cash flow forecasts for the relevant asset or liability  
D. Interest rates observable over standard time intervals

Question: The following information pertains to the utility bills of Dash Co.: Covered period Amount Payment date April 16 – May 15 $5000 June 1 May 16 – June 15 $6000 July 1 June 16 – July 15 $8000 August 1 What amount should Dash report as a liability on its balance sheet as of June 30?
A. $6000  
B. $7000  
C. $10,000  
D. $14,000

Question: During the audit of the financial statements of a non-issuer company, the accountant becomes aware of several lease agreements that should be capitalized but are not. The accountant considers these lease agreements material to the financial statements. The accountant decides to modify the standard review report since management will not capitalize the lease agreements. Under these circumstances, the accountant should  
A. Issue a negative conclusion due to non-compliance with GAAP.  
B. Express no assurance on the financial statements of the organization.  
C. Emphasize that the financial statements are intended for limited use only.  
D. Disclose the non-compliance with GAAP in a separate paragraph of the accountant's report.

Question: The non-profit organization Skytop Co. is considering purchasing a machine for $80,000 that will provide a uniform cash flow of $25,000 over four years. Skytop evaluates capital projects using discounted cash flows with a cost of capital of 10% per year. Based on the table below, what actions should Skytop take regarding the purchase of the machine and why? Future value of $1 in 4 years at 10% $1.464 Present value of $1 in 4 years at 10% $0.683 Future value of $1 ordinary annuity in 4 years at 10% $4.641 Present value of $1 ordinary annuity in 4 years at 10% $3.170 Purchase: Reason:
A. Yes, the net cash flow is $20,000  
B. Yes, the net present value is $36,025  
C. No net present value ($750)  
D. No net present value ($8,750)

Question: The defendant had a quarrel with a neighbor. During the argument, the defendant pulled out his utility knife, intending only to scare the neighbor. The defendant accidentally cut the neighbor's arm slightly with the knife. The defendant was unaware that his neighbor had hemophilia, which later caused the neighbor's death from the cut. What is the most serious crime the defendant can be convicted of?
A. murder.
B. Intentional murder.
C. Unintentional murder.
D. Battery.

Question: The homeowner transferred his property to his cousin "for life, with the remainder to the heirs (of the homeowner)." Later, the cousin transferred the property to a farmer "as long as he farms the property." After the cousin's death, the homeowner's heirs filed a lawsuit against the farmer for ownership rights. Which common law doctrine would be most applicable for the court to determine ownership of the property?
A. The Rule in Wild's Case.
B. The Doctrine of Destructibility of Contingent Remainders.
C. The Doctrine of Worthier Title.
D. The Rule Against Remainders in Favor of Heirs of the Grantee.

Question: In Duga Dogmena's case, he had a domesticated golden retriever named Rover. Rover was a good, friendly dog who loved to run and chase cars, but never harmed anyone. One dark evening before the streetlights came on, Rover was chasing cars on the street when Ginny Grandma, 85 years old, swerved to avoid hitting the dog. When she swerved, Ginny crashed into a parked car and sustained a head injury. If Ginny files a lawsuit against Dag Dogman under the theory of strict liability, the court is likely to rule in favor of 
A. Ginny, because Dag's dog was actually the cause of Ginny's injuries.  
B. Dag, because the retriever is a domesticated animal.  
C. Dag, if a statute or ordinance does not prohibit allowing dogs on public streets.  
D. Dag, because the strict liability rule for dogs would not include dogs that do not exhibit vicious tendencies.

Question: One night, the victim was at home when she heard a knock at the door. When the victim opened the door, three defendants were standing in front of her. They pushed the victim into her house and threatened her with bodily harm if she did not cooperate. Tying her up with ropes, the trio continued to search the victim's house. They then placed many valuables and other items of the victim into a large bag and hurriedly left her house. For what crimes should the defendants be convicted?
A. Assault, battery, and robbery.
B. Theft, burglary, and robbery.
C. Burglary and robbery.
D. Only robbery.

Question: During the deer hunting season, open to hunters with rifles, one hunter saw a deer in the forest. He shot at the deer, hoping to hit and kill it. Instead, he struck and injured a tourist. The hunter did not realize there was a tourist present. Does the injured traveler have a claim against the hunter for damages?  
A. No, because the hunter did not intend to shoot at the tourist.  
B. No, because the hunter did not have direct physical contact with the tourist.  
C. Yes, because the bullet from the hunter's rifle made direct physical contact with the tourist.  
D. Yes, because the hunter intentionally fired the rifle.

Question: Max entered a mini-market, pulled out a gun, and demanded that the cashier empty the cash register. As he nervously looked around for the police, the cashier reached out and tried to grab the gun. After that, Max dropped the gun, which accidentally fired, killing a nearby customer. Max is charged with first-degree murder. He is likely to be 
A. Acquitted, as he did not have the necessary intent required for first-degree murder.  
B. Acquitted, as the immediate cause of death was the cashier's actions.  
C. Convicted, as any death that is a natural and probable consequence of a crime is first-degree murder.  
D. Convicted, as the use of deadly weapon implies intent to cause serious bodily harm.

Question: A man was arrested and charged with robbery. After being taken into custody, he received Miranda rights and was then taken to the police station to prepare a report. At the station, the man told the officer that he was willing to confess. After that, the officer turned on the video recorder and recorded the man's confession. At the court hearing, the prosecution called the police officer to testify about the incriminating statements made by the man in his confession. After the man's lawyer objected, the proposed testimony of the police officer is 
A. inadmissible, as the video recording is the best evidence of the man's confession.  
B. inadmissible, as it is hearsay that does not fall under any recognized exception.  
C. admissible, as the police officer had firsthand knowledge of the confession.  
D. admissible, because the man was given his Miranda rights before the confession was obtained.

Question: The defendant told two men that the medical equipment company is now using an old warehouse by the river to store defibrillators. One night, the two men broke into the warehouse and started loading large boxes of defibrillators onto their truck. As they were leaving, one of the men accidentally threw a cigarette butt onto a pile of old cardboard boxes and papers. Soon after, the trash ignited into a small fire. Although the men managed to extinguish the fire without any danger to themselves, they did not do so. Instead, they fled. Meanwhile, the fire quickly spread, engulfing the entire warehouse. If the defendant is later charged as an accomplice to the conspiracy, he is most likely to be held liable 
A. accessory before the fact.  
B. second-degree director.  
C. accomplice.  
D. not liable.

Question: A man is being tried for securities fraud. He takes the stand to testify in his own defense. During direct examination, the man's lawyer presents evidence of his good character. If the prosecution objects, which of the following statements is correct?  
A. The defendant may provide evidence to support his truthfulness.  
B. The defendant may provide evidence to demonstrate his honesty.  
C. The defendant cannot provide evidence to demonstrate his honesty, as character evidence is inadmissible.  
D. The defendant cannot provide evidence of truthfulness unless it has been tested during cross-examination.

Question: A group of people stole a painting from an art museum. One of them, who was the driver, was arrested while committing another crime. He told the police, "I didn't even get any money from the art museum. Everything went to the first guy and the second guy." When the first and second guys are tried for the theft of the painting, is the driver's statement admissible in court?  
A. Yes, as a confession of a party opponent.  
B. Yes, as a statement against the interests of other defendants.  
C. No, because it was made while in custody and is therefore unreliable.  
D. No, because this statement was not made in furtherance of or in support of a conspiracy, and therefore it is hearsay.

Question: As a result of a traffic accident involving the defendant, a man and his passenger died. Now the man's wife is filing a lawsuit for damages for the loss of companionship and society. The wife testified that she and her husband had a close relationship and were happy in their marriage for over 15 years. Then, during cross-examination, the defendant's lawyer asked her if she "knew about the affair her husband had with his passenger?" The wife's lawyer immediately objected to this question. The judge must rule that the question is
A. objectionable because it goes beyond the direct examination.
B. objectionable because it was very prejudicial.
C. not objectionable because the plaintiff's knowledge of such a matter was evidence of the significance to be given to her loss.
D. not objectionable because it pertains to the issue of negligence.

Question: The federal law provides states with funds for child protection programs on the condition that such programs are implemented in accordance with federal standards. The United States filed a lawsuit in federal court against the state for an injunction, claiming that the child protection programs in the state, which were partially funded by federal funds allocated under this statute, did not meet federal standards. The state refused the lawsuit. Is it likely that the court will dismiss the lawsuit?
A. No, because Congress can impose any conditions on the receipt of federal funds.
B. No, since the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit lawsuits filed by the United States.
C. Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits lawsuits against the state in federal court.
D. Yes, because the protection of child welfare is the responsibility of the states.

Question: A man and a woman were racing in an illegal drag race. Both were exceeding the speed limit but were very careful. However, when the woman's car suddenly had a tire blowout, she lost control and crashed, injuring a pedestrian. Later, the pedestrian sued the man because the woman had no insurance and no assets. Is it likely that the pedestrian will win this action?
A. No, because the man did not cause any bodily harm.
B. No, because the man was driving very carefully.
C. Yes, because the man and woman acted in concert, engaging in a dangerous activity.
D. Yes, because the man was speeding.

Question: A consumer from State A filed a federal lawsuit against a manufacturer, registered and having its principal place of business in State B, for product liability in the amount of $100,000. The consumer claimed that a defect in the manufacturer's product caused serious injuries to the consumer. In its response, the manufacturer filed a third-party complaint against the product designer, also registered and having its principal place of business in State B. Arguing that the consumer did not sue the correct defendant, the manufacturer claimed that the designer is fully responsible for the defect that caused the consumer's injuries and that the manufacturer is not at fault. After being terminated, a woman filed a federal lawsuit against her former employer, claiming that her supervisor discriminated against her based on gender. The woman's complaint included a detailed account of what the supervisor said and did over the years, citing his phone calls and emails to her and her own emails to the supervisor's manager asking for help. The designer is aware that the manufacturer did not follow all of the designer's specifications in producing the product. Which of the following arguments is most likely to achieve the designer's goal of dismissing the third-party complaint?
A. The court lacks subject matter jurisdiction over the third-party complaint because both the manufacturer and the designer are citizens of State B.
B. The manufacturer failed to obtain the court's permission to file a third-party complaint.
C. The manufacturer's failure to follow the designer's instructions resulted in a defect that caused the consumer's injuries.
D. The manufacturer's third-party complaint did not state a proper third-party claim.

Question: In the course of his defense against the murder charge, the defendant provided testimony that he was committing a bank robbery in another state on the day the victim was killed. The testimony is 
A. admissible as non-hearsay.  
B. admissible as a statement against interest.  
C. admissible as a declaration against interest.  
D. admissible as a present sense impression.

Question: The woman was in her seventh month of pregnancy with her first child. One day, the woman was preparing a snack in her kitchen when she looked out the window and saw a horrific crime taking place. The woman watched in horror as a gang member pulled out a gun and used it to shoot a victim, a member of a rival gang. The gang member did not know that someone was witnessing him shoot the victim. The woman watched as the victim collapsed and fell dead on the neighbor's lawn. As a result of the shock from witnessing this horrific event, the woman had a miscarriage. If the woman files a claim against the local gang member who shot the victim, she will
A. recover, as she suffered physical injury, not just emotional.
B. recover, as the gang member acted intentionally in shooting the victim.
C. not recover, as the woman was not in the zone of danger.
D. not recover, as the gang member did not know the woman was watching.

Question: A man and his wife were in an unhappy marriage. The man was an alcoholic who physically abused his wife when he was drunk. One night, the man beat his wife, and she decided to kill him. The wife, who had experience with firearms, planned to shoot her husband while he was sleeping. Before carrying out her plan, the wife took out a life insurance policy on her husband for $1,000,000, naming herself as the beneficiary. Soon after, the husband and wife celebrated their 10th wedding anniversary. They went out for dinner and had a truly pleasant evening together. After a wonderful night, the wife changed her heart and decided that she really loved her husband and did not want to kill him. The wife confessed and told her husband about her plan, begging for forgiveness. The husband was outraged. He filed for divorce and reported his wife's plan to the police. If the wife is charged with attempted murder, she should be found 
A. guilty because she took out a life insurance policy.  
B. guilty because she intended to kill her husband.  
C. not guilty because she did not take a substantial step in committing the murder.  
D. innocent because she actually withdrew from criminal activity.

Question: Two cousins acquired ownership of real property as joint tenants with right of survivorship. The first cousin pledged his share in the joint tenancy as collateral for a $20,000 loan and signed a court note. Later, this was entered as a judgment against the cousin's share in the property. The cousin died a year later. The second cousin decided to sell the property, but the mortgage holder filed a lawsuit to prevent the sale and foreclose on it. The second cousin defended on the grounds that any lien on the cousin's share in the property was extinguished upon the cousin's death. Will the court grant the mortgage holder's lien against the sale of the property by the surviving cousin?
A. Yes, because the cousin's consent to the lien by court judgment is presumed by law, and this consent destroyed the joint tenancy.
B. Yes, because a mortgage or court lien against one joint tenant destroys the tenancy and extinguishes the right of survivorship.
C. No, because a joint tenant cannot lawfully obtain a court judgment solely against the interests of that joint tenant, as it would be an unconstitutional interference with the property rights of another.
D. No, because when the cousin died, the cousin became the sole owner by right of survivorship, according to the joint tenancy, which was completely intact.

Question: The defendant was charged with murder. The murder occurred on February 1. At the time of the crime, this jurisdiction required a unanimous verdict from all 12 jurors for a conviction of a crime punishable by death. On November 1, the state legislature passed a new law requiring a majority vote of seven out of 12 jurors for a conviction of a crime punishable by death. The trial of the defendant began on December 1. He was subsequently found guilty of murder by a vote of eight to four. Following the trial, the defendant's attorney filed a motion to overturn the verdict. What would be the most significant constitutional basis for overturning the verdict?
A. Ex post facto clause.  
B. Contract clause.  
C. Due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.  
D. Sixth Amendment right to a fair trial.

Question: One late afternoon, a woman was hitchhiking when a man picked her up. Soon after, the man stopped and parked the car in a roadside rest area. They were smoking marijuana when another car skidded and crashed into the man's car. As a result of the collision, the man's car was damaged, and the man sustained bodily injuries. The woman was also injured. In fact, the impact caused her to lose consciousness for several minutes. The woman sued the other driver, seeking compensation for his alleged negligence. In court, the woman testified about her injuries and the other driver's negligence. In defense, the other driver called a lawyer who lived next door to the woman. The lawyer suggested testifying that after the accident, the woman consulted him about her claim and confidentially asked the lawyer how she could falsely testify that she was not smoking marijuana at the time of the accident. Against the woman's lawyer's objection, the lawyer's testimony is
A. admissible as an admission.  
B. admissible as a statement against interest.  
C. inadmissible as it violates the woman's right against self-incrimination.  
D. inadmissible as it violates the attorney-client privilege of confidential communication.

Question: An irrevocable written offer (firm offer) by a merchant to sell goods
A. Must be separately signed if the offeree provides a contract form that contains the offer.
B. The term of validity is three months.
C. Is not transferable.
D. Cannot exceed three months, even if under consideration.

Question: A woman owned a 10-acre parcel of rural agricultural land in absolute fee. The woman agreed to sell the agricultural land to a man, and each signed a letter stating that the agricultural land was sold: "...for $10,000, the receipt of which is acknowledged." In fact, the man had not yet paid the woman $10,000. On the date set for closing, the woman transferred the deed to the agricultural land to the man, who gave the woman a check for $10,000. However, a few days after the woman deposited the check, she received a notice from her bank that the check was not honored due to insufficient funds in the account. The woman then sued the man. In court, the woman is trying to prove that the man actually did not pay her the $10,000 as stated in their written document. The man objects to the woman's proposed testimony. Will the judge uphold the man's objection?  
A. No, because the rule of evidence does not apply to events occurring after the drafting of the text.  
B. No, because the rule of evidence of conditional relevance does not operate to exclude evidence that demonstrates the absence or lack of consideration.  
C. Yes, because the written document appears to be a complete integration of the parties' agreement.  
D. Yes, because the doctrine of the parol evidence rule will not allow the woman to contradict her own signed acknowledgment that she received $10,000.

Question: A high school student ran for the position of president of the student council. He was the best student chosen to represent the class. Inexplicably, he delivered a campaign speech at a school assembly that was filled with vivid stories and anecdotes about fictional sexual escapades and the valor of certain teachers and students. Several faculty members and students complained. The principal suspended him for five days and stripped him of honors. The student, along with his parents, filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking an injunction and damages based on a violation of First Amendment free speech rights. The federal court ruled in favor of the student, but the case was appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court for a final decision. Did the Supreme Court support the assistance provided to the student?
A. No, the school was performing its proper function by trying to limit the use of vulgarity and offensive discourse in a high school where free speech can be restricted.
B. Yes, despite some discomfort for teachers and students, immature presentations should be tolerated out of respect for the necessity of providing students with platforms for free speech.
C. No, the student did not have a right to free speech, especially considering the violent disturbances in schools in recent years.
D. Yes, in modern society, sexual insults and sexual humor are so woven into the fabric of society that, in the interest of free speech, they must be tolerated.

Question: The landlord rented a commercial building to the tenant for five years. The rent was due on the first day of each month, and the landlord retained the right to terminate the lease if the tenant failed to fulfill obligations. The lease term ended 18 months ago. However, the tenant remained in possession of the building and continued to pay rent on time. The landlord continued to accept the rent. The fair rental value of the building now significantly exceeds what the tenant was paying, and the landlord recently found a third party willing to pay a higher rent. When the tenant paid the rent six weeks ago, the landlord accepted the rent but wrote to the tenant that she must vacate by the end of the month. The tenant, who still occupies the building, informed the landlord that she does not want to move and is willing to pay the current fair market rent. The landlord consulted his lawyer for advice on ownership rights. Who should be said to have the right to possession?
A. The landlord, as he properly notified the termination of the lease.
B. The landlord, as he retained the right of re-entry.
C. The tenant, as she stated she is willing to pay the current fair market rent.
D. The tenant, as the landlord did not provide valid reasons for terminating the lease.

Question: A paper manufacturing company entered into a contract with a construction company for the construction of a new warehouse. The contract stipulated that the construction company would receive payment after the completion of the warehouse. The contractor completed the construction of the warehouse, but it had minor deviations from the plans due to the replacement of certain building materials that were not available on the market. The construction company finished the work and is demanding payment. The paper company refused to pay due to deviations from the specifications. Is it likely that the construction company will win a breach of contract against the paper company?  
A. Yes, the company performing the construction work can always collect for the work done.  
B. No, the construction company cannot change the specifications and expect payment.  
C. No, the construction company is guilty of fraud and misrepresentation.  
D. Yes, the construction company has mostly fulfilled the contract.

Question: While visiting his son, the grandfather tripped over a toy left on the floor by his four-year-old grandson. The grandfather fell and sustained serious injuries. The grandfather regularly visited his son's home and knew that the grandson often left toys scattered around the house. The son never warned the grandfather to watch out for the toys. The grandfather sued his son for the injuries he sustained. At the court hearing, after the evidence was presented, both the grandfather and the son filed motions for a ruling on liability. The jurisdiction has abolished intra-family immunity and applies traditional premises liability rules. What action should the court take?
A. Deny both motions and submit the case to a jury for a determination of negligence.
B. Deny both motions and submit the case to a jury based on strict liability.
C. Grant the grandfather's motion, as the son is legally responsible for failing to warn about the danger of leaving toys on the floor.
D. Grant the son's motion, as the son had no duty to warn that the grandson might leave toys on the floor.

Question: The state educational agency, adhering to all legal requirements, acquired a parcel of land through eminent domain. The landowner accepted the awarded fair market value and did not contest it. For the next 15 years, the agency held the property but did not use it for educational purposes. In the 16th year, the agency abandoned the planned educational use and sold it at a properly announced auction in accordance with state law. The original landowner filed an appeal, claiming that the agency only took a fee simple that can be defined, and when it ceased targeted use for educational purposes, the fee simple ownership reverted to the original owner. Is it likely that the appellate court will decide that the landowner can assert the right to stop the attempt to transfer?  
A. No, because the state also acquired a fee simple ownership through adverse possession after 11 continuous uninterrupted years of holding.  
B. No, because the original transfer was conducted lawfully, and the landowner received fair market value, thus allowing the presumption of fee simple ownership in the agency.  
C. Yes, eminent domain is limited to the use of property that is urgently needed for public use, and failure to use it for that purpose forfeits ownership in the agency.  
D. Yes, because every acquisition of eminent domain involves payment that can simply be defined for state acquisition.

Question: In which of the following situations could the defendant's state of intoxication NOT refute his criminal guilt?  
A. The defendant drank a fifth of bourbon. Later that day, he approached the victim and, brandishing a knife, told her to come with him, or he would strike her. He led the victim to his car and then ordered her to undress. When the victim was taking off her tights, she kicked the defendant in the head, temporarily stunning him. The victim then successfully escaped from the car. The suspect was arrested and charged with attempted rape.  
B. The defendant attended a wedding at a hotel, where he drank several vodka daiquiris. After the reception, the defendant got into a fierce argument with the hotel parking attendant. The defendant retrieved a tire iron from his car and threw it at the attendant. The tire iron missed the attendant and hit the victim as he was entering the hotel. The suspect was arrested and charged with assault with intent to cause bodily harm.  
C. The defendant spent the entire evening drinking alcoholic beverages at a bar with three of his friends. An undercover detective overheard the defendant and his friends planning to rob the bar after closing. When the defendant attempted to pull a gun from his coat, he was quickly disarmed and arrested by the detectives. The suspect is charged with committing armed robbery.  
D. At his law school graduation party, the defendant drank two six-packs of beer. Around midnight, a girl approached the defendant and asked for a ride home. Although the girl was only 15 years old, she looked like a woman in her twenties. The defendant, who had been watching the girl all night, quickly agreed and showed her the way to his car. Once inside, they engaged in sexual intercourse. The age of consent in this jurisdiction is 17 years for women. The defendant was later arrested and charged with rape.

Question: A fumigation company was hired to exterminate pests in one of two buildings in a condominium complex that shared a common wall. The owners of the complex informed the fumigation company that the common wall separating the infested building from the uninfested one was an impenetrable fire wall. The fumigation company conducted its own thorough inspection and determined that the buildings were indeed completely separated by the wall. Residents of the condominium in the building that was to be sprayed were told to evacuate, but residents of the uninfested building were told they could remain while the other building was treated. During and shortly after the fumigation, during which a highly toxic chemical was used, many residents of the uninfested building became ill. It was determined that their illnesses were caused by the fumigation chemical. In fact, there was a hole in the fire wall separating the two buildings, but since it could only be observed from a certain position in the crawl space under the floor of the uninfested building, it was not discovered by either the fumigation company or any previous building inspector. Is it likely that the residents of the uninfested building will prevail in a tort lawsuit against the fumigation company?
