A. No, because the condominium owners were responsible for accurately conveying the condition of their buildings.  
B. No, because the fumigation company exercised a high level of care.  
C. Yes, because the fumigation company may be held strictly liable for its actions.  
D. Yes, because the fumigation company released a hazardous product into the stream of commerce.

Question: The landlord owns a two-story building. The landlord rented the building and surrounding property to the tenant for a term that began on December 1, 2006, and ended on November 30, 2008. Their lease agreement contained the following provisions: "The tenant agrees to pay rent in the amount of $500 per month on the first day of each month and to maintain the building located in the rented premises in as good a condition as it was at the time of the lease until the expiration of the agreement." On April 15, 2007, the tenant held an annual party called "Tax Time," where she and her friends all went to the post office to send their taxes and then drank and dined at the tenant's apartment to celebrate. After a few drinks, one of the tenant's friends became belligerent towards one of the party attendees, who challenged some of the friend's deductions. The friend lunged at another partygoer and crashed into a wall after the latter stepped out of the way. As a result of the accident, one of the walls of the apartment was damaged. This state is a common law jurisdiction. Additionally, the statute of limitations for a negligence claim for damages is five years from the time the cause of the damage arises. In the relevant claim for interpreting the tenant's obligation under the agreement to maintain the premises, which of the following is the most accurate?
A. The tenant is responsible for normal wear and tear under the maintenance agreement.
B. The tenant is liable under such an agreement for all defects, including damage to the wall.
C. The tenant's maintenance agreement is invalid against public policy, as the landlord is obligated to repair the premises that have deteriorated.
D. The tenant's duty to maintain the premises in good condition relieves the landlord of the obligation to disclose any hidden defects.

Question: A man claims to have inherited property from a wealthy businessman. His birth certificate states that he was born out of wedlock. The proceedings protocol for alimony shows that the businessman was recognized as the man's father. However, the man can establish his status as the businessman’s heir only if his mother and the businessman were legally married after his birth. Thus, the man must prove that this marriage existed. The man's lawyer could not find any marriage certificate or documentation. However, the lawyer has a photograph showing a couple dressed in wedding attire. The scene is in front of a church. It is evident that passersby are throwing rice at the couple, who seem to be smiling and bowing in response. The man gave the lawyer the photograph. He found it among his mother's belongings after her death. The man believes that the bride in the picture is his mother. He cannot recognize the groom. A former acquaintance of the businessman, who saw the picture, told the lawyer that he believes the groom is the businessman. If the lawyer wants to present the photograph as evidence that the mother and the businessman were married, the judge must make a ruling regarding the photograph.  
A. admissible only if the photographer is available to testify about the circumstances under which the photograph was taken.  
B. admissible only if a witness confirms that it is a correct and accurate representation of the relevant facts.  
C. inadmissible as non-verbal hearsay that does not fall under any recognized exception.  
D. inadmissible as not the best evidence.

Question: The association transferred a general warranty deed for a vacant parcel of land to the buyer. According to the agreement, the person receiving the grant and their successors were to proportionately participate in the paving of the road adjacent to the property. The grantee transferred the property to a married couple under a special warranty deed that did not contain any contractual conditions regarding the paving of the new road. The buyers did not have a lawyer and did not conduct a title search. When the road was completed, the married buyers refused to pay the share that was demanded from them. The original sellers of the parcel sued the couple in equity without a jury. The judge ruled that the couple must pay their share of the paving. Will the appellate court uphold the trial judge's ruling?
A. Yes, it is an agreement that runs with the land, as it was meant to apply to the heirs and "successors" of the first buyer.
B. Yes, because the landowner is liable for their share of the improvement of any adjacent private roads in any case.
C. No, because the general warranty of the original sellers did not extend to the first buyer.
D. No, because the requirement for the paving had to be specified in the deed to the married couple, and it was not.

Question: A man and his wife were shopping at a local department store when the wife saw a dress that she particularly liked. The wife, who weighed over 300 pounds, could not find a large enough size to fit her. Then she saw a store clerk and asked if the store had the dress in her size. The clerk looked at the wife and said, "You look like a hippopotamus, and I'm very sorry, but we don't have that dress in hippopotamus size." Another customer in the store heard this comment and started laughing. The wife was very upset and hurried out of the store. If the wife sues the department store based on the clerk's actions, the wife will be
A. winning, as the statement was overheard by another customer.
B. winning, as the clerk's behavior was extreme and outrageous.
C. losing, because the clerk was just expressing his opinion.
D. losing, because the wife was only harmed.

Question: A college student and a man got into a fight at a bar during a game of pool. The college student allegedly started the fight by hitting the man over the head with a pool cue after the man made a winning shot. In the trial against the college student for assault, the prosecution called as a witness one of the college student's classmates. The classmate was not present during the fight at the bar. The classmate offered to testify that the next day during class he approached the college student and said, "It was wrong of you to start a fight with that man over a game of pool," after which the college student bowed his head and walked away. The classmate's testimony is 
A. admissible as part of res gestae.  
B. admissible as an admission.  
C. inadmissible as hearsay, not within any recognized exception.  
D. inadmissible as self-serving.

Question: The suspect is being tried for kidnapping. The victim testified that one of the kidnappers referred to another as "Speed." The prosecutor calls a prison employee to testify that while the defendant was in jail awaiting trial, other inmates referred to the defendant as "Speed." Are the prison employee's testimonies admissible?
A. No, because this hearsay is not an exception.  
B. No, because it is significantly more prejudicial than probative.  
C. Yes, as indirect evidence that the defendant was one of the kidnappers.  
D. Yes, to confirm the victim's truthfulness.

Question: One company offered to sell several batches of stones for landscape design at a specified price and terms. The recipient of the offer sent a notification to the offeror stating, "We have received your offer to sell stones for landscape design on the specified terms as of this date." The offeror shipped the goods after receiving this notification. On the day of shipment, the recipient published a form of acceptance with minor changes to the terms. After the goods arrived, the recipient of the offer called the offeror's manager and told him that the company could not accept the offer at this time, that he was sending the goods back, and to "ignore any documents we have sent." The offeror sued the recipient of the offer for breach of contract. Who will win?
A. The offeror will have the advantage, as the publication of acceptance completes the contract between the parties.
B. The recipient of the offer will have the advantage, as he never accepted the offer on the same specified terms.
C. The offeror will have the advantage, as he shipped the goods when he received the first acceptance.
D. The recipient of the offer will have the advantage, as he rejected the offer when he called the offeror's manager.

Question: A patient at a federal hospital reported that a nurse committed sexual assault against her. The man was arrested. During the trial, the prosecution provided evidence that the man had been convicted of two previous charges of sexual assault against two other women, both committed approximately two years ago. The charges and the man's modus operandi in those convictions were nearly identical to this case. The defense attorney objected to the evidence on the grounds that its prejudicial impact outweighs its probative value. Based on the Federal Rules of Evidence, what is the most likely ruling the court will make on this issue?
A. The evidence is too prejudicial and should be excluded.
B. The evidence is inadmissible because it is not relevant to the charges and has low probative value.
C. The evidence is admissible because current state policy strongly favors the arrest and prosecution of sexual predators.
D. The evidence is admissible due to the factual similarity to this charge, which gives the evidence significant probative value.

Question: The landlord owned an apartment that he rented to a college graduate for a three-year term starting December 1, 2007, for a monthly rent of $1,000, payable on the first of each month. After the college graduate lived in the apartment for six months, on June 1, 2008, he transferred his interest in the premises to a college student. The college student paid rent for two months and then transferred his interest to a sophomore college student. The sophomore took possession on August 1, 2008, and paid rent for August but did not pay rent for the next three months of occupancy. Then on December 1, 2008, the sophomore transferred the premises to a freshman college student, who took possession but did not pay rent to the landlord during his occupancy from December 1, 2008, to April 1, 2009. On April 5, 2009, the landlord filed a lawsuit against the freshman college student to recover the unpaid rent for the premises. The freshman is most likely liable for 
A. $8,000.00  
B. $7,000.00  
C. $5,000.00  
D. $4,000.00

Question: A woman owned four beach houses. Each house had star-shaped windows. As the hurricane season approached, she hired a carpenter to build star-shaped windows and deliver them to the four houses. Due to the unique shape of the windows, the carpenter was forced to do all the work by hand. The carpenter and the woman signed a contract in which the carpenter promised to build and deliver the storm windows to all four beach houses within 30 days, and the woman promised to pay $8,000 ($2,000 per house) within one week after the work was completed. Two weeks after signing the contract, a fire destroyed the carpenter's workshop, where he kept all the finished storm windows waiting for delivery. The carpenter then sent the woman a letter stating, "The fire destroyed my equipment and inventory, including the storm windows that were completed and waiting for delivery. I am bankrupt and cannot fulfill my obligations under the contract." The woman then called the carpenter and told him, "If you do not fulfill your contractual obligations, I will sue you!" In a lawsuit for specific performance to compel the carpenter to build and deliver the storm windows, the woman is most likely to be 
A. successful, because the carpenter's loss of inventory does not excuse his duty to perform.  
B. successful, because the beach houses will suffer serious damage in the event of a hurricane without the storm windows being installed.  
C. unsuccessful, because the carpenter's performance would be excused by an act of God.  
D. unsuccessful, because the carpenter's loss of inventory will make his work impossible.

Question: The ranch owner is the owner of a ranch located at the top of a mountain. Below the ranch is a mansion owned by a millionaire. The stream is a non-navigable watercourse that originates at the top of the mountain and flows down into the valley. Both the ranch and the mansion are within the watershed of the stream. When the millionaire purchased the mansion in 1956, he began taking water from the stream and using it to irrigate the southern half of his property, which he used as a farm. By 1956, the southern half of the estate had been cleared and put into cultivation, while the northern half remained wooded and virtually unused. The millionaire continued this established pattern of use and never ceased using the water in this manner. In 1986, the ranch owner built a house on the ranch and began treating water from the stream for domestic use. That year there were heavy rains, causing the stream to flow from the mountain at a high water level. However, in 1987, a drought caused the water level to be very low. Thus, there was only enough water for the millionaire's agricultural irrigation or, alternatively, to meet all of the ranch owner's domestic water needs and one-quarter of the millionaire's irrigation needs. The mountain is in a jurisdiction where the statute of limitations is 15 years. The ranch owner continues to take water for personal use, but it is insufficient for irrigating the mansion. The millionaire then files a relevant lawsuit in 1996 to declare that his water rights in the stream prevail over the ranch owner's rights. Furthermore, the millionaire moves to have the entire flow of the stream transferred to him, regardless of the impact this may have on the ranch owner. If this state adheres to the common law of riparian rights but does not adhere to the doctrine of prior appropriation, who should the court rule in favor of?
A. The ranch owner, because as the upstream landowner, he would have greater rights to the water than the downstream owner.  
B. The rancher, because domestic use is superior and protected over agricultural use.  
C. The millionaire, because he obtained an easement by prescription to divert as much water as he may need.  
D. The millionaire, because he used the water for his benefit earlier than the ranch owner and has continuously used the water.

Question: The landlord has a three-story house. The landlord leased the building and surrounding property to the tenant for a term of six years, starting from December 1, 2003, and ending on November 30, 2009. On April 15, 2004, a neighbor who owned an adjacent plot of land burned leaves and underbrush on his land. A strong wind blew towards the land leased by the landlord to the tenant, carrying the burning leaves onto the tenant's property. The building caught fire, and the damage from the fire amounted to $150,000. Due to the fire, the tenant did not occupy the leased premises from the day of the fire, as the building was uninhabitable. This state is under common law jurisdiction. Additionally, the statute of limitations for a negligence claim for damages is five years from the time the cause of the damage arose. On May 1, 2004, the landlord filed a lawsuit against the tenant, claiming breach of contract for non-payment of rent. The court should rule in favor of
A. the landlord, because the tenant remains obligated to pay rent even if the property became uninhabitable due to the fire.
B. the landlord, because the obligation to pay rent is tied to the land.
C. the tenant, because it would be unfair to enforce the lease provision in the rental agreement due to the premises being made uninhabitable.
D. the tenant, because more states are adopting laws that relieve the tenant of their obligation to pay rent if the premises become uninhabitable due to fire or other natural disasters.

Question: A healthy 2-year-old girl was brought to the office for a routine examination. The child was weaned at 6 months of age and began walking at 10 months. On medical examination, she has mild leg deformities (10th degree genu varum). Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation for management at this time?
A. Increased vitamin D intake  
B. Special exercise program  
C. Surgical correction  
D. No treatment needed at this time

Question: A man is accused of murdering his wife. The prosecution claims that on December 17, the man killed his wife by administering a massive injection of succinylcholine while she was asleep. Succinylcholine is a drug that anesthesiologists use in small amounts as a muscle relaxant. The prosecution asserts that the lethal dose administered to his wife relaxed her lung muscles so much that she suffocated. Other accusations claim that the man's primary motive was to obtain a life insurance policy on his wife for $500,000, of which he was the beneficiary. The first witness for the defense was a doctor who signed the death certificate of the wife. The defendant's lawyer asked her, "Isn't it true that the cause of death was a heart attack?" The doctor answered negatively and stated that the cause of death was unknown. The defendant's lawyer called her testimony a recent fabrication and asked her if she did not state at the investigative hearing that the cause of death was a heart attack. The prosecution immediately objected to this question. The judge must rule that this question is
A. objectionable because the party cannot accuse its own witness.
B. objectionable because the defendant's lawyer did not lay a proper foundation.
C. not objectionable because the party can accuse its own witness due to a prior inconsistent statement.
D. not objectionable because the doctor's testimony at the hearing that took place shortly after the death would be more reliable.

Question: In a large city, littering is always a problem. The state law against littering prohibits throwing trash and other items from any vehicle onto public roads. This is a misdemeanor that carries a fine of $50 without imprisonment. For a third offense, the fine is $500 and there is a provision for 5 days of imprisonment. The statute has no requirement for criminal intent. John and his family are returning from a picnic on the weekend when his children throw trash bags and lunch leftovers out of the back window of the moving car. John is stopped and given a ticket for $50. Can he succeed in defending himself by claiming that he did not know what his children were doing and that he had no criminal intent to violate any laws?
A. No, because this is likely a strict liability law that does not allow for a defense based on mental state.
B. Yes, because he did not know what his children were doing in the back seat, and he did not participate in the violation and did not know they did it or were going to do it.
C. And because the police cannot prove who in the car threw the trash out the window.
D. No, since his criminal intent is clearly established by the circumstances of the events.

Question: A 55-year-old man presented to the doctor with a recurring widespread blistering condition for 2 weeks. Physical examination shows lesions, most numerous in flexural areas, including the axillae and groin. The blisters do not break easily, and there are no oral cavity lesions. These blisters are most likely the result of an adhesion disorder involving which of the following?
A. Basement membrane  
B. Dermal papillae  
C. Langerhans cells  
D. Melanocytes

Question: The court case arose in state courts when the Secretary of Commerce attempted to prevent a person from mailing their new advertising brochures. According to the Secretary's interpretation, the new brochures contained obscene photographs and sexual expressions. The Secretary acted under the authority granted to him by section 1123(b) of state law, which provided: "If the Secretary of Commerce determines that commercial mailings to residents of the state are inappropriate for minors, the Secretary has the authority to prohibit such mailings." The case reached the state supreme court, which ruled that the statute was unconstitutional as it violated both commerce clause provisions and supremacy clause provisions. If this case is reviewed by the U.S. Supreme Court, it will reach that court 
A. by appeal.  
B. by certiorari.  
C. if five justices vote for its review.  
D. despite the doctrine of adequate and independent state grounds.

Question: One late evening, an accountant walked into a bar and ordered a sour whiskey. The bartender served the drink, even though the accountant looked and acted as if he was already very drunk. Soon, the accountant drank another five cocktails that the bartender served, despite the fact that the accountant was clearly and unmistakably intoxicated. After finishing his sixth drink at the bar, the accountant wished the bartender goodnight, swayed out of the bar, got into his car, and drove off. A few blocks, weaving back and forth on the road, the accountant crashed his car into a pedestrian who was walking on the sidewalk next to the road. The pedestrian sustained serious injuries to his back and legs. The bartender's action of serving drinks to the accountant is likely to be considered as 
A. the direct cause of the pedestrian's injury.  
B. the proximate cause of the pedestrian's injury.  
C. the direct cause of the pedestrian's injury.  
D. the intervening cause of the pedestrian's injury.

Question: A 37-year-old man presented to the emergency department because he has been experiencing nausea and dizziness for the past hour. His history is significant for esophageal varices due to alcoholic cirrhosis and ascites, which are being treated with spironolactone. He drinks eight to ten alcoholic beverages daily. While you are gathering additional history, the patient vomits a large amount of bright red blood and is difficult to arouse. Vital signs: temperature 36.0°C (96.8°F), pulse 110/min, respirations 12/min, and blood pressure 90/50 mmHg. After starting intravenous fluid administration, which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
A. Organize transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt
B. Start intravenous vasopressin therapy
C. Perform endotracheal intubation
D. Perform upper endoscopy

Question: A man and a woman, who were friends, decided to buy a car together. The man put in $5,000, and the woman's father signed a loan for $10,000. The title was registered in the woman's name, and the man was paying off the loan. They verbally agreed that it was joint property, equal ownership. A few months later, their relationship soured. They argued over ownership and use of the car. One day, the man tried to drive off with the car, but the woman jumped in and continued to argue while he was driving. He then crashed into a pole and destroyed the car out of spite, saying that if he couldn't have it, no one would. Law enforcement arrested the man for car theft (theft from the owner) and vandalism (damage to someone else's or joint property). Assuming the accuracy of the above facts is beyond reasonable doubt, what crime or crimes are likely to result in a sustained conviction?
A. He may be convicted of theft, but not for criminal actions.  
B. He cannot be convicted of any crime.  
C. He may be convicted only for vandalism.  
D. He may be convicted for both theft and vandalism.

Question: A 68-year-old woman has a history of breast cancer that has recurred twice in the last 5 years. She has undergone radiation and chemotherapy for metastatic bone cancer. Today she comes to the office seeking help with mid-thoracic back pain so she can use fewer pain medications. The most appropriate osteopathic manipulative treatment technique for this patient's spine is  
A. high-velocity, low-amplitude  
B. indirect myofascial release  
C. isotonic therapeutic exercise  
D. medium-velocity, medium-amplitude

Question: The player learned that his friend was going on vacation to visit a casino. The gambling player, who was a passionate fan of college football, approached his friend. The player explained that he wanted to place a bet with a bookmaker that his favorite team would win the college football championship next year. The player further explained that he read that the odds of his team winning the football championship next year were listed as 100-1, and he wanted to bet $1000 on his team. The gambling player told his friend that he would pay him for his efforts. After further discussion, the gambling player wrote the following agreement: "I hereby promise to pay my friend $100 if he places a $1000 bet for me that my favorite team will win the college football championship next year. The bet should be made at My Lucky Sportsbook at the casino. I also promise to pay my friend $100 within 30 days after the bet is made. My friend promised not to tell anyone about the bet." After both the player and his friend signed the agreement, the player gave him $1100, which included $1000 to place the bet and $100 as an initial deposit for his friend's efforts. Then the friend went on vacation. Shortly after arriving, the friend tried to place the bet for the player. However, the friend found out that the player's lucky casino had recently closed its sportsbook. The friend then went to another neighboring casino and found that they had a sportsbook that also offered 100-1 odds on the player's favorite team winning the college football championship next year. The friend placed the bet using the sportsbook of the other casino. Upon returning from vacation, the friend handed the betting slip to the player. Nothing more was said until 30 days later when the friend asked the player when he would receive the last $100. After that, the player refused to pay the friend any more. What of the following is the best defense for the player in the event of a breach of contract claim by the friend regarding the $100?
A. The contract was void ab initio because the contract could not be performed in full within one year.
B. The fact that the friend placed the $1000 bet at another casino instead of the player's casino constituted a material breach of contract, which discharged the player from any further contractual obligations under the terms of the agreement.
C. During the vacation, the friend told his girlfriend about the $1000 he bet on behalf of the player.
D. Since the player's lucky casino no longer had a sportsbook to place the bet, all contractual obligations were suspended under the doctrine of impossibility of performance.

Question: The suspect was arrested and charged with conspiracy to obtain stolen property. During the presentation of the accused, a defense attorney represented him. After posting bail, he was released. After his release, the defendant got a job as a bartender at a local bar. Three weeks before the scheduled trial, an informant entered the bar. After a few drinks, the informant started a conversation with the defendant, who was on duty at the time. The defendant was unaware that the man was a paid police informant. During their conversation, the informant told the defendant that he had read about his arrest in the newspapers and asked the defendant for the names of his accomplices. Unbeknownst to him, the defendant made some confessions, which the informant later relayed to the prosecutor. At the court hearing, the prosecution attempted to introduce the defendant's confessions as evidence. The defendant's motion to exclude this evidence will likely be 
A. denied, as the defendant's statements were voluntary.  
B. dismissed, as the defendant assumed the risk that his trust in the informant was misplaced.  
C. granted, as the defendant's right to counsel under the Sixth Amendment to the Constitution was violated.  
D. granted, as the defendant's right against self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment was violated.

Question: A 27-year-old man was hospitalized 45 minutes after being involved in a car accident. Physical examination shows a sluggish response to stimuli. Neurological examination shows no other abnormalities. A skull X-ray shows a linear fracture of the base of the skull without depression. Two weeks later, the patient develops polyuria and polydipsia. Laboratory tests show normal serum glucose concentration, increased serum osmolality, and decreased urine osmolality. After administration of desmopressin, urine osmolality increases. The favorable effect of this drug is most likely due to the activation of which of the following?
A. Adenylate cyclase  
B. Ca2+ channels  
C. Janus kinase  
D. Serine kinase

Question: Anticipating an increase in business volume for the holiday season, the owner of a retail store decided to hire another employee. On October 31, the owner signed a written contract with the employee, which stipulated that the employee would be hired to work in the retail store in November and December for $2,000 per month. At the end of November, the owner noticed that the business had not grown as much as he had expected. The owner informed the employee that if he did not agree to a pay cut, he would be terminated. Reluctantly, on December 1, the employee verbally agreed to a pay cut of $500 for December. Which of the following statements regarding the agreement on December 1 between the owner and the employee is most accurate?
A. It constituted a valid reform of their original written contract.
B. It constituted a valid modification of their original written contract.
C. It constituted a novation of their original written contract.
D. It did not change the rights and obligations of the parties under the terms of their original contract.

Question: A 44-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a neck lump that she noticed 1 week ago. She denies any tenderness, fever, weight loss, or fatigue. Physical examination reveals a freely mobile 2 cm mass in the lower left lobe of the thyroid gland. In addition to measuring thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine levels, the most appropriate initial diagnostic method for this lesion is  
A. thyroid nuclear scan  
B. iodine-131 scan  
C. fine-needle aspiration  
D. thyroid ultrasound

Question: At the subway station in the city, there is always significant construction going on, including the renovation of the elevator shaft between the platform and ground level. There is a warning sign that says "this elevator is currently out of service, please do not use it." A passenger sees the signs but still attempts to ride the elevator and gets injured when she falls into the shaft. When the passenger sues the city for negligence, the city claims she assumed the risk. Is this a valid and accurate defense under these circumstances?  
A. Yes, because she was fully informed and should have known that the elevator was dangerous based on the signs.  
B. Yes, because these signs indicate her negligence and are a legitimate reason for her own harm.  
C. No, because the sign did not explain the danger, only that it was out of service, and therefore she did not know what she was facing.  
D. No, because the city has strict liability when everyone relies on the subway.

Question: The defendant decided to rob a bar because he knew that a new security system was in place that was faulty, and that night was the best time for the break-in. Late in the evening, the defendant broke into the bar and began loading large kegs of beer onto his truck. As he was leaving, the defendant accidentally threw a cigarette butt into the trash bin behind the bar. Soon after, the trash ignited into a small fire. Although the defendant managed to extinguish the fire without any danger to himself, he did not do so. Instead, he climbed into the truck and drove away. Despite the fire spreading beyond the trash bin, firefighters quickly responded and were able to put it out. The floor behind the bar is charred. The statutes for both burglary and arson in this jurisdiction include residential and business structures. For which of the following crimes should the defendant be convicted?
A. Arson, burglary, and theft.
B. Arson and robbery.
C. Theft and robbery.
D. Arson, robbery, and burglary.

Question: Daylight Corp. manufactured, assembled, and sold a steel cutting press designed to cut aluminum sheets into can lids. In 2002, Goodboy Beverages purchased a luxury model of the Daylight cutting press for $20,000. In 2002 and 2003, Daylight received several complaints about dangerous malfunctions from other customers of the cutting presses. In response, Daylight created a safety device and offered it for $5,000 in a brochure sent to all its customers, mentioning that several users had been injured while using the cutting press model. Goodboy received the brochure but did not purchase the $5,000 safety device. In 2004, a Goodboy employee was injured by the press. During the trial, Daylight argued that if Goodboy had purchased the safety device, the injury would not have occurred, and requested a directed verdict. The court should
A. Grant Daylight's motion, as Goodboy's refusal to purchase the safety device was an effective assumption of risk.
B. Deny the motion, as Goodboy's negligence in not purchasing the safety device was less than Daylight's negligence in manufacturing the dangerous press in the first place.
C. Deny the motion, as jurors may consider that Daylight could reasonably foresee that Goodboy would not want to pay $5,000 for the safety device.
D. Deny the motion, as the press was inherently dangerous, and Daylight bore strict liability.

Question: A recent law school graduate was hired for a bar review course on an oral agreement as a consultant for the editorial team. Her duties included preparing new course outlines, proofreading, and grading students' homework. The bar review course agreed to pay the graduate an initial salary of $2500 per month. Three months later, the regional director of the bar review courses approached the graduate and handed her a newly published 60-page brochure titled "Employment Guide." He instructed the graduate to read the guide and noted that it contained important information regarding the company's policy considerations and employee compensation. When the graduate returned home that evening, she began reading the textbook. After reading about 30 pages, the graduate became tired and went to sleep. She never managed to read the rest of the guide. Six months later, the graduate received a termination notice from the bar review course. The notice stated that the graduate was being terminated for failure to perform her duties, as she complained about the low quality of the bar review course materials and refused to work overtime. After her termination, the graduate filed a lawsuit against the bar association for breach of contract. Which of the following, if true and proven, would provide the best defense for the bar review course?
A. All other employees of the bar review courses worked overtime when required.
B. When the graduate agreed to work for the bar review course, the company never made any promises regarding job security or duration of employment.
C. The materials in the bar review course were recently reviewed by the American Bar Association's Committee on Legal Education and received a "high rating."
D. The second page of the bar review course guide contained a paragraph stating that all policies, instructions, and employee compensation are "purely gratuitous and not intended to create any permanent contractual obligations."

Question: One Sunday, a sports fan went to a professional football match. While standing in line at a kiosk, he got into an argument with three men who were ahead of him in line. The three men were friends and attended the game together. One of the men punched the fan in the mouth. A fight broke out. During the altercation, one of the other three men hit the fan on the head with a bottle, causing him to suffer a serious concussion. The sports fan does not know for sure which of the three men hit him with the bottle. If the sports fan files a lawsuit against the man who punched him in the mouth for damages for his head injury, will the sports fan win?
A. Yes, because the man who punched him in the mouth was the instigator who threw the first punch that started the argument.
B. Yes, because the man who punched him in the mouth and the other men acted in concert.
C. No, because the man who punched him in the mouth did not actually hit the sports fan with the bottle.
D. No, because the sports fan cannot provide evidence of which of the men hit him on the head with the bottle.

Question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the office for a routine check-up. She was diagnosed with Turner syndrome in childhood during an evaluation for coarctation of the aorta. During today's visit, her mother reports that the girl has been talking about babies. You have been the patient's doctor for the past 6 years and know that she is in the prepubertal stage. The most appropriate advice to give the patient, if she wants to have a family, is that she will need to do which of the following?
A. adopt
B. undergo amniocentesis if she becomes pregnant
C. have surgery
D. receive genetic counseling

Question: A married couple sued a real estate broker for misrepresentation and breach of contract due to the failure to fulfill promises made regarding the purchase of a home. They claimed that they received promises from the broker that if they immediately bought the house, the sellers would provide them with a $15,000 discount after closing. During the closing, the sellers claimed they were unaware and did not pay. During the trial against the broker, the couple called one of the broker's agents to testify, who stated that he was present at the meeting with the buyers and heard the broker make the same promise. The broker denied that the testimony was hearsay. What is the court most likely to decide regarding the admissibility of the testimony?
A. The testimony is admissible as it is a party admission made through an authorized agent of the party regarding a matter within the scope of his duties.
B. The testimony is inadmissible as the agent was not authorized to speak on behalf of his principal.
C. The testimony is inadmissible as it is pure hearsay offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
D. The testimony is admissible even if it is hearsay, as the broker is available for cross-examination.

Question: A 40-year-old man presented to the clinic with symptoms of odynophagia and gastroesophageal reflux. He also reports that he had vomiting last week. His past medical history reveals AIDS, and his last CD4 count was 30 cells/μL. The stool test result and hemoglobin level are normal. A rectal examination reveals brown stool that is positive for occult blood. What is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this patient?
A. prescription for a proton pump inhibitor and a prokinetic agent  
B. prescription for an H2-blocker trial for 6 weeks  
C. prescription for clotrimazole lozenges  
D. referral for upper endoscopy with biopsy

Question: A 27-year-old woman, pregnancy 2, paragraph 1, at 12 weeks of pregnancy came to the doctor for a prenatal check-up. She feels well. Her first pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated. Medications include folic acid and multivitamins. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 108/60 mmHg. Pelvic examination shows that the size of the uterus corresponds to a 12-week gestation. A urine strip shows leukocyte esterase; urinalysis shows leukocytes and rare gram-negative rods. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Recommend drinking 8 ounces of cranberry juice daily  
B. Oral therapy with amoxicillin  
C. Oral therapy with metronidazole  
D. Intravenous therapy with cefazolin

Question: A 67-year-old woman presents to the doctor with mild bruising for the past 4 months. She has a history of lung cancer, which she underwent radiation therapy for 6 months ago. She has a 2-year history of hypertension treated with a thiazide diuretic and an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. Examination, including neurological assessment, reveals no abnormalities except for numerous ecchymoses. Hemoglobin concentration is 13 g/dl, leukocytes 5000/mm3, platelets 35000/mm3. Serum antiplatelet antibody analysis is negative. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnosis?
A. Abdominal CT
B. Chest CT
C. Bronchoscopy
D. Bone marrow aspiration

Question: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the doctor due to a 2-day history of fever and painful swelling of the left ankle. He has a history of recurrent cervical lymphadenitis and pneumonia since childhood. Two years ago, a culture from an abscess in the cervical region grew Staphylococcus aureus. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F). Examination shows a tender, erythematous, swollen left ankle; point tenderness over the medial malleolus. Bone scanning shows increased uptake in the left lower metaphysis of the tibia. Culture of the bone aspirate grows Serratia marcescens. The nitroblue tetrazolium test shows no color change. What is the most likely mechanism of these findings?
A. Arrest of B-lymphocyte maturation
B. Dysmorphogenesis of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches
C. Impaired chemotaxis
D. Impaired phagocytic oxidative metabolism

Question: A 36-year-old female head of a marketing department is sent to the office for fasting serum cholesterol assessment, which is 249 mg/dL. There is a family history of early ischemic heart disease (IHD), and her father suddenly died at the age of 46 from a myocardial infarction. She tells you that she has never experienced chest pain. She is currently not sexually active and has no children. She claims that due to a stressful lifestyle, she cannot eat properly or follow a special diet, and usually eats fast food. She exercises two to three times a week for about 20 minutes on a treadmill. For the past 20 years, she has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily. Her only medication is acetaminophen for tension headaches. Her height is 165 cm (5 feet 5 inches) and weight is 76 kg (167 pounds); BMI is 28 kg/m2. Vital signs today are normal. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities except for mild obesity. What is the most important step in preventing IHD in this patient?
A. Stress reduction program based on biofeedback  
B. More rigorous and consistent exercise program  
C. Smoking cessation program  
D. Strict low-calorie diet

Question: A 27-year-old woman presented to the doctor with complaints of chronic diarrhea for 3 years and periodic crampy lower abdominal pain. The pain usually decreases during defecation and does not occur at night and does not interfere with sleep. She says she is frustrated with her symptoms and has stopped traveling due to frequent, urgent toilet needs. She has no serious illnesses and is not taking any medications. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 70/min, respiration 14/min, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg. The lower abdomen is slightly tender on palpation; there is no rebound tenderness or guarding. The rest of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory test results are within reference values. Fecal occult blood test is negative. Anti-gliadin antibodies are absent. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy from the options below?
A. Nefazodone  
B. Nortriptyline  
C. Phenelzine  
D. Sertraline

Question: A 26-year-old woman with HIV infection presents to the clinic with pain and redness of the left lower leg for 4 days. She states that the symptoms began after she tripped over a tree branch in her yard and scraped her left leg. Current medications include antiretroviral therapy and ibuprofen as needed. Vital signs: temperature 38.3 °C (100.9 °F), pulse 86/min, respirations 14/min, and blood pressure 138/70 mm Hg. There is a 5 × 8 cm area on the anterior surface of the left lower extremity that is swollen, erythematous, and painful. She has a history of rash after taking erythromycin and has had an anaphylactic reaction to penicillin. Which of the following antibiotic therapies is most appropriate for this patient?
A. Amoxicillin  
B. Ciprofloxacin  
C. Clarithromycin  
D. Clindamycin

Question: A 37-year-old man with type 1 diabetes is hospitalized due to poor glucose control over the past 2 months. Despite the poor control, he insists on being discharged. He reports feeling fatigued, irritable, and hopeless for the past 3 months. He states that he has not been adhering to his diabetic regimen, adding, "Sometimes I forget." He avoids his family and friends because he is not in the mood to see them, but admits that he feels lonely. He has not gotten out of bed for 2 days, which led his wife to call an ambulance and have him hospitalized. Prior to admission, his only medication was insulin, although he often missed doses. He does not consume alcohol. His height is 168 cm (5 feet 6 inches) and weight is 100 kg (220 pounds); BMI is 36 kg/m2. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse 68/min, respiration 18/min, blood pressure 150/85 mmHg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Mental status examination reveals he is fatigued, with a restricted affect. There is no evidence of suicidal thoughts. Cognition is intact. His fasting serum glucose concentration is 120 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Respect the patient's wishes and discuss home care options  
B. Respect the patient's wishes provided he consents to care  
C. Order neuropsychological testing  
D. Seek a court order for the appointment of a legal guardian

Question: A 35-year-old man comes to the office for the result of his HIV test, and he is informed that the result is positive. The patient resists disclosing this to his wife, as he has not told her about his extramarital sexual partners. The doctor informs the patient that his wife's right to know is paramount, as she may also be HIV-positive. Which of the following relationships best describes the rationale for the doctor's recommendation that the patient inform his wife of his condition rather than conceal this information?
A. autonomy outweighs beneficence  
B. autonomy outweighs justice  
C. beneficence outweighs autonomy  
D. nonmaleficence outweighs autonomy

Question: A previously healthy 19-year-old college student presents to the student health service 24 hours after the onset of headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia. She does not recall any contact with sick individuals. She had chickenpox at age 7. Her last examination 1 year ago included a PPD skin test and was unremarkable. She takes multivitamins and an herbal weight loss supplement daily. She received all appropriate vaccinations in childhood but has not had any since then. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. There is no family history of serious illness. She appears lethargic. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F), pulse 112/min, respirations 20/min, blood pressure 100/68 mmHg. Examination reveals diffuse petechiae. Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs are present. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. A lumbar puncture is performed. Analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shows numerous segmented neutrophils and decreased glucose concentration. Gram staining of the CSF reveals gram-negative cocci. What is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy from the options below?
A. Ceftriaxone  
B. Clindamycin  
C. Erythromycin  
D. Metronidazole

Question: A previously healthy 17-year-old girl presented to the doctor with a cough triggered by physical exertion and nasal congestion for 2 months. She plays field hockey and has noticed that she coughs when running on the field. The cough is non-productive and resolves during rest. She has not experienced chest pain or palpitations. She is not taking any medications and does not smoke. Her sister has asthma. The patient appears well. Pulse is 68 bpm, respiration is 16 breaths per minute, blood pressure is 100/75 mmHg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows oxygen saturation of 99%. Cardiopulmonary examination reveals no abnormalities. Chest X-ray shows no abnormalities. Spirometry shows an FEV1:FVC ratio of 90% and FEV1 at 90% of predicted. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A. asthma  
B. Chronic bronchitis  
C. Gastroesophageal reflux disease  
D. Post-nasal drip syndrome

Question: A 77-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of a syncopal episode that occurred while walking. Cardiac examination reveals a systolic murmur of grade 3/6 best heard at the right upper sternal border. There is radiation of the murmur to the neck. The valve anomaly most likely responsible for this episode is  
A. aortic regurgitation  
B. aortic stenosis  
C. mitral regurgitation  
D. mitral stenosis

Question: A 10-year-old boy was brought in for further examination 2 days after being admitted to the emergency department for hives, hoarseness, and dizziness. His symptoms began 15 minutes after being stung by a bee and lasted about 60 minutes; they resolved before he was treated. Over the past year, he has been stung by bees three times, and each reaction has been more severe. Examination shows no abnormalities. What is the most appropriate recommendation to prevent morbidity and mortality from this condition in the future?
A. Avoid places known to have bees  
B. Avoid wearing colorful clothing outdoors  
C. Carrying diphenhydramine tablets  
D. Carrying self-injectable epinephrine

Question: A 46-year-old man with Marfan syndrome, aortic insufficiency, and mitral regurgitation presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain for the past 3 hours. He describes the pain as tearing, radiating to the neck. A week earlier, he experienced a similar but less severe chest pain and took aspirin. What is the most likely cause of the worsening symptoms?
A. Acute bacterial endocarditis  
B. Acute myocardial infarction  
C. Aortic dissection  
D. Esophageal reflux with spasm

Question: A 78-year-old woman is hospitalized for left knee replacement due to degenerative joint disease. She has type 2 diabetes, a long history of hypertension, and chronic kidney disease secondary to diabetes and hypertension. Reversible causes of kidney failure have been excluded. She underwent tonsillectomy at age 9 and laparoscopic cholecystectomy at age 68. Her serum creatinine concentration upon admission was 6.0 mg/dL. Her current therapy includes a low-sodium and low-protein diet per the American Diabetes Association (ADA), enalapril, and acetaminophen. She is a retired seamstress. She and her husband live on a farm 90 miles from the nearest dialysis facility. Considering long-term treatment options for this patient, which of the following factors is the most acceptable to consider?
A. Her eligibility for Medicare  
B. Her history of abdominal surgery  
C. Her history of arthritis  
D. Her suitability for home dialysis

Question: _______ is the least developed area of the brain at birth.  
A. brainstem  
B. cerebral cortex  
C. limbic system  
D. cerebellum

Question: The procedure that involves repeatedly presenting a stimulus to the client until the appeal of that stimulus decreases is best described as  
A. stimulus saturation  
B. response prevention  
C. flooding  
D. implosion

Question: Parkinson's disease is caused by the progressive degeneration of cells that produce dopamine:
A. suprachiasmatic nucleus.
B. insular cortex.
C. substantia nigra.
D. entorhinal cortex.

Question: A 27-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his sister due to increasing confusion for the past 10 hours. He is unable to answer questions. His sister states that he recently visited a psychiatrist for the first time because he heard voices; he was prescribed medication, but she is not sure what it is. She says he has a history of excessive alcohol use, and she thinks he has also experimented with illicit drugs. He appears acutely ill. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F), pulse 124/min, blood pressure 160/102 mmHg. Examination reveals profuse sweating and muscle rigidity. His neck is stiff. The abdomen is soft, non-tender. Mental status examination shows psychomotor agitation alternating with lethargy. The white blood cell count is 15,600/mm3, and serum creatine kinase activity is 943 U/L. What is the most likely explanation for this patient's symptoms?
A. Amphetamine intoxication  
B. Bacterial meningitis  
C. Delirium fever  
D. Malignant neuroleptic syndrome

Question: A multicenter phase 2 study was conducted to determine the efficacy of a new vaccine for the prevention of HIV infection. The study involved 4000 subjects aged 20 to 65 years. Of these, 2100 were men and 1900 were women; 2500 were white, 1000 were African American, 300 were Latino, and 200 were residents of the Asian/Pacific Islander region. The trial results showed no overall benefit from the vaccine. However, a retrospective analysis revealed a small but statistically significant vaccine protection among African Americans. Which of the following is the most accurate justification for doubting the validity of the vaccine efficacy analysis against HIV among African American study subjects?
A. HIV infection is more prevalent among African Americans  
B. The study was not blinded  
C. A type II error occurred  
D. The vaccine response among African Americans was not a primary outcome measure

Question: A 29-year-old man presented to the office with complaints of rapid heartbeat, poor sleep, and a general feeling of unease. He moved 2 months ago to get a promotion and found that he cannot concentrate on his new duties. He is worried about his ability to adapt to the increased responsibilities at work and states that he has been ill for 3 days in the last 2 weeks. The most likely diagnosis is  
A. adjustment disorder with anxious mood  
B. generalized anxiety disorder  
C. major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate  
D. obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

Question: A 35-year-old man presents to the clinic for follow-up regarding sarcoidosis. His only new complaint is leg pain that worsens with activity. He has been taking glucocorticoids for the past 6 months. Vital signs are currently: temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse 78/min, respiration 14/min, and blood pressure 110/70 mmHg. The patient is thin, and does not report any acute distress. Auscultation of the chest reveals scattered bilateral basilar crackles. There is mild pain in the left hip, present with both active and passive range of motion. The Dorsalis pedis pulse is intact. Neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?
A. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head  
B. Herniated nucleus pulposus  
C. Hip joint stenosis  
D. Osteoporosis

Question: A man who owned a haberdashery store placed a phone order with a wholesale supplier of cashmere and wool clothing for "three dozen purple cashmere socks, size 10-13 at the current resale price." The supplier's sales agent orally accepted the order at an agreed price of $250 per dozen. In accordance with the supplier's usual business practice, the sales agent mailed a confirmation letter, which he signed and dated: "According to your phone order, this letter serves to confirm the purchase of 36 dozen cashmere socks, color purple, size 10-13, at the agreed price of $250 per dozen: $9000. This letter was received by the man, who glanced at it but did not notice the wording "36 dozen." The man placed the letter in his files and did not respond to it. Three weeks later, the supplier offered 36 dozen purple cashmere socks, which the man rejected on the grounds that he only ordered three dozen. The supplier resold the same purple cashmere socks to another buyer for a total price of $8000. The supplier sued the man for the difference of $1000. If the man cites fraud as a defense, will such a defense be successful?
A. Yes, because the statute was not satisfied by the supplier's tender of goods that were rejected by the man, and the supplier did not rely on the oral agreement, other than the attempt to deliver.
B. Yes, because the agreed price for three dozen socks was over $500, and the supplier's memo incorrectly stated the quantity of goods ordered.
C. No, because the supplier's written memo was sufficient to satisfy the statute's requirements against the supplier, and the man, having reason to know the contents of the memo, did not give notice of objection within 10 days of receipt.
D. No, because the supplier's written memo acted as an acceptance, with proposals for additional terms that became part of the contract after the man did not object to such additional terms within a reasonable time.

Question: Presenting specific arguments against their views, arguments that are then decisively refuted, can contribute to  
A. strengthening their ambivalence towards the attitude  
B. weakening their resistance to later persuasive appeals  
C. making them indifferent to the object of the attitude  
D. instilling chemistry against later persuasive appeals

Question: The most dangerous physiological complication of nerve bulimia is  
A. swelling  
B. dehydration  
C. gastrointestinal disorder  
D. electrolyte imbalance

Question: A 46-year-old patient, gravida 1, para 1, presented for an appointment with complaints of 2-week-long black discharge from the right nipple, which has been ongoing for 2 weeks. The patient underwent mammography and breast ultrasound 2 months ago to evaluate the palpable increase in glandular tissue in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, which was detected during the last annual examination. The studies showed likely benign results with recommended follow-up in 6 months. Otherwise, the medical history is unremarkable, and the patient is not taking any medications. The BMI is 30 kg/m2. Vital signs are normal. Upon palpation, a mass is noted in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, but no other formations are present. There is slight black discharge from the right nipple. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnosis?
A. Ductography  
B. Excisional biopsy of the glandular tissue  
C. Repeat mammography  
D. Repeat ultrasound of the right breast

Question: A 30-year-old woman who has never given birth presents to the office with complaints of mood changes. She states that for the past few months she has been anxious, hyperactive, and unable to sleep for 3-4 days before the onset of her menstrual period. She further reports that on the day her period starts, she experiences acute depression, suffers from anorexia, and is irritable and lethargic. She has no psychiatric history. Physical examination results are normal. She and her husband have been trying to conceive for over 2 years. History indicates a tuboplasty about a year ago to correct a blocked fallopian tube. The most likely diagnosis is 
A. adjustment disorder with depressed mood  
B. bipolar disorder I, mixed  
C. cyclothymic personality  
D. generalized anxiety disorder

Question: The main function of the psychological licensing commission is best described as:  
A. developing laws that govern the practice of psychology.  
B. anticipating sanctions for unethical and illegal behavior by psychologists.  
C. protecting public welfare.  
D. accrediting psychology graduate programs.

Question: The next measurement of general cognitive abilities would be most appropriate for use with a non-verbal teenager:
A. Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales–5
B. Leiter–R
C. Kaufman Assessment Battery for Children–II
D. Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children–IV

Question: Over the course of 1 year, a study is conducted to evaluate the antileukemic activity of a new tyrosine kinase inhibitor in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in blast crisis. All patients participating in the study are informed that they will be treated with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. They are assigned to sequential dose cohorts ranging from 300 to 1000 mg/day of the drug. Each dose is administered to six to eight patients. The effectiveness of the treatment is determined based on the results of a complete blood count and bone marrow assessment, which are regularly conducted throughout the study. This study is best described as which of the following?
A. Case-control
B. Cross-sectional study
C. Open-label clinical trial
D. Randomized clinical trial

Question: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is most successfully used for 
A. psychogenic amnesia 
B. catatonic schizophrenia 
C. delusional depression 
D. obsessive-compulsive personality disorder

Question: A researcher interested in studying the potential impact of parental alcoholism on child and family development recruits 12-year-olds (n = 100), 13-year-olds (n = 100), and 14-year-olds (n = 100) — half of whom have alcoholic parents and half do not — for a long-term longitudinal study assessing various outcomes. This study is best characterized as:  
A. True experiment  
B. Cross-sequential cohort design  
C. Natural experiment  
D. Cross-sectional cohort design

Question: The genotype of an individual ___________.
A. 23 pairs of chromosomes are inherited from parents
B. The context of the environment
C. Noticeable appearance and characteristics
D. Physical properties of a person

Question: In which type of therapy is the initial intervention the "miracle question"?
A. transtheoretical
B. interpersonal
C. REBT
D. solution-focused

Question: After a brutal beating and a gunshot wound to the abdomen, a 42-year-old woman undergoes resection of a perforation of the small intestine. During the surgery, plastic reconstruction of facial bone fractures, open reduction, and internal fixation of the left femur are also performed. Thirty-six hours after the operation, she is not sleeping but is not in full condition. She is receiving intravenous morphine via a patient-controlled pump. She states that she needs morphine to relieve pain but is worried about becoming dependent. She has no history of psychoactive disorders. She drinks one to two glasses of wine per week. Which of the following initial actions by the physician is most appropriate?
A. Assure the patient that her chances of becoming dependent on drugs are negligible
B. Continue morphine but intermittently administer naloxone intravenously
C. Switch the patient to oral acetaminophen as soon as she can take medications orally
D. Switch the patient to intramuscular lorazepam

Question: A 37-year-old woman with HIV presents to the doctor with a 1-month history of progressive diarrhea and a weight loss of 1.8 kg (4 pounds). Over the past week, she has had six large watery stools daily. She is currently on triple antiretroviral therapy. She works as a flight attendant and regularly operates domestic flights within the United States. She also flies to Asia at least once a month. Her height is 163 cm (5 feet 4 inches) and weight is 59 kg (130 pounds); her BMI is 22 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 88/min, blood pressure is 112/64 mmHg. Her abdomen is distended. The rest of the examination shows no abnormalities. Her CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 400/mm3 (normal ≥500). What is the most likely pathogen?
A. Cryptosporidium parvum  
B. Cytomegalovirus  
C. Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex  
D. Salmonella enteritidis

Question: According to the definition in the APA General Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services and the CPA Practical Guidelines for Providers of Psychological Services, "psychological services" include all of the following except?  
A. conducting scientific research  
B. program development  
C. consultation on assessment and intervention  
D. supervision of psychological services

Question: There are also certain ways to increase external validity. Based on your knowledge of these methods, what does CLUSTER SAMPLING refer to?
A. ensures the representativeness of the sample for the population
B. ensures proportional representation
C. the unit of sampling is a natural group
D. subjects and/or the experimenter do not know the purpose or the group to which they belong

Question: A 25-year-old woman consulted a doctor about numbness in her right arm for 2 months. During this period, she most often felt tingling in the ring and little fingers of her right hand. She has no serious illnesses and is not taking any medications. She works as a cashier and uses a computer at home. She played pitcher in a softball league for 5 years until she stopped 2 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows full muscle strength. Palpation of the right elbow reveals sharp pain in the ring and little fingers of the right hand. Sensation of pinprick and light touch is decreased on the medial half of the ring finger of the right hand and on the entire little finger. The most likely cause of these findings is the entrapment of which of the following on the right?
A. Median nerve at the wrist  
B. Musculocutaneous nerve at the forearm  
C. Radial nerve at the forearm  
D. Ulnar nerve at the elbow joint

Question: An 18-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department 10 minutes after sustaining a stab wound to the chest. Upon arrival, he does not respond to painful stimuli. Pulse is 130/min, breathing is 8/min, shallow, systolic blood pressure is 60 mmHg. The patient is intubated and mechanical ventilation is initiated, and a 0.9% saline infusion is started. After 5 minutes, the pulse is 130/min, and blood pressure is 70/40 mmHg. Upon examination, a 2 cm wound is found in the left sixth intercostal space at the midclavicular line. Jugular venous distension is noted. Breath sounds are normal. The trachea is midline. Heart tones are not auscultated. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of the patient?
A. Chest X-ray  
B. Echocardiography

D. Testimony is inadmissible to confirm contemporaneous oral agreements that modify or contradict the terms of the written contract.
